clusters.rule: Do not perform per-row database work inside a loop over DAGs, task instances, or event rows: hoist the query out of the loop, batch it, or pass the already-fetched data in, and eager-load any relationship the loop dereferences (joinedload/selectinload) rather than letting it lazy-load per row.
clusters.trigger: A session.scalar()/scalars()/execute() call, or a dotted lazy relationship access (event.dataset.uri, record.dag.<attr>, ti.<rel>), appears inside a for-loop over dags_needing_dagruns, dataset_triggered_dag_info, mapped task instances or other scheduler-loop rows, on a query carrying no joinedload/selectinload option.
clusters.rationale: The scheduler loop runs continuously against the metadata DB, so a query or lazy attribute touched once per row turns a single statement into N; reviewers insist the data be fetched once, eagerly, before the loop starts.

clusters.rule: Express "no referencing row" in ORM queries as a correlated ~exists(select(Child.fk).where(Child.fk == Parent.id)) anti-join rather than <col>.not_in(select(...)), and do not carry a redundant is_not(None) inside the EXISTS.
clusters.trigger: The diff contains .not_in(select(...)) or NOT IN (SELECT ...) in a SQLAlchemy query, typically a scheduler/triggerer cleanup filter over a nullable FK column.
clusters.rationale: NOT IN over a nullable column has surprising three-valued-logic semantics and plans badly on the large cleanup tables; the correlated EXISTS form is what the repo's other cleanup queries already use.

clusters.rule: Write SQLAlchemy queries in the 2.0 style - session.scalar()/session.scalars() over select(Model).where(...) - not the legacy session.query(Model).filter(...) API or Select.filter().
clusters.trigger: diff adds session.query(...).filter(...) in source or test code, or calls .filter() on a Select object.
clusters.rationale: Airflow has migrated to the SQLAlchemy 2.0 select API; leaving legacy Query/filter forms in new code re-introduces the style the migration removed and blocks the eventual removal of the legacy layer.

clusters.rule: A FastAPI route decorator must declare every status code its handler can produce: each status raised via HTTPException belongs in the responses= mapping, and the decorator's status_code must agree with the success codes the handler actually returns.
clusters.trigger: raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_4xx_...) in a handler body whose decorator does not list that status in responses=, or a route declaring status_code=HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT whose handler also returns a different 2xx code.
clusters.rationale: The decorator is what generates the OpenAPI spec and the generated UI client, so an undeclared status code is invisible to every consumer of the API.

clusters.rule: Every DB-backed list endpoint in the FastAPI APIs must paginate its query - use the paginated_select convention in the core API, or an explicit limit/offset (or documented hard cap) in the execution API - never return the whole collection.
clusters.trigger: A GET list route in api_fastapi/core_api/routes/ or the execution API calls session.scalars(select(...)).all() with no paginated_select, limit or offset.
clusters.rationale: Collection endpoints run against unbounded metadata tables, so an unpaginated route is a latency and memory hazard the first time a deployment grows; pagination is the established shape for every other list route.

clusters.rule: Express sizing and spacing in Airflow UI components with Chakra UI token values (e.g. height={5}, p={2}), not raw CSS pixel strings passed through props or inline style/sx objects.
clusters.trigger: A Chakra UI component receives a size, padding, margin or font-size value as a quoted pixel string (height="20px", style={{ padding: '8px' }}) rather than a numeric token.
clusters.rationale: Chakra tokens are what keep the UI's spacing scale and theming coherent; hardcoded pixels opt individual components out of the design system.

clusters.rule: Keep FastAPI route modules to route handlers only: Pydantic request/response models belong in the package's datamodels module, authorization and business helpers in its services module, query/filter construction in the corresponding Query* filter class's to_orm, and callback or domain-object definitions in the module that owns the domain model.
clusters.trigger: A Pydantic BaseModel, an authorization dependency, a callback-definition object (e.g. _ImportPathCallbackDef), or resolution/query-building logic (e.g. resolve_task_group_pattern_to_task_ids) is defined or constructed inline inside a routes/*.py handler in the core API or a provider package.
clusters.rationale: The Core API's datamodels/services/filter-parameter layering is what makes routes reviewable and reusable, and provider APIs are expected to mirror it; logic inlined into a handler is unreachable for other callers and untestable on its own.

clusters.rule: Implement behaviour common to all implementations of a pluggable hierarchy in its base class or a shared mixin (BaseExecutor, BaseCoordinator) rather than duplicating it in each concrete subclass.
clusters.trigger: A new workload-handling method, or language-agnostic plumbing such as socket server startup / accept helpers, is added to multiple concrete executors or per-language coordinators with no base-class implementation.
clusters.rationale: Executors and coordinators are extension points implemented in-tree and out-of-tree; anything the base class does not provide has to be re-implemented by every existing and future subclass, and third-party ones simply never get it.

clusters.rule: Do not add public API to a widely shared base class when its only consumer lives in another package or layer; keep the member with the layer that uses it, and require at least one in-scope consumer before it joins the shared surface.
clusters.trigger: A property, class attribute or method is added to a core or shared base class (CronMixin and other timetable bases, DbApiHook and other shared hooks) whose only reference site is a downstream package such as the task SDK or providers/common/ai.
clusters.rationale: Every member on a shared base class becomes public API that all subclasses and downstream implementers inherit and maintain; reviewers want the concern kept in the layer that actually needs it rather than pushed into the shared contract.

clusters.rule: Fetch exactly the columns the consuming code reads: enumerate columns instead of select(SomeModel) in grid/UI and other hot-path queries, restrict with_row_locks selects to the key actually used, and do not add a column to load_only() that no caller consumes.
clusters.trigger: A grid/UI or hot-path query uses select(SomeModel) instead of listing columns, a with_row_locks(select(Model)) retrieves the full entity when only .id is consumed, or a column is added to a load_only(...) call that no downstream code path reads.
clusters.rationale: These queries run per page load or per scheduler pass over wide tables, so every extra column is bytes off the wire and rows the ORM has to hydrate for nothing; the column list is expected to match what the code actually reads.

clusters.rule: In `execute_complete`, branch explicitly on `event["status"]` and handle every status the paired trigger can emit — success, error, timeout and cancelled — before reading any payload field; never collapse all non-success statuses into one failure branch.
clusters.trigger: `execute_complete` reads payload fields without a prior status check, or returns on `status == "success"` and falls through to a single failure/cancel handler while the paired Trigger can emit timeout or cancelled statuses.
clusters.rationale: A trigger and the operator method that resumes from it are one contract written in the same PR. If the operator does not decode each status the trigger can emit, a cancellation or a timeout is reported to the user as the wrong error, or a payload field is read off an event that never carried one.

clusters.rule: When a broad `except Exception` wraps code that deliberately raises `AirflowException`, add an `except AirflowException: raise` clause before the generic handler so the specific exception is neither re-wrapped nor swallowed.
clusters.trigger: A `raise AirflowException(...)` inside a `try` whose only handler is `except Exception as e`, with no preceding `except AirflowException: raise`.
clusters.rationale: The deliberate raise carries task-failure semantics that callers and the task runner branch on; letting the catch-all re-wrap it turns a precise, intended failure into an opaque generic one.

clusters.rule: Operator, sensor and trigger error paths — including the failure and timeout branches of `execute_complete` — must raise Airflow exception types (`AirflowException`, `AirflowFailException`, `AirflowTaskTimeout`), never `RuntimeError` or another builtin.
clusters.trigger: diff adds `raise RuntimeError(...)` (or another builtin) on a trigger-event failure/timeout branch, or replaces an existing `raise AirflowException(` with `raise RuntimeError(` in an operator, sensor or trigger.
clusters.rationale: Airflow's exception hierarchy is what the task runner and every caller catch on; swapping in a builtin silently changes retry and failure handling for code that was catching the Airflow type.

clusters.rule: Post-submit commands and other cleanup that must run once a job finishes belong in a `try/finally` that covers the whole method including its early-exit guards, so they execute on success, failure and kill alike.
clusters.trigger: A `_run_post_submit_commands()` / sidecar-cleanup call sits outside a `finally`, or a `raise` appears before the `try/finally` that wraps it, in `SparkSubmitHook.submit()` or a K8s/YARN poll method.
clusters.rationale: These hooks exist to tear down sidecars and driver-side state; if the job raises or is killed the cleanup is exactly what still has to happen, so placing it on the success path only leaks the resources it was written to reclaim.

clusters.rule: Display counts for a paginated API result from the response's `total_entries`, never from the length of the returned array.
clusters.trigger: A badge, counter or summary renders `someList.length` / `data.items.length` where the list came from a paginated Airflow endpoint or a query that passes an explicit `limit`.
clusters.rationale: The array is one page bounded by `limit`, so its length silently under-reports the true count as soon as the result exceeds the page size; the endpoint already returns the real total.

clusters.rule: To clear an existing server-side field through an Airflow PATCH/PUT endpoint, send `null` rather than `undefined`, so the key is present in the JSON body and lands in `model_fields_set` on the backend.
clusters.trigger: A mutation maps an empty form field to `undefined` in a PATCH/PUT request body or update mask.
clusters.rationale: `undefined` is dropped during JSON serialisation, so the field never reaches `model_fields_set` and the backend treats the clear as "not supplied" and leaves the old value in place.

clusters.rule: Test for presence with an explicit `is not None` (Python) or `!== undefined && !== null` (TypeScript) rather than truthiness wherever `0`, `False` or an empty string is a legitimate value.
clusters.trigger: `if value:` / `if not value:` in Python or `if (value)` / `Boolean(value)` in TypeScript used as a presence check on a field — `bundle_version`, `dag.fileloc`, an active `map_index = 0` filter, an XCom value — whose valid domain includes falsy values.
clusters.rationale: Airflow's domain is full of legitimately falsy values — map index 0, an empty bundle version, a `False` XCom — so a truthiness check quietly drops real data instead of testing whether the value was supplied.

clusters.rule: Put imports at module scope; an import inside a function, method, fixture or test body is acceptable only to break a genuine circular import or for deliberate lazy loading (worker isolation, `TYPE_CHECKING`), and must carry a comment naming the reason — stdlib modules always go at the top of the file.
clusters.trigger: An `import` / `from ... import` statement inside a function, method, test helper or fixture body — `importlib`, `logging` and other stdlib modules included — with no adjacent comment explaining the cycle or lazy-loading reason it avoids.
clusters.rationale: A body-level import hides the module's real dependency graph and repeats the import machinery on every call; the exceptions are narrow and known, so the ones that are legitimate say why, and everything else moves to the top.

clusters.rule: Generate the execution JWT inside the same try block as, and before, the commit that transitions the task instance to running, so a token-generation failure cannot leave a TI committed as running without a token.
clusters.trigger: `services.aget(JWTGenerator)` / `generator.generate()` or the `X-Execution-Token` / Refreshed-API-Token assignment is placed after the `session.commit()` / `session.flush()` that moves the TI to running.
clusters.rationale: Once the state transition is committed the worker is considered started; a token failure after that point strands a task instance in running that no worker can ever authenticate for.

clusters.rule: Count DEFERRED task instances toward `max_active_tis_per_dag` and `max_active_tis_per_dagrun`; any divergence between those maps and the DAG-run active-tasks map behind `max_active_tasks` must be deliberate and justified in a comment.
clusters.trigger: A scheduler concurrency query or map (`task_concurrency_map`, `task_dagrun_concurrency_map`, `dag_run_active_tasks_map`) filters on `[running, queued]` and omits `TaskInstanceState.DEFERRED`, or adds/removes DEFERRED from one map without the same treatment in the others.
clusters.rationale: A deferred task still holds its slot against the per-task limits users set, so leaving it out lets the scheduler over-schedule past the configured concurrency; the three maps back different limits, so their differences have to be explained rather than accidental.

clusters.rule: When `create_dagrun()` is given a `bundle_version`, resolve it to a `DagVersion` first and drive everything that depends on the DAG definition — partition-key validation, deadline configuration — off that resolved version rather than `self` or the head DAG.
clusters.trigger: `create_dagrun()` calls `self.validate_partition_key(...)`, reads `self.deadline`, or otherwise uses the head DAG object while a `bundle_version` or resolved DAG argument is also present.
clusters.rationale: The point of pinning a run to a bundle version is that the run behaves like that version of the DAG; validating or configuring it against the latest parsed DAG defeats the pin and produces runs the pinned code would have rejected.

clusters.rule: Use the enum member (`DagRunState`, `TaskInstanceState`, a provider status enum such as `DmsTaskWaiterStatus`) wherever a state is compared or passed; never a raw string literal that duplicates its value.
clusters.trigger: A raw lowercase state string is passed as `state=` to `create_dagrun`, `DagRun(...)` or `TaskInstance(...)`, or a comparison like `if status != "<state_string>"` is added where the provider already defines a matching Enum.
clusters.rationale: The enums are the single definition of the legal state set; a duplicated string literal is invisible to renames and typos and drifts out of sync with the enum it copies.

clusters.rule: Diagnostics for conditions that are expected on paths the scheduler loop or the execution API re-runs every iteration or heartbeat must be logged at DEBUG; do not add INFO or WARNING logging to a hot fall-through branch.
clusters.trigger: A `log.info(...)` is added on a fallback or miss path inside a heartbeat or other high-frequency execution-API handler, or a `self.log.warning(...)` is added to a scheduler-loop helper on a branch whose rows re-enter it on the next loop.
clusters.rationale: These branches run at loop frequency and their condition is normal, so a high log level floods operator logs with an entry per iteration and trains people to ignore genuine warnings.

clusters.rule: Do not silence a failure with a blanket `except Exception: pass`-style handler: let the error propagate or chain it, or suppress only the specific expected exception types and log the suppression at debug.
clusters.trigger: A broad silent handler wraps credential resolution / token refresh in a secrets backend, or conn-id filesystem injection for `ObjectStoragePath` in `sdk/io/path.py`.
clusters.rationale: The swallowed error is the only evidence of what actually went wrong; hiding it converts a diagnosable credential or provider failure into a generic downstream error nobody can trace back.

clusters.rule: airflow-core, including `airflow-core/tests/`, must not import task-SDK internals — `airflow.sdk._shared`, SDK-only exceptions from `airflow.sdk.exceptions`, or other private SDK paths; tests for SDK-only symbols live in the SDK test tree.
clusters.trigger: An import in airflow-core source or tests is pointed at `airflow.sdk._shared.X`, `airflow.sdk.exceptions`, or another `airflow.sdk` internal namespace.
clusters.rationale: The core/task-SDK split is a distribution boundary, not just a package layout; reaching into SDK internals from core re-couples the two and makes the SDK's private modules impossible to change independently.

clusters.rule: Treat the numeric `status` field on the error object as the UI's API-error contract: read it as `(error as ExpandedApiError).status` / `error?.status` rather than `instanceof ApiError`, and attach `status` to any `Error` thrown from a raw `fetch()` inside a query function.
clusters.trigger: diff adds `instanceof ApiError` in a UI query or hook, or a `useQuery` `queryFn` calls `fetch()` directly and throws a plain `Error` without a `.status` property on a non-OK response.
clusters.rationale: The global QueryClient retry guard and the UI's error handling both key off `error.status`; an `instanceof` check breaks across bundling boundaries and a status-less thrown Error makes 4xx responses retry as if they were transient.

clusters.rule: Instance attributes belong to `__init__`: initialise every resource handle and state flag there, and never first-assign or overwrite them in `execute()`, `run()`, `submit()` or `get_conn()` — those methods resolve values into local variables and reset released resources to `None` after cleanup.
clusters.trigger: diff assigns `self.<resource>` or a state flag for the first time inside `async def run()` / `submit()` / `execute()`, or `get_conn()` assigns to `self.<param>` from `connection.extra_dejson` or a `getattr(..., default)` fallback chain.
clusters.rationale: Triggers, hooks and operators are serialised, resumed and re-entered, so an attribute that only exists after a particular method has run raises `AttributeError` on the other paths and makes the object's state depend on call order.

clusters.rule: Do not guard a Task SDK API client or supervisor-comms response with an `isinstance(resp, XResponse)` check whose else branch silently returns `[]`/`None`: these calls return their response model or raise `ServerResponseError`, so use the result directly and raise on an unexpected type.
clusters.trigger: An `isinstance(<resp>, <X>Response)` check with an `else` fallback around a `self.client.<resource>.<method>(...)` call in `supervisor.py`, or around a `SUPERVISOR_COMMS.send(...)` result in task-sdk `execution_time` context functions.
clusters.rationale: The client contract already guarantees the response model or an exception, so the isinstance branch is dead code whose else arm turns a protocol violation into an empty result the caller then treats as legitimately empty data.

clusters.rule: In provider code, raise the most appropriate built-in Python exception (ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError) for argument validation, internal invariant violations and third-party service failures, rather than AirflowException.
clusters.trigger: A new `raise AirflowException(...)` inside a provider hook, operator or trigger for parameter validation, an internal/programming error, or an error originating in an external service.
clusters.rationale: AirflowException is Airflow's own signalling channel. Using it for ordinary programming errors or third-party failures makes provider errors indistinguishable from Airflow control flow and hides the real cause from users; the built-in exception types already say what went wrong.

clusters.rule: A provider must not unconditionally import, call or attribute-access an airflow-core symbol that does not exist in its minimum supported core version: gate it behind an AIRFLOW_V_X_Y_PLUS check (or `getattr(obj, "attr", default)`) and keep the older fallback path.
clusters.trigger: Provider code imports, calls or reads an airflow-core symbol, method or attribute introduced after that provider's minimum supported Airflow version with no version guard or fallback, or a diff deletes the Airflow 2 branch from a provider that still supports Airflow 2.
clusters.rationale: Providers are released independently of core and are installed against a range of Airflow versions, so any core API newer than the declared floor has to be optional at runtime — otherwise the provider fails at import for every user on an older core.

clusters.rule: Express cross-version Airflow compatibility through the shared compat layer — the `AIRFLOW_V_X_Y_PLUS` sentinels in `version_compat` and the helpers in `providers/common/compat` — instead of inline `packaging.version.parse` comparisons or per-provider copies of the same check.
clusters.trigger: Provider code compares `packaging.version.parse(airflow_version)` against a literal version string, or repeats an inline `if AIRFLOW_V_3_X_PLUS` shim that already exists in (or belongs in) `providers/common/compat`.
clusters.rationale: Version gates are scattered across dozens of providers; when they live in one compat module they can be audited and retired in a single change, whereas hand-rolled comparisons drift and are missed when a minimum version is finally raised.

clusters.rule: Every version-compatibility shim in a provider must carry a comment naming the exact release involved — the minimum `>=X.Y.Z` that exports the symbol, or a `# TODO: Remove once minimum supported Airflow version is X.Y`.
clusters.trigger: A `try: from airflow.sdk... except ImportError:` fallback, or another version-compat workaround block, is added to a provider with no comment naming the version that introduces or retires it.
clusters.rationale: Shims are the hardest thing to clean up later: without the version written down, nobody can tell when raising the minimum supported version makes the block dead code, so it survives long past its purpose.

clusters.rule: A dependency pin or upper bound added to a provider's `pyproject.toml` as a workaround must carry a comment naming the upstream issue and the condition under which the cap can be lifted.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a `<X.Y` upper bound or a pinned/transitive dependency to a provider's `pyproject.toml` with no accompanying note or linked issue explaining when it may be relaxed.
clusters.rationale: Caps added for a transient upstream breakage become permanent because no later reader can tell whether the reason still holds; recording the trigger for removal is what makes the pin reviewable a release later.

clusters.rule: Every package a provider imports directly must be declared as a dependency in that provider's `pyproject.toml` in the same PR; do not rely on it arriving transitively.
clusters.trigger: diff adds `import <package>` under `providers/<name>/src/` where `<package>` is absent from `dependencies` (or the relevant extra) in `providers/<name>/pyproject.toml`.
clusters.rationale: Providers are installed standalone, so a package that happens to be present in the CI image via another provider's dependency tree simply is not there for the user; the import breaks at runtime for exactly the people who install only this provider.

clusters.rule: Import anything a provider does not require unconditionally — a package behind an optional extra, or another provider's package — inside `try`/`except ImportError`, and either raise `AirflowOptionalProviderFeatureException` naming the extra to install or degrade the feature; never import it unconditionally at module top level.
clusters.trigger: A provider module imports a package declared only as an optional extra, or a symbol from another `airflow.providers.*` package, at module top level with no `try`/`except ImportError` guard.
clusters.rationale: A top-level import of something optional turns a missing extra into an import failure for the whole provider; guarding it keeps the rest of the provider usable and turns the error into an actionable message naming what to install.

clusters.rule: Reuse Airflow's established name for a concept instead of inventing a synonym: `run_after` for the DAG run scheduling timestamp, `wait_for_completion` for the wait-for-finish flag, and an `a`-prefixed method name (`aget_connection`) for the async variant of an existing method.
clusters.trigger: A new or renamed parameter/method uses `logical_date` or `date` for scheduling time, `wait_for_termination` for a completion flag, or an `async_`-prefixed name where a sync counterpart already exists.
clusters.rationale: Users move between providers constantly; a synonym for a parameter that is already named consistently across the AWS and core operators forces them to re-learn the same flag per package and shows up in every DAG they write.

clusters.rule: In executor methods that also reference `airflow.executors.workloads`, name the sequence parameter `workload_items`; do not keep the colliding name `workloads` or alias the module import to work around the collision.
clusters.trigger: An executor method (`_process_workloads` or an override) declares a parameter named `workloads` in a module that does `from airflow.executors import workloads`, or imports that module under an alias to dodge the shadowing.
clusters.rationale: The parameter shadows the module the same function needs, and aliasing the import hides the collision instead of removing it; renaming the local is the fix that keeps every executor override reading the same way.

clusters.rule: FastAPI apps and routers exposed by a provider plugin must declare their own auth dependencies at route or router level — `Depends(requires_access_*)` for authentication, plus `GetUserDep` alongside `SessionDep` on state-mutating handlers — rather than relying on the parent app's middleware.
clusters.trigger: A route or router defined under `providers/**/plugins/*.py` or a provider's `worker_api/routes/` declares no `requires_access_*` dependency, or a POST/PATCH/DELETE handler takes `SessionDep` without `GetUserDep`.
clusters.rationale: A provider's sub-app is mounted into the API server, and the mount point's middleware is not a guarantee the plugin controls; declaring the dependency on the route is what makes the auth requirement visible and survives remounting.

clusters.rule: Serializers and deserializers for user-extensible types must go through the registration registry: `encode_*` must validate the class with a `find_registered_custom_*` lookup before trusting `qualname(var)`, and `decode_*` must guard `import_string` with an `is_core_*_import_path` check plus a registered-custom fallback.
clusters.trigger: A new `encode_*` function serializes a custom subclass using only `qualname(var)` with no registry guard, or a new `decode_*` function calls `import_string(var[Encoding.TYPE])` without a preceding core-import-path check and registry-based fallback.
clusters.rationale: Serialized DAG data is attacker-reachable input to the scheduler; an unvalidated type path on either side of the round trip turns deserialization into arbitrary import, so both halves have to be anchored to the registry.

clusters.rule: Never log or print a Connection, a ConnectionResult, `Connection.get_uri()` output, or any credential-bearing string — including temporary debug output; redact it, or apply the security code-scanning suppression, before logging.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a `print(...)` or `log.*` call whose argument derives from a Connection object, a connection URI, a password or a secret — notably under `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/execution_time/`.
clusters.rationale: Task and scheduler logs are retained and widely readable, so a single interpolated connection URI leaks the credential to everyone with log access at every level, debug included.

clusters.rule: Operators, triggers, notifiers and listeners must reach a third-party service through the provider's Hook class (sync or async) rather than constructing the underlying client or session inline.
clusters.trigger: diff constructs a provider's underlying client or HTTP session directly — `confluent_kafka.Producer(...)`, `aiohttp.ClientSession()` — inside an operator, trigger, notifier or listener where the provider already exposes a Hook wrapping it.
clusters.rationale: The Hook is where connection resolution, extras handling, auth and retry live; building the client inline bypasses all of it, so the operator quietly stops honouring the Airflow connection users configured.

clusters.rule: Take a service's scheme, host and port from the Airflow connection (and its extras) named by the operator's `*_conn_id`; do not hardcode them or re-parse them out of another string such as a queue URI.
clusters.trigger: A provider hook, operator or trigger builds a request URL from a hardcoded scheme or port (e.g. `requests.get(f"http://{host}:8080/...")`), or parses `host:port` out of a URI string instead of reading the connection identified by its conn_id.
clusters.rationale: The connection is the one place a deployment configures where a service lives and how it is reached; hardcoding a scheme or port makes the operator unusable on TLS or non-default deployments, and re-parsing a URI silently diverges from the connection the user actually set.

clusters.rule: When a provider change raises the minimum Airflow core or Task SDK version it actually requires — swapping a core import for the `common.compat.sdk` equivalent, or dropping SDK-specific parameters from a system test — update that provider's declared minimum version in the same PR.
clusters.trigger: A diff replaces a core import with its `airflow.providers.common.compat.sdk` equivalent, or removes SDK-specific env vars or parameters, with no matching change to the provider's declared minimum core/SDK version.
clusters.rationale: The declared minimum is what the release manager and the resolver act on; when the code starts requiring a newer core or SDK and the metadata does not say so, the provider installs cleanly and then fails at runtime for users on the older version.

clusters.rule: In user-facing prose - documentation, newsfragments, release notes, changelog entries, config.yml descriptions and UI strings - spell Airflow's core nouns the Airflow 3 way (Dag, Dags, Dag run, Dag files, Dag bundles, Dag Processor, API Server); never all-caps DAG/DAGs, "DAG processor" or "webserver", and reserve all-caps DAG for code identifiers and quoted strings.
clusters.trigger: A docs page, newsfragment, RELEASE_NOTES.rst bullet, changelog entry, config.yml description or translated UI string adds prose containing "DAG"/"DAGs" outside backticks or a code identifier, or uses "webserver"/"DAG processor".
clusters.rationale: Airflow 3 deliberately re-spelled these concepts; the all-caps forms leak pre-3.0 vocabulary into text users read, while the code identifiers keep their old casing, so reviewers correct the prose on sight.

clusters.rule: Keep a PR's diff scoped to what its title and description claim: regenerate uv.lock against fresh main so it carries only the dependency changes this PR actually makes, and split an independent schema-fix migration or a second unrelated feature into its own PR or call it out in the description with its own rationale.
clusters.trigger: The diff contains uv.lock changes no source change in the PR accounts for (extras added or dependencies dropped by a rebase), an independent schema-fix migration alongside a feature migration, or a second unrelated feature.
clusters.rationale: Reviewers read the description as the contract for the diff; unexplained lockfile churn and piggy-backed migrations or features cannot be reviewed or reverted independently of the feature the PR is named for.

clusters.rule: Pick the newsfragment from the change's actual user-visible impact: none at all for a documentation-only or purely internal change, and bugfix.rst rather than significant.rst for an internal fix that changes no observable behaviour.
clusters.trigger: A PR whose diff touches only docs also adds a file under newsfragments/, or a significant.rst fragment is added for an internal race-condition fix or scheduler-internal improvement with no API or behaviour change.
clusters.rationale: Newsfragments become the release notes users read; a fragment for a change nobody outside the repo can observe, or a significant fragment for an internal fix, inflates the upgrade reading users must do.

clusters.rule: Keep a locale's do-not-translate / keep-in-English list to the bare CamelCase code identifiers quoted verbatim as code (Asset, TaskInstance, DagRun); compound phrases and the same concepts appearing as UI labels must follow the wording that locale's i18n JSON files already use.
clusters.trigger: A locale file under .github/skills/airflow-translations/locales/ lists a multi-word phrase built around an Airflow term, or blanket-lists CamelCase identifiers, without distinguishing code identifiers from UI labels the locale's JSON already translates.
clusters.rationale: The guideline file has to agree with the translations already shipped in that locale's JSON; a list that blocks whole phrases or UI labels contradicts existing strings and freezes wording the translators deliberately localised.

clusters.rule: A bug fix to an example DAG that is motivated by a specific configuration (e.g. a non-UTC [core] default_timezone) must extend tests/unit/always/test_example_dags.py so that DAG is imported under the triggering config.
clusters.trigger: An example_dags/ file is modified to fix a datetime/timezone or other config-dependent issue with no added or modified case in test_example_dags.py exercising that configuration.
clusters.rationale: Example DAGs are only parsed under the default config in CI, so the exact scenario that produced the bug stays untested unless the example-DAG test is extended to cover it.

clusters.rule: Mocks standing in for a real Airflow, provider or SDK type must be specced - MagicMock(spec=...), spec_set= or create_autospec, including nested attributes - so signature drift against the real class fails the test; MagicMock(autospec=True) is a no-op keyword and specs nothing.
clusters.trigger: A bare Mock()/MagicMock() (or MagicMock(autospec=True)) substituted for a known type - the Task SDK execution API Client, RunContext, ToolsetTool, a credentials object, a SerializedDAG cache entry, an AWS hook or its async connection, a SQLAlchemy session, an ORM instance, a DAG or an operator method - and then given attributes.
clusters.rationale: An unspecced mock accepts any attribute or signature, so the test keeps passing after the real class changes; specced mocks are what makes these tests catch drift instead of hiding it.

clusters.rule: Do not use pytest's caplog fixture to assert on log output; assert on observable behaviour or return values, or capture the logger directly with a mock.
clusters.trigger: caplog appears as a fixture argument, or caplog.text/caplog.records is asserted on, in a test under providers/**/tests/, kubernetes-tests/ or the core test suites.
clusters.rationale: Log text is not the contract under test; caplog assertions break on unrelated logging changes and depend on handler and propagation setup that differs between the unit, provider and integration suites.

clusters.rule: Pin the query count with assert_queries_count when adding or changing a database access path whose cost matters: a new test for a FastAPI route returning a collection, and any performance-motivated ORM change such as replacing session.merge() with session.add().
clusters.trigger: A new test exercises a FastAPI route returning a collection (assets, DAGs, task instances) with no assert_queries_count context manager, or a diff swaps session.merge( for session.add( on a task_instance/dag_run path with no accompanying assert_queries_count.
clusters.rationale: Query-count regressions - a lost eager load, a re-introduced merge - are invisible in a passing functional test; assert_queries_count is the only thing that makes the performance intent of the change fail CI when it is undone.

clusters.rule: In Playwright e2e tests, wait on an explicit UI condition - a key element becoming visible before a navigation helper returns, expect.poll() for post-click assertions - never read state immediately after an action and never page.waitForLoadState('networkidle').
clusters.trigger: A goto/navigateTo* helper is added with no subsequent waitFor/toBeVisible, page content is compared immediately after a navigation click without expect.poll, or waitForLoadState('networkidle') is called.
clusters.rationale: The UI keeps fetching after navigation, so an immediate read or a networkidle wait is a race that flakes in CI; waiting on the element the test actually depends on is both deterministic and self-documenting.

clusters.rule: E2e tests and page objects must fail when the feature is broken: no if-guards around the assertions and no try/catch or .catch(() => false) around visibility/state checks - use web-first assertions such as expect(el).toBeVisible()/toBeHidden() and let failures propagate.
clusters.trigger: A tests/e2e/specs/*.ts diff adds an if (count > 0) { ... } guard or similar short-circuit around the assertions, or a Playwright page-object method wraps isVisible()/isEnabled() in try/catch returning false.
clusters.rationale: A conditional or swallowed check turns the spec into a test that passes whether or not the feature works, which is worse than no coverage because it looks like coverage.

clusters.rule: When a Helm value moves to a new path, or the executor or CRD that exercised it is removed, migrate the existing chart tests to the still-supported path instead of deleting them, so deprecated-but-supported overrides keep coverage.
clusters.trigger: A helm test or parametrize case using the old broad value path is deleted when a component-scoped or per-executor path is introduced, while the old path is still listed in the NOTES.txt deprecation notice.
clusters.rationale: The old value paths remain supported for chart users mid-upgrade; deleting the test that covered them removes the only proof the deprecated path still renders correctly.

clusters.rule: Every chart/values.yaml parameter must be declared in chart/values.schema.json, and where a value's behaviour depends on another value that dependency must be documented in both files.
clusters.trigger: A key is added to chart/values.yaml with no corresponding entry in chart/values.schema.json, or a conditional expression in the config: block references two or more .Values fields while only one carries an explanatory comment.
clusters.rationale: The schema is what validates users' values files and what the chart docs are generated from, so a key or a gating dependency that lives in only one of the two files is invisible to half the people who need it.

clusters.rule: Provider changelog.rst entries must read as sentence-case, user-facing prose: strip conventional-commit prefixes such as fix: or feat(...), do not open with a lowercase word, name no internal tooling such as Dependabot, and state the concrete change.
clusters.trigger: A line added to providers/*/docs/changelog.rst starts with a lowercase word or a fix:/feat: prefix, or mentions dependabot instead of describing the user-visible change.
clusters.rationale: The changelog is published documentation, not a commit log; raw commit titles and tooling names read as repo internals to the provider's users.

clusters.rule: A changelog or release-note entry is a single concise line stating the user-visible change; PR narration, methodology notes, test-coverage clauses and the detailed explanation belong in the PR.
clusters.trigger: A multi-sentence bugfix entry is added to chart/RELEASE_NOTES.rst, or a provider changelog line carries parenthetical test-coverage, refactor-rationale or methodology text.
clusters.rationale: Release notes are scanned, not read; the reasoning behind a fix is already preserved in the PR the entry links to.

clusters.rule: Add a bullet to a provider's changelog.rst only when that provider's own source files change; a PR limited to test files, to another provider's tests, or to non-functional pyproject.toml marker comments gets no entry.
clusters.trigger: A new bullet or version section in providers/<name>/docs/changelog.rst for a diff whose changed files are all under tests/, belong to a different provider, or are only '# use next version' comments.
clusters.rationale: A changelog entry announces a release of that provider to its users; test-only or cross-provider churn changes nothing they can observe and forces an otherwise unnecessary release.

clusters.rule: Example DAGs must be plain, self-contained and copy-pasteable against current main: no try/except ImportError compatibility shims for older Airflow versions or optional dependencies, and no imports of helpers shared across example DAG files.
clusters.trigger: A file under example_dags/ adds a try: from ... except ImportError: fallback import block, or imports a helper defined in another example or support module.
clusters.rationale: Example DAGs are read as the copy-paste starting point and are rendered into the docs; a version shim or a shared helper import gives readers a snippet that does not stand on its own and documents versions main no longer targets.

clusters.rule: Build test fixtures from the real library type the production code inspects - a V1PodStatus for a pod's status, a real sqlite3.OperationalError as an exception's orig - rather than a plain dict or string stand-in.
clusters.trigger: Test code assigns pod.status = {"key": value} instead of a V1PodStatus instance, or mocks sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError with a plain string as orig where the implementation reads e.orig.args[0].
clusters.rationale: The code under test reaches into the object's real shape - attributes, args tuples - so a dict or string stand-in exercises a shape that never occurs in production and passes where the real type would fail.

clusters.rule: Import symbols that have been migrated to the Task SDK from their airflow.sdk.* public path, not from the legacy airflow-core module (e.g. XCOM_RETURN_KEY from the Task SDK BaseXCom rather than airflow.models.xcom; exceptions from airflow.sdk.exceptions rather than airflow.exceptions).
clusters.trigger: A file, docs example or provider imports a symbol from airflow.models.xcom / airflow.exceptions (often with a `# type: ignore[no-redef]`) when the same symbol is already exported by airflow.sdk.*.
clusters.rationale: Task-facing code must not depend on airflow-core internals; the SDK path is the supported surface and the legacy path is being removed.

clusters.rule: Do not grant the token:workload scope on state-changing execution-API routes; restrict token:workload to read-only endpoints (GET variable/keys, GET/HEAD xcom, GET connection, GET dag_run) and keep PUT/POST/DELETE routes token:execution only.
clusters.trigger: A router.put/post/delete endpoint in the execution API declares Security(require_auth, scopes=[..., "token:workload"]), or a has_variable_access / has_xcom_access dependency on a write route is replaced by a workload-inclusive scope list.
clusters.rationale: The workload token is long-lived and low-privilege; widening it to mutations lets a worker hold write authority for far longer than the execution token it should be using.

clusters.rule: In SQLAlchemy 2.0 declarative models the Mapped[...] annotation is authoritative for nullability: it must agree with the column's nullable setting, and a redundant nullable=True kwarg must not be passed alongside Mapped[X | None].
clusters.trigger: A mapped_column(...) carries nullable=True while its annotation is Mapped[X | None], or a Mapped[X | None] annotation sits on a column declared nullable=False (or vice versa).
clusters.rationale: The annotation is what type checkers and readers trust; a mismatch between it and the column definition is a silent lie about the schema.

clusters.rule: Read tri-state boolean config options (declared type: boolean with default: ~) through conf.getboolean without a fallback that contradicts the declared default, and never use conf.has_option to test whether such an option is enabled.
clusters.trigger: conf.getboolean(section, key, fallback=False) is used for a key whose config.yml default is True, or conf.has_option(section, key) is used as the condition for a boolean feature flag.
clusters.rationale: has_option is true whenever the key exists, including when its value is False, and an explicit fallback silently overrides the value declared in config.yml - both produce a flag that ignores what the operator configured.

clusters.rule: Help text for CLI date arguments that filter runs by partition or logical date must state the exact semantics: whether the end bound is inclusive or exclusive (and what value covers a whole calendar period), and that the calendar day is derived from the UTC instant rather than the user's local or the timetable's timezone.
clusters.trigger: A CLI argument in cli_config.py / dag_command.py adds --start-date / --end-date (or another type=parsedate date filter) whose help text does not spell out inclusivity and the UTC-day interpretation.
clusters.rationale: Ambiguity between midnight-on-the-last-day and first-of-next-month, or a tz-aware input shifting the interpreted day, causes silent data loss the user only notices later.

clusters.rule: Changes to callback execution must be applied to both the executor path and the triggerer path so the two stay behaviourally identical: a new context key must be added via the shared build_context_from_dag_run helper (and declared in the Context TypedDict and KNOWN_CONTEXT_KEYS), and both paths must fail the same way when required context such as the DagRun cannot be fetched.
clusters.trigger: callback_supervisor.py populates context or handles a fetch failure differently from the corresponding build_context_from_dag_run / context-fetch code in triggerer_job_runner.py (e.g. one returns None while the other raises or exits).
clusters.rationale: Callbacks can run on either path; divergence means a callback silently sees different context or keeps running with None instead of retrying, depending on where it happened to be scheduled.

clusters.rule: New or changed behaviour on a public API endpoint must be covered by tests asserting the new response, including the new validation error path and the changed default.
clusters.trigger: A bulk endpoint gains a validation guard, or a service method changes what an endpoint returns by default, without new or updated tests for those paths.
clusters.rationale: Reviewers asked for the tests because the new branch was otherwise unexercised.

clusters.rule: Bulk endpoints must enforce the same authorization and state guards as their single-item counterparts: shared helpers must take the HTTP method as a parameter instead of hardcoding "PUT", and handle_bulk_delete must apply the single-delete state checks unless the relaxation is documented and intentional.
clusters.trigger: A shared authorization helper (e.g. _categorize_entities) hardcodes method="PUT" but is called from a bulk-delete path, or handle_bulk_delete omits a guard the single-delete route applies (e.g. refusing RUNNING DagRuns).
clusters.rationale: The bulk route is the easy way around the single-item route; if it is laxer, the guards on the single-item endpoint are decorative.

clusters.rule: Every actions/upload-artifact step in a GitHub Actions job must use a unique artifact name, including names built from a shared dynamic suffix.
clusters.trigger: Two or more upload-artifact steps in the same job share a name: value or the same name template (e.g. both container-logs-${{env.JOB_ID}}).
clusters.rationale: Duplicate artifact names make the second upload clobber or fail against the first, so the logs the step exists to preserve are lost exactly when a job failed.

clusters.rule: Task-SDK client changelog entries belong in the Task-SDK changelog, not in the airflow-core RELEASE_NOTES.rst.
clusters.trigger: RELEASE_NOTES.rst gains a line mentioning task-sdk / Task SDK client inside an airflow-core section.
clusters.rationale: The distributions release on separate cycles; an entry in the wrong changelog tells users a change shipped in a version that does not contain it.

clusters.rule: A database migration shipped in a patch release may only repair a bug in an existing migration; it must not change payload semantics such that users who already ran the original upgrade end up in a different state from a fresh install.
clusters.trigger: A patch-release PR modifies a file under migrations/versions/ and changes upgrade()/downgrade() logic beyond a no-op correction.
clusters.rationale: Patch releases are applied by users who have already migrated; divergent end states between upgraded and fresh installs are undetectable and unfixable after the fact.

clusters.rule: A new config option introduced in a patch release must be declared in config.yml and explicitly called out in that minor version's upgrade notes.
clusters.trigger: A patch PR adds a key to config.yml, or documents a new [section] key_name, with no corresponding entry in the upgrade notes.
clusters.rationale: Operators read upgrade notes to decide whether a patch is safe; a silently added option changes behaviour they never opted into.

clusters.rule: A reusable workflow whose workflow_dispatch trigger is gated by a committer allowlist must apply the same allowlist check to its workflow_call trigger.
clusters.trigger: A workflow defines a committer-restricted workflow_dispatch block but exposes workflow_call without an equivalent contains(fromJSON([...]), github.event.sender.login) guard.
clusters.rationale: Otherwise any caller workflow bypasses the gate entirely, which is exactly the escalation the allowlist exists to prevent.

clusters.rule: Provider governance documentation must not state that a sponsoring committer is absolved of technical responsibility for the PRs they merge; committers remain responsible for CI health and security review regardless of steward approval.
clusters.trigger: PROVIDERS.rst or an equivalent governance document says the sponsor is NOT responsible for the codebase or for merged PRs.
clusters.rationale: Merge rights carry ASF accountability; wording that disclaims it invites unreviewed provider code into the release.

clusters.rule: Illustrate provider policy concepts in governance documentation with vendor-neutral examples (e.g. the http provider) rather than a named commercial vendor.
clusters.trigger: PROVIDERS.rst or a provider governance document uses a specific vendor name (Slack, AWS, GCP) as the sole illustrative example of a policy.
clusters.rationale: Naming one vendor in policy text reads as a statement about that vendor's standing in the project.

clusters.rule: Every locale skill file under .github/skills/airflow-translations/locales/ must declare that it extends the global rules in ../SKILL.md and that the locale file takes precedence on conflict.
clusters.trigger: A locale skill file (.github/skills/airflow-translations/locales/<lang>.md) is added or modified without a reference to ../SKILL.md and an explicit precedence statement.
clusters.rationale: Without the precedence statement a translator cannot tell which rule wins when the global and locale guidance disagree.

clusters.rule: Documentation for extensible Airflow interfaces (state backends, secrets backends, other plug points) must describe the contract and behaviour rather than enumerate concrete method signatures.
clusters.trigger: A .rst file adds a list-table or code-block of full method signatures (e.g. async def ...) for a pluggable backend or extension point.
clusters.rationale: Signatures change between releases; documented ones go stale immediately and mislead implementers.

clusters.rule: A CI shell script that starts `airflow standalone` in the background and polls for readiness must check liveness with `kill -0 $AIRFLOW_PID` so it exits as soon as the process dies instead of waiting out the full timeout.
clusters.trigger: A CI script launches airflow standalone in the background, captures its PID, then polls in a timed loop with no kill -0 $AIRFLOW_PID check.
clusters.rationale: Without the liveness check a crashed standalone burns the whole timeout on every CI run and reports a timeout instead of the real failure.

clusters.rule: AIP skill SKILL.md files must anchor AIP URL detection to the Apache Confluence prefix https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/AIRFLOW rather than treating any https:// argument as the AIP URL.
clusters.trigger: A SKILL.md under .github/skills/aip-* describes AIP URL detection as "other https:// arguments are the AIP URL" with no cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/AIRFLOW anchor.
clusters.rationale: An unanchored pattern makes the skill fetch arbitrary URLs the user passed for another purpose.

clusters.rule: Locale skill files must cross-reference the rationale already documented in airflow-core/src/airflow/ui/public/i18n/locales/<lang>/README.md when they consolidate that locale's translation conventions.
clusters.trigger: A locale skill file under .github/skills/airflow-translations/locales/ is created or updated with no reference to the in-tree i18n README for that locale.
clusters.rationale: The README holds the reasoning the locale's translators already agreed on; a skill file that restates conventions without pointing at it will drift from them.

clusters.rule: Docs examples showing regex filtering of asset partition keys must call .partition_key_pattern(), not .partition_key() (which is exact-match).
clusters.trigger: A docs example passes a regex string to .partition_key(.
clusters.rationale: The example as written silently does an exact-match comparison and never fires.

clusters.rule: Documentation for a feature introduced in a specific Airflow version must get its own .. note:: block or subheader rather than being nested under a section that documents a different feature.
clusters.trigger: A diff adds documentation for a new feature (e.g. Resumable Tasks) inside an existing section covering a distinct feature (e.g. Deferred Operators).
clusters.rationale: Readers scanning for the section's subject skip past the buried feature, and version applicability gets attached to the wrong thing.

clusters.rule: Derive component versions such as TASK_SDK_VERSION from PACKAGE_VERSION with packaging.version.parse_version() and its .minor/.micro attributes, never by splitting the version string on ".".
clusters.trigger: PACKAGE_VERSION.split('.') is used to derive a version component.
clusters.rationale: String splitting breaks on pre-release, dev and post suffixes that the project's versions actually carry.

clusters.rule: Auth-manager documentation must reference get_url_refresh() for the token-refresh endpoint rather than hardcoding a literal path such as POST /auth/token/refresh.
clusters.trigger: Documentation hardcodes an auth token refresh URL path instead of pointing at the get_url_refresh method.
clusters.rationale: The path is auth-manager specific; a hardcoded one is wrong for every manager that overrides it.

clusters.rule: Airflow documentation must describe the current behaviour without comparing it to earlier versions; drop phrases like "no longer", "previously", "used to" and "as of version X".
clusters.trigger: Documentation prose adds "no longer", "previously", "used to", or "as of Airflow X.Y".
clusters.rationale: Docs are versioned; historical comparison belongs in release notes and rots in place in the guide.

clusters.rule: Document task-state-store and asset-state-store values as JsonValue (any JSON-serialisable type), not as strings.
clusters.trigger: Docs describe a task store or asset store value type as "string"/"str" rather than JsonValue or JSON.
clusters.rationale: The stores accept arbitrary JSON; documenting them as strings makes users serialise by hand.

clusters.rule: Authentication documentation must not present the FAB Auth Manager as the default; the default auth manager in Airflow 3 is the Simple Auth Manager.
clusters.trigger: Docs or configuration examples imply the FAB Auth Manager is in use by default.
clusters.rationale: FAB moved to a provider in Airflow 3; examples assuming it fail on a stock install.

clusters.rule: Getting-started and quickstart documentation must cover both the uv-based install path and the standard pip + venv path.
clusters.trigger: The install quickstart section is added or rewritten covering only uv or only pip.
clusters.rationale: Newcomers arrive with whichever tool they already have; a single-tool quickstart blocks the other half of them.

clusters.rule: A significant newsfragment describing a permission or endpoint change must name the surface precisely (e.g. "FastAPI UI /dags endpoint") to distinguish it from other endpoints sharing the same path.
clusters.trigger: A significant.rst newsfragment mentions /dags or another ambiguous path without saying whether it is the UI route or the public REST API endpoint.
clusters.rationale: Operators decide whether the change affects them from this line alone, and the two surfaces have different audiences.

clusters.rule: Do not enable asyncio debug logging in production code paths or default configuration.
clusters.trigger: PYTHONASYNCIODEBUG, loop.set_debug(True), or asyncio debug logging is enabled in non-test code.
clusters.rationale: Asyncio debug output includes coroutine arguments, which puts connection credentials into task logs.

clusters.rule: Do not add native/binary C-extension libraries to the mandatory dependencies of airflow-core; they belong in an optional extra or a provider.
clusters.trigger: A library distributed only as a compiled wheel, with no pure-Python fallback, is added to the dependencies list in airflow-core/pyproject.toml.
clusters.rationale: Core must install on every platform and Python build the project supports; a mandatory binary wheel makes core uninstallable wherever it has no wheel.

clusters.rule: is_authorized_* methods on BaseAuthManager and its subclasses must take the generic auth-user type-var (user: T) and express multiple user ids as set[str]; they must not accept concrete Airflow model types such as HITLUser.
clusters.trigger: An is_authorized_* method is added or modified on an auth manager taking a concrete Airflow model type instead of user: T or primitives.
clusters.rationale: BaseAuthManager is implemented outside the repo; binding its signatures to core models forces every third-party auth manager to import them.

clusters.rule: Extend an existing is_authorized_* method with an optional parameter rather than adding a parallel is_authorized_<action>_for_<entity> method to the BaseAuthManager interface.
clusters.trigger: A new method matching is_authorized_.*_for_ is added to BaseAuthManager.
clusters.rationale: Every method on this interface must be implemented by every downstream auth manager, so the interface has to stay small.

clusters.rule: Do not set document.title from inside React components in the Airflow UI; the title is defined once in index.html.
clusters.trigger: A document.title assignment appears inside a useEffect in a .tsx file under the Airflow UI source tree.
clusters.rationale: Per-page title juggling in components fights the single definition and leaves stale titles when the component unmounts.

clusters.rule: Resolve the authenticated user through resolve_user_from_token (core_api/security.py) rather than calling get_auth_manager().get_user_from_token directly from middleware or route code.
clusters.trigger: A direct get_auth_manager().get_user_from_token( call appears outside resolve_user_from_token.
clusters.rationale: resolve_user_from_token carries the error translation and validation every caller needs; bypassing it produces routes that authenticate slightly differently.

clusters.rule: Name JWT duration parameters valid_for (a relative duration); do not call them expiry or expires_at, which imply an absolute timestamp.
clusters.trigger: A JWT-generation method takes a parameter named expiry or expires_at whose value is actually a TTL integer or timedelta.
clusters.rationale: Callers pass what the name says; an absolute-sounding name receiving a TTL produces tokens with wildly wrong lifetimes.

clusters.rule: When cursor pagination receives an unparseable cursor token (e.g. a malformed UUID for a Uuid column), raise HTTP 400 instead of silently falling back to the raw value.
clusters.trigger: An except block in _coerce_value or cursor-parsing code returns the original value rather than raising.
clusters.rationale: A silently accepted bad cursor returns a plausible but wrong page, which the client cannot detect.

clusters.rule: Keyset cursor pagination over a nullable sort column must use null-aware comparisons (an IS NULL tie-break or COALESCE) that match the ORDER BY null-ordering semantics.
clusters.trigger: Cursor code appends and_(*eq_conditions, col > value) for a column that can be NULL without an IS NULL guard.
clusters.rationale: col > NULL is never true, so rows with a null sort key silently vanish from or terminate the paging sequence.

clusters.rule: Use if/elif rather than consecutive if statements for the mutually exclusive lower_bound / lower_bound_excluded filter branches so the query does not emit redundant WHERE clauses.
clusters.trigger: Two consecutive `if self.value and self.value.lower_bound...` blocks appear for bound conditions that cannot both apply.
clusters.rationale: The reviewer pointed out that both branches can run and add duplicate predicates.

clusters.rule: Annotate DAG-bearing attributes in API parameter and datamodel classes as SerializedDAG (imported under TYPE_CHECKING from airflow.serialization.serialized_objects) rather than Any.
clusters.trigger: A property or attribute in a parameter/datamodel class is typed None | Any where the value is a serialized DAG.
clusters.rationale: Any here hides the one type the code actually depends on and defeats the type checking these modules otherwise get.

clusters.rule: Queries built from _RegexParam must be wrapped with apply_regex_query_timeout, and the _RegexParam docstring must state that obligation.
clusters.trigger: A route uses _RegexParam or regex_param_factory without a corresponding apply_regex_query_timeout call, or a _RegexParam class/factory has no docstring warning about it.
clusters.rationale: User-supplied regexes can be catastrophically slow in the database; the timeout is the only thing keeping one request from occupying a connection indefinitely.

clusters.rule: In SortParam.get_resolved_columns(), derive attr_name after applying to_replace so the resolved name matches the ORM attribute used in ORDER BY and cursor encoding.
clusters.trigger: attr_name = lstriped_orderby is assigned before the to_replace mapping is applied.
clusters.rationale: The reviewer caught the ordering defect: the encoded cursor referred to a column the ORDER BY did not use.

clusters.rule: When a Pydantic validator silently coerces an unrecognised stored value to None, emit a log.warning so schema drift between the server and the database stays observable.
clusters.trigger: `except ValidationError: return None` in a Pydantic validator with no preceding log.warning when the value was not already None.
clusters.rationale: Silent coercion turns a schema mismatch into an empty field in the UI with nothing anywhere indicating why.

clusters.rule: Boolean timetable properties consumed by the API (e.g. is_backfillable) must be persisted as a DagModel column via a migration, not derived at runtime by matching timetable_summary strings.
clusters.trigger: A frozenset of timetable summary strings is used in a datamodel or route to derive a boolean DAG property instead of reading a DagModel column.
clusters.rationale: Summary strings are display text from arbitrary timetables, including third-party ones; matching on them silently misclassifies any timetable not in the list.

clusters.rule: When redacting a dict value in an API response serializer, keep it a JSON-serialisable dict rather than wrapping the result in str().
clusters.trigger: str(redact(value)) where value is a dict in a Pydantic response serializer or validator.
clusters.rationale: Stringifying turns structured trigger kwargs into a Python repr the client has to parse, and it leaks into the public schema.

clusters.rule: Compare DagRunType enum members directly against dm.allowed_run_types rather than comparing their .value.
clusters.trigger: DagRunType.<member>.value not in dm.allowed_run_types (accessing .value before the membership test).
clusters.rationale: allowed_run_types holds enum members, so the .value comparison never matches and the check always rejects.

clusters.rule: Partition-date-window localization implemented inline in a route must not silently use a different interval convention from DagRun.apply_partition_date_window; consolidate the logic or cross-reference it in a comment.
clusters.trigger: An inline timetable.localize_partition_datetime call in a route duplicates DagRun.apply_partition_date_window with a different inclusive/half-open boundary.
clusters.rationale: The reviewer noticed the two copies had already drifted on the interval boundary.

clusters.rule: Validate that a requested try_number exists in the database before using it to build extra links, and return 404 when it does not.
clusters.trigger: ti.try_number = try_number is assigned in an extra-links route with no preceding check that the try number exists.
clusters.rationale: Without the check the endpoint renders links for a try that never ran, which look valid to the caller.

clusters.rule: Do not name a variable task_instance when it may hold either a TaskInstance or a TaskInstanceHistory; use a neutral name such as row, entity, or model.
clusters.trigger: A variable named task_instance is assigned from a query that can return either TI or TIH ORM objects.
clusters.rationale: The two models have overlapping but different attributes; the name tells the next reader they can rely on TI behaviour that may not be there.

clusters.rule: Use entity.name when collecting pool names in bulk-action validation; check attribute names against the actual Pydantic body class before building error lists.
clusters.trigger: invalid_entities.append(entity.pool) or a similar wrong attribute access on a PoolBody instance in bulk-action validation.
clusters.rationale: PoolBody has no such attribute, so the validation path raises instead of reporting the invalid entities.

clusters.rationale: These are the two cases clients depend on to terminate iteration, and the ones most often wrong.

clusters.rule: Every new router included in the execution API's authenticated_router must have a matching endpoint(...).didnt_exist entry in the unreleased Cadwyn version file.

clusters.rule: Query-string parameters that are used as regex patterns must reject the empty string with HTTP 400 rather than executing regexp_match("").
clusters.trigger: A regex query parameter (e.g. partition_key_pattern) is validated against None only, not against the empty string.
clusters.rationale: An empty pattern matches everything, so the filter the caller asked for silently does nothing.

clusters.rule: A new state table keyed on an asset must come with a decided lifecycle for its rows when the corresponding AssetActive row is removed - a cascade delete or an explicit GC policy - not unbounded accumulation.

clusters.rationale: Orphaned state rows in the metadata database are never cleaned up by anything else and grow without limit.

clusters.rule: When a new conditional branch is added in a service method, update the response-serialisation helper to cover it so the branch is not dead code.

clusters.rule: Assign a large dict to a named variable before passing it to Model.model_validate() rather than inlining the literal in the call.

clusters.rationale: A scoped session shares the caller's connection, so committing it commits the caller's work too; only a genuinely separate session gives early visibility without that side effect.

clusters.rule: config.yml descriptions must not name internal database tables; describe the concept in user-facing terms instead.

clusters.rule: Do not add email- or SMTP-related configuration options to airflow-core; route email settings through the SMTP provider.

clusters.rule: Do not define domain-model enums (e.g. WeightRule) in configuration.py; put them in the module that owns the concept.

clusters.rule: Type warning_types-style parameters as an open-ended homogeneous tuple (tuple[DagWarningType, ...]) rather than a fixed-length tuple.
clusters.trigger: A parameter typed tuple[DagWarningType, DagWarningType] is added or modified in dag_processing/collection.py.

clusters.rule: In DagBundleManager._refresh_dag_bundles, remove a bundle from _force_refresh_bundles only after DB persistence succeeds, and clear _bundle_versions when persistence fails.

clusters.rule: Generate the executor workload type error message from the ExecutorWorkload union rather than listing the type names by hand in an f-string.

clusters.rationale: Ignoring slots lets one workload type starve task instances of the executor's fixed capacity.

clusters.rationale: Airflow supports multiple active schedulers; without skip-locked selection two of them dispatch the same row.

clusters.rule: A foreign-key column used as a subquery filter predicate in scheduler queries must have an explicit Index(...) declaration unless an existing index is confirmed to cover it.

clusters.rationale: Airflow does not get an index on an FK for free on all supported databases, and these predicates run on every scheduler loop.

clusters.rule: To call get_template_context from the triggerer, construct a RuntimeTaskInstance via RuntimeTaskInstance.model_construct(...); do not call it on a plain TaskInstance.
clusters.trigger: .get_template_context() is called on an airflow.executors.workloads TaskInstance inside the triggerer job runner.

clusters.trigger: `with suppress(Exception):` is introduced around an await call in triggerer_job_runner.py.
clusters.rationale: Cleanup failures in the triggerer are otherwise completely invisible, and the triggerer is a long-lived process where they accumulate.

clusters.rule: An Alembic upgrade() must not DELETE or truncate existing rows in place of a data-preserving migration; a bare DELETE FROM with a TODO is not acceptable.
clusters.trigger: op.execute("DELETE FROM ...") is added in an upgrade() function alongside a "# TODO: Implement data-preserving migration" comment.
clusters.rationale: Users run these migrations against production metadata databases; silent data destruction on upgrade is unrecoverable.

clusters.rationale: The two-path form makes the retention behaviour of any given row impossible to reason about and changes retroactively when the config changes.

clusters.rule: Route SQLAlchemy 1.4/2.0 compatibility shims through airflow.utils.sqlalchemy rather than inline try/except ImportError blocks in individual model files.
clusters.trigger: A model file adds a try/except ImportError block to shim mapped_column or Mapped from sqlalchemy.orm instead of importing from airflow.utils.sqlalchemy.
clusters.rationale: One shim in one place is what makes the eventual version drop a single-file change instead of a sweep across every model.

clusters.rule: Validate user-supplied DAG run configuration with dag.params.deep_merge(dag_run_conf).validate() before starting a backfill.
clusters.trigger: A backfill code path passes dag_run_conf to create_dagrun (or similar) without first calling dag.params.deep_merge(...).validate().
clusters.rationale: Without the validation, bad user input surfaces as a 500 from deep inside run creation instead of a 4xx naming the offending param.

clusters.rule: Extract the duplicated encrypt/decrypt field logic into a shared mixin instead of copying the Connection model's get_extra/set_extra + synonym pattern into a new model.
clusters.trigger: A new model re-implements the get_extra/set_extra property and synonym pattern already present in the Connection model.
clusters.rationale: The reviewer flagged the copied Fernet handling on connection_test.py.

clusters.trigger: mapped_column(sa.JSON, ...) or Column(sa.JSON, ...) appears without parentheses on the type.
clusters.rationale: The project writes them instantiated throughout, and the bare-class form behaves differently once a type takes arguments.

clusters.rule: Prefix module-internal helper functions with an underscore so they do not become part of the public API surface.
clusters.trigger: A new module-level function is added in airflow-core without a leading underscore but referenced only within the same file or package.
clusters.rationale: General Python API-surface hygiene raised on one new helper.

clusters.rationale: The hit rate is the metric operators use to size this cache; a path that skips the counter makes it read low exactly under the concurrency it is meant to measure.

clusters.rule: Do not call session.flush() midway through a write_dag unit of work; add every related object to the session first and flush once at the end.
clusters.trigger: A session.flush() call appears mid-function inside write_dag or a similar multi-object DB write, before all related objects have been added.
clusters.rationale: A mid-way flush leaves half the DAG's rows persisted if a later step raises, which the readers of those tables cannot distinguish from a complete write.

clusters.rule: When updating a DagVersion record, update bundle_version alongside the other version metadata.
clusters.trigger: Code updates DagVersion (or calls DagVersion.get_latest_version) without also updating the associated bundle_version.

clusters.rule: In PartitionMapper.to_upstream() implementations, derive the parse format from self.output_format rather than hard-coding a slice length and format string.

clusters.rationale: output_format is overridable, so a hard-coded parse silently misreads keys the mapper itself produced.

clusters.rationale: The scheduler waits on the key the mapper emits; a naive datetime shifts it by the UTC offset and the dependency never resolves.

clusters.rule: Update the docstring when a method is decorated with @provider_info_cache so it describes the cached semantics rather than the former uncached helper's.

clusters.rationale: Every clearing entry point - UI, API, CLI - goes through that function; a flag handled elsewhere applies on some paths and not others.

clusters.rule: Public method overrides on Timetable subclasses must carry an explicit return-type annotation.

clusters.rationale: Timetable is implemented by providers and by users; the annotations are the contract they code against.

clusters.rationale: Two overlapping re-export mechanisms in one module drift apart, and the redundant one is what readers check first.
