clusters.trigger: A trigger or callback resolves a DAG file via get_unique_dag_module_name (sha1 of the absolute path) with no bundle_version or run-version identifier on the trigger payload.
clusters.rationale: The reviewer asked for the limitation to be written down at the resolution site.

clusters.rule: A new SharedStreamManager stream type whose upstream requires an ack or commit side-effect (e.g. a Kafka offset commit) must not be routed through the unidirectional filter_shared_stream API; scope the change to read-only or idempotent upstreams, or extend the API with an ack path first.
clusters.trigger: An open_shared_stream implementation commits, acks, or advances a cursor after a filter accepts, through the one-way filter_shared_stream channel.
clusters.rationale: The one-way channel gives the producer no way to learn whether the consumer actually handled the message, so acking there loses data on failure.

clusters.rule: Use a bounded asyncio.Queue (non-zero maxsize) for per-subscriber queues in shared-stream triggers; never put_nowait into an unbounded queue from a broadcast producer.
clusters.trigger: asyncio.Queue() with no maxsize inside a trigger subscribe/poll method, combined with put_nowait from a producer loop.
clusters.rationale: A slow subscriber on an unbounded queue turns into unbounded memory growth in the triggerer process, which serves every deferred task.

clusters.rule: When adding an i18n key to en/common.json, seed the same English string into every other locale's common.json.
clusters.trigger: A key is added to ui/public/i18n/locales/en/common.json and no other locale's common.json is touched.
clusters.rationale: Missing-key fallback behaves inconsistently across locales, so some users see the key name instead of text.

clusters.rule: Place new i18n keys under the namespace object matching their UI section (taskGroup.documentation), not as a flat concatenated top-level key (taskGroupDocumentation).
clusters.trigger: A top-level key is added to a locale JSON file whose name concatenates an existing namespace with a sub-concept.
clusters.rationale: Translators work namespace by namespace; flat keys fall outside the section they belong to and get missed.

clusters.rule: Capitalise acronyms in translation strings as they are in English (JSON, DAG, API, UI, ID).
clusters.trigger: A locale JSON value introduces a well-known acronym in all-lowercase.
clusters.rationale: The acronyms are product terms users match against the UI and docs; lowercasing them reads as a different word.

clusters.rule: Prefer icons from react-icons over custom inline SVG in the Airflow UI; add a custom icon only when react-icons has no suitable option.
clusters.trigger: A new custom icon component (createIcon({...}) or a raw <svg>) is added under ui/src/assets/ or ui/src/components/.
clusters.rationale: The shared library keeps sizing, stroke weight and theming consistent, which hand-rolled SVGs silently break.

clusters.rule: Pass only the i18n namespaces a file actually uses to useTranslation.
clusters.trigger: A useTranslation([...]) call lists namespaces that the file's translate calls never reference.
clusters.rationale: Each listed namespace is loaded for the component, so unused ones are bundle and fetch cost for nothing.

clusters.rule: Normalise response shapes and map fields in the backend API so it returns one consistent response type; do not re-shape API responses in frontend components.
clusters.trigger: A frontend component destructures and rebuilds an API response object to normalise its shape.
clusters.rationale: Every other consumer of that endpoint has to repeat the same re-shaping, and they will not do it the same way.

clusters.rule: Sync async-loaded data into react-hook-form fields with the useForm({ values: ... }) option rather than a useEffect that calls reset() or setValue().
clusters.trigger: A useEffect calls form.reset() or form.setValue() to populate fields after an async fetch resolves.
clusters.rationale: The values option is the library's supported path and does not fight user edits that land while the fetch is in flight.

clusters.rule: An /* eslint-disable max-lines */ comment must be accompanied by an inline justification for why the file legitimately exceeds the limit.
clusters.trigger: /* eslint-disable max-lines */ is added with no explanatory comment on the same or the following line.
clusters.rationale: Without a reason the disable outlives the situation that justified it and nobody can tell whether removing it is safe.

clusters.rule: When a component calls the same callback both debounced and immediately, cancel any pending debounced invocation before making the immediate call.
clusters.trigger: Both a debouncedX and a direct X call reach the same onChange within one event-handler chain (e.g. onPaste calling onChange while an earlier onInput scheduled debouncedOnChange).
clusters.rationale: The queued debounced call fires afterwards with the older value and overwrites what the immediate call just applied.

clusters.rule: DagVersion and BundleVersion must be represented by visually distinct icons in the UI.
clusters.trigger: DagVersionIndicator and BundleVersionIndicator (or equivalent components) render the same icon.
clusters.rationale: The two versions differ and users act on that difference; one icon for both makes the distinction invisible.

clusters.rule: An "All" option in a state or status filter must clear the filter by omitting the query parameter, not send state=all to the API.
clusters.trigger: A filter option whose value is the string "all" is passed through as a query parameter to an Airflow API endpoint.
clusters.rationale: The API has no "all" state, so the request either 422s or filters to nothing.

clusters.rule: Do not wrap a single stable function delegation in useCallback with an empty dependency array in the Airflow UI; pass the stable reference directly.
clusters.trigger: useCallback(() => stableFn(arg), []) is added where stableFn is already stable and the wrapper adds no logic.
clusters.rationale: The UI builds with React Compiler, which already handles memoisation; the manual wrapper is noise that can also capture a stale arg.

clusters.rule: Shared literal constants in the Airflow UI (localStorage keys, gradients, pixel offsets, colours) must live in a `constants.ts` module — the global `src/constants/` one for cross-cutting keys, the feature folder's own for feature-local values — not inline in components.
clusters.trigger: A `.tsx` component defines or inlines a string/number literal (localStorage key, gradient string, pixel offset) that is also used by another component instead of importing it from a constants module.
clusters.rationale: Duplicated literals drift apart silently; the reviewers want one place to look for a key or a shared visual value.

clusters.rule: When a persisted UI state value becomes invalid because the URL context it depends on is absent (e.g. `dagView` set to gantt with no `runId`), add a `useEffect` that coerces the stored value back to a valid default.
clusters.trigger: A `useLocalStorage`-backed view mode is read in a layout that can be rendered without the URL param that mode requires.
clusters.rationale: A stale localStorage value otherwise renders a view that cannot work for the current route.

clusters.rule: Normalize field values (e.g. `""` to `undefined`/`null`) before comparing them against the initial value when building an `updateMask`; do not push a field into `updateMask` based on an un-normalized comparison.
clusters.trigger: diff adds an `updateMask.push(...)` guarded by a raw `!==` comparison between a form value and its initial value.
clusters.rationale: An empty input and an absent value are the same edit; comparing raw values marks untouched fields as changed.

clusters.rule: Use the OpenAPI-generated react-query hooks for all API calls in the UI; do not write raw `fetch` calls with manually encoded query strings.
clusters.trigger: diff adds `fetch(`${OpenAPI.BASE}...`)` or manual `encodeURIComponent`/`join("&")` query construction in `airflow-core/src/airflow/ui/src/queries/`.
clusters.rationale: Hand-rolled calls bypass generated types, auth handling and cache keys, and drift when the spec changes.

clusters.rule: Do not prop-drill URL search-param values (e.g. `tryNumber`) through multiple component levels; read them directly from `useSearchParams` in the consuming component.
clusters.trigger: diff threads a value that originates from the URL through one or more intermediate component props.
clusters.rationale: The URL is already global state; passing it down couples intermediate components to data they do not use.

clusters.rule: Use Chakra semantic color tokens in `.tsx` component files; do not reference hardcoded colour-scale strings outside the designated theme/utils file.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a literal colour scale reference (e.g. `blue.500`, `green.300`) in a component instead of a semantic token.
clusters.rationale: Hardcoded scales break the light/dark theming the semantic tokens provide.

clusters.rule: When a component queries with a hard `limit`, compare `total_entries` against the limit and give the user a way to see the remainder (e.g. a '+ N more' modal) rather than silently truncating.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a component that renders a limited list without any affordance for the case `total_entries > limit`.
clusters.rationale: Silent truncation hides data the user has no way of knowing exists.

clusters.rule: Filter-reset logic must clear only filter search params; it must not delete the ordering/sort param.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a reset handler that deletes search params by iterating broadly or that includes the ordering key in the delete list.
clusters.rationale: Sort order is a separate user preference from filtering and should survive a filter reset.

clusters.rule: Filter inputs that are redundant in a context-specific view (e.g. a DAG ID filter on a page where `dagId` is already in the URL path) must be hidden by conditional rendering.
clusters.trigger: diff reuses a shared filters component on a scoped page without conditionally hiding the filter that the route already fixes.
clusters.rationale: A filter that cannot change the result set is noise and invites confusing states.

clusters.rule: Group a feature's sub-components in a named folder (e.g. `TaskFilters/`) with a single barrel export, and import only the folder's root component from outside.
clusters.trigger: diff adds an import that reaches into a feature folder for a non-root sub-component.
clusters.rationale: Keeps the feature's internals refactorable and its public surface one component.

clusters.rule: Reset the pagination OFFSET search param whenever a filter or filter mode changes, so the user is not left on a now-empty page.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a handler that sets a filter search param without also clearing/resetting the offset param.
clusters.rationale: The offset from the previous, larger result set can exceed the new total and shows an empty table.

clusters.rule: Use `airflow/utils/hashlib_wrapper.py` instead of calling `hashlib.md5()` directly, so hashing still works in FIPS-enabled environments.
clusters.trigger: diff adds `import hashlib` or a `hashlib.md5(` call in airflow-core Python source.
clusters.rationale: Bare MD5 raises under FIPS; the wrapper passes `usedforsecurity=False`.

clusters.rule: A new Alembic migration must add its `_REVISION_HEADS_MAP` entry for the next unreleased Airflow version, and the map must stay monotonic: each version's head must chain back through the previous version's head, never to a later revision.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a migration under `airflow/migrations/` without a `_REVISION_HEADS_MAP` entry, or adds/edits an entry under an already-released version key or one whose `down_revision` does not follow the previous head.
clusters.rationale: The map drives upgrade/downgrade targeting per release; a mis-ordered or wrongly-versioned entry sends users to the wrong revision.

clusters.rule: E2e page objects and specs must take the DAG under test from `testConfig.testDag.id`; do not hardcode a DAG ID, neither as a spec-level constant nor as a default parameter value on a page-object method.
clusters.trigger: diff adds `const DAG_ID = "example_bash_operator"` in `tests/e2e/specs/*.ts`, or a `tests/e2e/pages/*.ts` method with a default string argument such as `dagId: string = "example_bash_operator"`.
clusters.rationale: A hidden default silently binds the suite to one example DAG and hides which DAG a test actually exercises.

clusters.rule: E2e specs that assert on state produced by a DAG run must trigger the DAG and wait for `"success"` in a `test.beforeAll` block before running assertions.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a `test.describe` block in `tests/e2e/specs/*.ts` asserting run-dependent state without a `beforeAll` that triggers the DAG and verifies its status.
clusters.rationale: Otherwise the assertions depend on leftover state from other specs.

clusters.rule: Mermaid initialisation in the Airflow UI must be owned by a React context provider under `src/context`, not by a module-level mutable variable.
clusters.trigger: diff adds or modifies mermaid initialisation outside `airflow-core/src/airflow/ui/src/context/`.
clusters.rationale: Module-level init state is not re-entrant across renders and cannot react to theme changes.

clusters.rule: In e2e page objects targeting an `InputWithAddon`, locate the field with `getByText(label)` plus `.locator('input')` rather than `getByRole('textbox', { name: ... })`.
clusters.trigger: diff adds `getByRole("textbox", { name: ... })` in a page object for a field rendered by `InputWithAddon`.
clusters.rationale: That component does not give the inner input an accessible name, so the role query never matches.

clusters.rule: In `FileTaskHandler._read`, treat `UP_FOR_RETRY` and `UP_FOR_RESCHEDULE` as states with a completed attempt rather than actively-running states, and serve their logs through the fallback path.
clusters.trigger: diff changes the `ti.state` condition in `FileTaskHandler._read` around `TaskInstanceState.UP_FOR_RETRY` / `UP_FOR_RESCHEDULE`.
clusters.rationale: Those states have finished an attempt, so streaming from a live worker returns nothing.

clusters.rule: Express carve-outs from `State.unfinished` as a module-level `frozenset` constant rather than inline `... or state == SPECIFIC_MEMBER` conditions.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a `ti.state not in State.unfinished or ti.state == ...` pattern.
clusters.rationale: The set of exceptional states is the thing being defined; naming it once keeps the branches consistent.

clusters.rule: Do not prefix a TypeAlias or class with `Legacy` for a shape that will keep existing indefinitely; use a domain-meaningful contrast such as `LogResponse` vs `StreamingLogResponse`.
clusters.trigger: diff introduces a `Legacy`-prefixed TypeAlias or class name.
clusters.rationale: Non-streaming log providers are not going away, so `Legacy` misdescribes the type as deprecated.

clusters.rule: Enums that DAG authors in other languages must understand (WeightRule, TriggerRule, and similar) must be defined in the ExecAPI OpenAPI spec, not shared through Python code or `airflow-shared`.
clusters.trigger: diff moves or adds an Airflow enum to `airflow-shared/`, or imports one from there in task-SDK or provider code.
clusters.rationale: The Go and Java SDKs generate from the spec; a Python-only home makes the value unavailable to them.

clusters.rule: Custom SQLAlchemy `@compiles` functions must emit bound parameters, never string-interpolated values.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a `@compiles` function building SQL with an f-string, `%` or `.format()` containing column or value expressions.
clusters.rationale: Interpolating user-controlled values into compiled SQL is an injection path.

clusters.rule: A provider module path may only be added to the `test_providers_modules_should_have_tests` allowlist in the same PR that adds the referenced test file.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a path string to the project-structure allowlist without the corresponding test file in the same PR.
clusters.rationale: The allowlist is a promise that coverage exists; adding the path first makes the check permanently lie.

clusters.rule: Test names that reference a multi-word SQLAlchemy/DB exception must separate the words with underscores (`data_error`, not `dataerror`).
clusters.trigger: diff adds a test function whose name concatenates a known multi-word exception name without underscores.
clusters.rationale: Run-together names are unsearchable and read wrongly in test output.

clusters.rule: Alembic stairway migration tests must include the failing revision ID in the failure message.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a loop over migration revisions calling `command.upgrade`/`downgrade` without re-raising or failing with the `revision_id` in the message.
clusters.rationale: Without it the CI log says only that some migration broke, and the revision has to be bisected by hand.

clusters.rule: When an airflow-core test exercises code whose raise site now lives in `airflow.sdk`, assert against the exception class imported from the SDK package, not the same-named class in `airflow.exceptions`.
clusters.trigger: diff imports an exception from `airflow.exceptions` in a test whose subject raises the SDK's copy of that class.
clusters.rationale: After the class moved, the two are distinct types and the assertion can never match.

clusters.rule: In prose — docstrings and test names — spell the Python class as `Dag`, not `DAG`.
clusters.trigger: diff adds or edits a docstring or test name using all-caps `DAG` for the Python class in a sentence.
clusters.rationale: The project renamed the class and standardised the prose spelling with it.

clusters.rule: Tests asserting on a tag/stats dictionary that should be fully specified must assert full dict equality, not a series of per-key assertions.
clusters.trigger: diff replaces `assert tags == {...}` with individual `assert tags["key"] == ...` assertions.
clusters.rationale: Per-key assertions let unexpected extra keys pass silently, which is exactly the regression these tests exist to catch.

clusters.rule: Prefer top-level `def test_*` functions over tiny one-scenario test classes in files whose dominant pattern is top-level functions.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a narrow new test class to a file where top-level test functions are the established pattern.
clusters.rationale: A class per scenario adds nesting without shared setup and fragments the file.

clusters.rule: Paginated bulk-action API endpoints must have a test that exercises multi-page traversal (e.g. `limit=1`) to prove the action applies across every page.
clusters.trigger: diff adds tests for a paginated bulk PATCH/POST endpoint with no `limit=1` case.
clusters.rationale: Bulk handlers commonly act only on the first page; single-page tests never see it.

clusters.rule: New task-group / task-instance state-change API handlers must have unmocked integration tests covering upstream and downstream propagation, past/future run coverage and the deadlock/409 paths.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a `TestPatch*TaskGroup`/`TestPatch*TaskInstance` class whose tests all mock the underlying state-transition method.
clusters.rationale: Mocking the transition leaves the real DB logic — the part that breaks — untested.

clusters.rule: Tests for endpoint parameters that accept several values (e.g. True/False/None filter flags) must be `@pytest.mark.parametrize`d, not folded into one assertion block.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a test function asserting several filter-param combinations sequentially in a single body.
clusters.rationale: Parametrized cases report which combination failed instead of stopping at the first assertion.

clusters.rule: Tests for async-generator middleware in the execution API (e.g. `_extract_w3c_trace_context`) must cover the `athrow` path and assert whether `detach` is called on it.
clusters.trigger: diff adds or modifies tests for such a generator without a case that throws into the generator.
clusters.rationale: Route errors take the throw path, which is where context leaks happen.

clusters.rule: When an execution-API feature claims multi-backend support through SQLAlchemy constructs such as `regexp_match`, its tests must run against every claimed backend, not just Postgres.
clusters.trigger: diff adds tests marked only `@pytest.mark.backend("postgres")` for a backend-portable construct.
clusters.rationale: These constructs compile differently per dialect, so a Postgres-only test proves nothing about MySQL or SQLite.

clusters.rule: Version-compat guards in airflow-core tests must name the lowest Airflow version at which the change actually landed (e.g. `AIRFLOW_V_3_0_PLUS` when the move happened in 3.0).
clusters.trigger: diff uses `AIRFLOW_V_3_1_PLUS` or higher to guard a symbol introduced or moved in an earlier 3.x release.
clusters.rationale: An over-tight guard silently skips the test on versions where it should run.

clusters.rule: Do not add redundant `try/except ImportError` compatibility shims: not in airflow-core tests for symbols that exist in the current core, and not in provider modules for imports that `airflow.providers.common.compat` already redirects.
clusters.trigger: diff introduces a `try: from airflow.X import Y / except ImportError: ...` block where the import cannot fail, or duplicates a redirect the common.compat layer already performs.
clusters.rationale: Dead compat branches are never exercised and hide which versions are really supported.

clusters.rule: Consolidate multiple `session.flush()` calls in test setup into a single flush at the end, unless an earlier flush is required by a subsequent setup query.
clusters.trigger: Two or more `session.flush()` calls appear in the setup section of one test function or fixture.
clusters.rationale: Extra flushes add round trips and imply an ordering constraint that does not exist.

clusters.rule: When a Helm value is split into executor-specific keys (e.g. `workers.labels` into `workers.celery.labels` / `workers.kubernetes.labels`), document it as deprecated in favour of the per-executor keys — with an example for each new key — and never as a 'rename'.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a deprecation notice in chart docs, `NOTES.txt` or `_helpers.yaml` that says 'renamed to X' for a split value, or removes the worker example without adding one per new key.
clusters.rationale: There is no single replacement key; calling it a rename tells users to migrate to the wrong one.

clusters.rule: `chart/newsfragments/*.significant.rst` entries for breaking changes must enumerate every removed Helm value with its replacement as an explicit old-to-new mapping, not a prose summary.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a `.significant.rst` newsfragment mentioning removed values or dropped executor support without listing the specific key mappings.
clusters.rationale: Users upgrade by diffing their values file against this list; prose leaves them guessing.

clusters.rule: Kustomize-overlay CI must not pull arbitrary third-party DockerHub images without an image-allowlist validation step.
clusters.trigger: diff adds an `image:` referencing a third-party DockerHub image under `chart/kustomize-overlays/` with no allowlist or validation check.
clusters.rationale: An untrusted image running in CI can exfiltrate the job's credentials.

clusters.rule: The Helm OTel collector ConfigMap must expose a values key that lets users supply their own complete collector `config.yml` instead of only the Airflow-generated body.
clusters.trigger: diff adds an OTel collector ConfigMap template with no `.Values` override for the whole config body.
clusters.rationale: Collector configs are highly site-specific; without a full override users must fork the chart.

clusters.trigger: diff renders both `traces:` and `metrics:` pipelines unconditionally regardless of which backends are enabled.
clusters.rationale: An unconditional pipeline makes the collector fail or export to a backend the user never configured.

clusters.rule: In Helm Service templates, name the user-supplied annotations key `.Values.<component>.service.annotations` (not `extraAnnotations`) when the resource has no Airflow-generated annotations of its own.
clusters.trigger: diff introduces `.Values.<component>.service.extraAnnotations` on a Service where no Airflow-generated annotations are applied.
clusters.rationale: `extra` only makes sense when it is added to something; otherwise the key just reads wrong.

clusters.rule: Tests for `@operator_defaults` must include a case where the operator explicitly overrides the decorator's default (e.g. `retries=0` beating `@operator_defaults(retries=3)`).
clusters.trigger: diff adds `@operator_defaults` test cases that only cover the decorator supplying its value.
clusters.rationale: Precedence is the whole contract of the feature and is the part most likely to break.

clusters.rule: DAG serialization test fixtures containing fields that are always emitted because their defaults come from `airflow.cfg` at parse time (e.g. `catchup`, `max_active_runs`, `max_active_tasks`) must carry an inline comment saying so.
clusters.trigger: diff adds or edits a serialization fixture including such fields with no explanatory comment.
clusters.rationale: They look redundant against the schema, and future readers delete them.

clusters.rule: Sentinel objects such as `NOTSET` and `SET_DURING_EXECUTION` must have `repr()` and `str()` return the same stable string their `serialize()` produces, not the class name.
clusters.trigger: diff changes `__repr__`/`__str__` on a sentinel class to return the class name.
clusters.rationale: The serialized form is what shows up in logs and stored payloads; two spellings of the same sentinel confuse comparisons.

clusters.rule: A test that takes the `caplog` fixture must assert on captured log output; if there is nothing to assert, remove `caplog` and its setup.
clusters.trigger: A test function accepts `caplog` but contains no assertion against `caplog.text` or `caplog.records`.
clusters.rationale: Unused caplog implies coverage that is not there and slows the test.

clusters.rule: Do not bundle unrelated tightening (e.g. adding `spec=` to an existing MagicMock) into a PR whose title describes a distinct bug fix; drop the hunk or call it out in the PR body.
clusters.trigger: diff modifies an existing `mock.MagicMock()` to add `spec=` in a file otherwise changed only for an unrelated fix.
clusters.rationale: Unannounced extra changes make the fix harder to review and to revert.

clusters.rule: In `topological_sort` and other task-group ordering paths, index positions with a `dict[task_id, index]` rather than repeated `list.index()` lookups.

clusters.rule: Docker Compose services under `airflow-e2e-tests/` must not set a fixed `container_name`, must address each other by service-name hostname, and must not publish host ports without a demonstrated external need.
clusters.trigger: diff adds `container_name:` or a host-port mapping to a service in a compose file under `airflow-e2e-tests/`.

clusters.rule: In `chart/RELEASE_NOTES.rst`, wrap every Helm values key reference in double RST backticks (e.g. ``workers.celery.nodeSelector``).

clusters.rule: ADR documents must cite the actual function or method where the described behaviour lives; do not name a helper when the logic sits in the exported entry point.

clusters.rule: Source release tarballs built from the Java SDK must `export-ignore` binary wrapper artifacts such as `gradle-wrapper.jar`.

clusters.rule: Public interfaces and classes in the Java/Kotlin SDK must carry KDoc/JavaDoc.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a `public interface` or `public class` under `java-sdk/sdk/src/main/kotlin/` with no KDoc block.

clusters.rule: A provider's `tags` in `provider.yaml` must match the tags declared in its `get_provider_info.py`.
clusters.trigger: diff changes `tags:` in `provider.yaml` or the tags list in `get_provider_info.py` so the two disagree.
clusters.rationale: The two sources feed generated provider docs and produce conflicting categorisation.

clusters.rule: Hooks accepting an enum-like parameter such as `access_type` must validate it against the module's `VALID_*` constants and raise `ValueError` listing the allowed values before making any API call.

clusters.rationale: Without the guard a typo silently falls through to a default branch or a confusing remote error.

clusters.rule: A Trigger test that verifies one deadline path (e.g. `execution_deadline`) must set the other deadline (`end_time`) to a future value so exactly one timeout branch is exercised.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a Trigger unit test where both `end_time` and `execution_deadline` are already expired.
clusters.rationale: With both expired the test passes whichever branch fires and proves neither.

clusters.rule: Public provider API must stay backward compatible: renaming an executor attribute or method requires a deprecated property/forwarding wrapper under the old name, and removing an operator parameter requires deprecating it and mapping its values onto the replacement rather than dropping it.
clusters.trigger: diff renames a public attribute or method on a `BaseExecutor` subclass with no shim, or removes a parameter (e.g. `wait_policy`) from an operator and hard-codes one of its former values.

clusters.rule: When an operator's behaviour depends on a boolean that the trigger consumes (e.g. `cancel_on_kill`), the operator must expose it as a parameter and pass it through instead of hard-coding a value at trigger construction.
clusters.trigger: diff instantiates a trigger with a boolean argument that is not exposed as a parameter on the enclosing operator.
clusters.rationale: The behaviour is user-visible, so users must be able to choose it.

clusters.rule: When refactoring an operator's execution paths, a documented parameter (e.g. `awslogs_enabled`) must keep its documented effect in both the deferrable and non-deferrable paths.
clusters.trigger: diff refactors deferrable execution and leaves a previously-honoured parameter with no effect in `execute_complete`.
clusters.rationale: The parameter is still documented and still set by users; silently ignoring it in one path is a behaviour regression.

clusters.rule: Operator links whose data only exists after the job completes (e.g. a CloudWatch log stream ARN) must be persisted after the wait, not before it, in the non-deferrable path.
clusters.trigger: diff calls `_persist_links()` or equivalent before `hook.wait_for_job()` where the link data is only available post-completion.
clusters.rationale: Persisting early stores an incomplete link that never resolves for the user.

clusters.rule: When changing behaviour that existing tests cover, update the tests to cover both the new branch and the altered or removed one; do not leave assertions describing behaviour that no longer exists.
clusters.trigger: diff changes conditional logic in an operator without adding or updating tests for both sides of the condition.
clusters.rationale: Stale assertions pass while describing the wrong contract.

clusters.rule: Amazon provider docstrings must append `(templated)` to the description of every parameter listed in `template_fields`.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a `:param:` line in an Amazon provider operator, trigger or sensor for a field present in `template_fields` without the `(templated)` marker.
clusters.rationale: Users cannot otherwise tell which arguments accept Jinja.

clusters.rule: An AWS operator's `execute()` should return a minimal meaningful identifier (ARN, URI, name) rather than the raw boto3 response dict.
clusters.trigger: diff ends an AWS operator's `execute()` with `return response` where `response` is the raw boto3 response.
clusters.rationale: The whole response becomes an XCom payload with metadata users neither need nor can rely on.

clusters.rule: Provider how-to RST docs must order lifecycle sections to follow the resource lifecycle: Create, Start, Stop, Update, Delete.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a section to a provider how-to doc out of lifecycle order.
clusters.rationale: Readers follow these pages top to bottom as a walkthrough.

clusters.rule: A constraint stated in an operator docstring (e.g. a maximum list size) must be enforced by a runtime check in `__init__`; do not document bounds that are not validated.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a docstring stating a numeric bound for a parameter with no matching validation in `__init__`.
clusters.rationale: An unvalidated bound surfaces as an opaque API error at execution time instead of a clear failure at parse time.

clusters.rule: AWS executors must not log each individual task failure inline; aggregate failures and log them once at the summary point.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a `self.log.info(...)`/`self.log.error(...)` inside a per-task failure branch of an AWS executor sync loop.
clusters.rationale: A large failing batch floods the scheduler log with one line per task.

clusters.rule: AWS hooks that build a boto3 client must subclass the Boto-specific base (`AwsBaseHook`), not the generic `BaseHook`.
clusters.trigger: diff adds an AWS hook importing `BaseHook` from `airflow.providers.common.compat.sdk` while creating a boto3 client itself.
clusters.rationale: `AwsBaseHook` already handles session, region and credential resolution consistently with every other AWS hook.

clusters.rule: In deferrable operators, call `self.persist()` (or any link/XCom persistence) before `self.defer()`.
clusters.trigger: diff places a persist or XCom push after a `self.defer(...)` call in the same code path.
clusters.rationale: `defer()` raises `TaskDeferred`, so every line after it is unreachable.

clusters.rule: In `execute_complete`, read all required state from the trigger event dict; never fall back to an attribute set during `execute`.
clusters.trigger: diff uses `self.job_id` or another `execute`-time attribute inside `execute_complete` as a fallback when the event lacks the value.
clusters.rationale: `execute_complete` runs in a fresh task instance after deferral, so those attributes are not the ones `execute` set.

clusters.rule: An async trigger's `run()` must define and handle distinct SUCCESS and FAILURE terminal states; do not collapse every non-transitional status into a single success event.
clusters.trigger: diff adds an `async def run()` that yields a `TriggerEvent` without separate success/failure handling, or compares status against a single string rather than the provider's Enum.
clusters.rationale: Collapsing terminal states makes a failed remote job complete the task successfully.

clusters.rule: Avoid adding unit tests that only re-exercise paths an existing broader test already covers; prefer fewer, higher-value tests over branch-by-branch duplication.
clusters.trigger: diff adds several small test functions each covering a single branch already exercised as a sub-case of an existing test in the same file.
clusters.rationale: Duplicate coverage costs CI time and has to be maintained twice.

clusters.rule: In caplog-based trigger tests, call `caplog.set_level(...)` before invoking the method under test.
clusters.trigger: diff adds an `async def test_*` that asserts on `caplog.records`/`caplog.text` without a preceding `caplog.set_level`.
clusters.rationale: Otherwise capture depends on the ambient log level and the test fails only on some machines.

clusters.rule: Operator parameters referenced as `self.<param>` in `execute()`/`execute_complete()` must be declared as constructor arguments and assigned in `__init__`.
clusters.trigger: diff references `self.<param>` in an operator method where `<param>` is absent from the class `__init__` signature.
clusters.rationale: Users cannot set the value and the attribute does not exist at runtime.

clusters.rule: Spark provider docs for K8s-API tracking must state that the worker's kube client is used for pod tracking and that the K8s path bypasses `ResumableJobMixin`, so a retry submits a fresh driver rather than reattaching.
clusters.trigger: diff adds or edits a Requirements/Caveats section for K8s-based Spark submission under `providers/apache/spark/docs/`.
clusters.rationale: Operators of large clusters need to know a retry means a second driver, not a reattach.

clusters.rule: Spark provider documentation describing worker-crash and resubmission behaviour must mention that a non-idempotent job can conflict on resubmission, not only that compute is wasted.
clusters.trigger: diff adds prose about job resubmission under `providers/apache/spark/docs/` without mentioning idempotency conflicts.
clusters.rationale: The conflict, not the wasted compute, is the failure mode that corrupts user data.

clusters.rule: Inside async trigger methods (including helpers such as `safe_to_cancel()`), wrap synchronous DB and hook calls in `sync_to_async()`.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a synchronous call (e.g. `self.get_task_instance()`, `hook.stop_query()`) inside an `async def` of a `BaseTrigger` subclass without `await sync_to_async(...)`.
clusters.rationale: A blocking call in the triggerer stalls every other trigger sharing that event loop.

clusters.rule: In system tests, set `AIRFLOW_CONN_*` environment variables and perform connection setup — including reads of `SystemTestContextBuilder` values — inside a `@task`-decorated function, never at DAG-parse scope.
clusters.trigger: diff adds `os.environ[...] = ...` or connection construction at module/DAG-definition scope in a system test file.
clusters.rationale: Parse-time setup runs in the wrong process and resolves XComs before they exist, so the connection is missing in the worker that runs the tasks.

clusters.rule: System tests must mark each step of the task chain with its phase — setup, test body, teardown — following the pattern in canonical examples such as `example_sqs.py`.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a `chain(...)` in a system test with no comments or naming distinguishing the phases.
clusters.rationale: The system-test harness and readers rely on that structure to tell fixture work from the assertion under test.

clusters.rule: System tests must be run end-to-end locally before submission; reviewers reject system tests that have not been exercised.
clusters.trigger: diff adds or substantially modifies a file under `providers/*/tests/system/`.
clusters.rationale: System tests hit real cloud services that CI does not exercise on PRs, so review is the only gate.

clusters.rule: `pytest.raises(ClientError)` in provider tests must carry a `match=` asserting the specific AWS error code under test.
clusters.trigger: diff adds `pytest.raises(ClientError)` without `match=` in a provider unit test.
clusters.rationale: Any boto error satisfies the bare form, including one from unrelated setup.

clusters.rule: Remove unused `moto` fixtures and their `mock_aws` imports from unit test modules that make no real AWS API calls.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a `@pytest.fixture` wrapping a hook in `mock_aws()` that no test in the module references.
clusters.rationale: Leftover moto scaffolding implies AWS interaction that the module does not have and slows the suite.

clusters.rule: Kerberos auth resolution in the Spark provider hook must handle the krb5 ccache path alongside keytab/principal so REST calls to a Kerberized YARN RM always carry an Authorization header.

clusters.rationale: Deployments that authenticate via ccache get unauthenticated requests and an opaque 401.

clusters.rule: Do not land code nothing reaches: a new module-level constant must be referenced in the same PR, and a runtime-gated branch must be reachable from an entry point added in that PR or carry a TODO naming the follow-up PR that will make it reachable.

clusters.rationale: Scaffolding merged ahead of its caller is indistinguishable from a bug and rots before the follow-up lands.

clusters.rule: Notes and warnings in provider changelog RST must use the `.. note::` / `.. warning::` directive rather than plain prose.
clusters.trigger: A `docs/changelog.rst` diff adds a paragraph that reads as a note or warning without the directive.
clusters.rationale: Plain prose renders as body text on the docs site and loses the emphasis it was written for.

clusters.rule: Documentation claims about KubernetesPodOperator deduplication or ambiguity prevention must be scoped to the specific code path where the guarantee actually holds (e.g. `get_or_create_pod`), not asserted end-to-end.
clusters.trigger: A provider docs RST diff claims 'no possibility of ambiguity failure' or equivalent absolute language about pod reconnect behaviour.
clusters.rationale: The guarantee holds only inside one function; stated absolutely it promises something the operator does not deliver.

clusters.rule: New keyword arguments on `KubernetesPodOperator.__init__` (and other cncf.kubernetes operators) need a matching `:param name:` docstring entry describing the type; for `Callable` parameters the entry must name what each positional argument means.
clusters.trigger: diff adds a keyword argument to such an `__init__` with no corresponding `:param:` entry.
clusters.rationale: A bare callable signature is unusable without knowing what gets passed to it.

clusters.rule: When persisting pod identity to the task state store, either verify the stored `uid` against the live pod on reconnect or leave `uid` out of the payload.

clusters.rationale: Storing a field nothing checks implies a verification the code does not perform.

clusters.rationale: Users on older Airflow otherwise set it and see no effect with no explanation.

clusters.rule: When replacing a deprecated parameter with a version-gated successor, translate the deprecated parameter's value automatically for runtimes below the required version instead of forcing users to switch names.
clusters.trigger: diff deprecates parameter A and adds replacement B that only works on Airflow >= X.Y, with no fallback making B behave like A below X.Y.
clusters.rationale: Otherwise users on supported older versions must keep the deprecated name and are warned for doing the only thing that works.

clusters.rule: Kubernetes field selectors built from comma-separated `!=` expressions must be checked for the intended Boolean semantics (`NOT A AND NOT B`) before merging.

clusters.rationale: The comma is an AND, which is easy to write when an OR of exclusions was meant.

clusters.rule: Failures deleting a Kubernetes driver pod must not surface as task errors; wrap the cleanup call in `contextlib.suppress` or a flag that downgrades the failure to a warning.
clusters.trigger: A `_delete_driver_pod()` or equivalent cleanup call appears inline in a polling loop with no error suppression or configurable severity.
clusters.rationale: A cleanup hiccup should not fail a job that otherwise succeeded.

clusters.rule: Do not change the default value of an existing operator or hook parameter used by pre-existing code paths; a new path may enforce its own floor (e.g. with `max()`), but the legacy default must stay as it was.
clusters.trigger: diff changes the default of an `__init__` parameter (e.g. `status_poll_interval`) that pre-existing execution paths already use.
clusters.rationale: Changing a default silently changes behaviour for every existing user who never set it.

clusters.rationale: On failure the payload has no `driverState`, so the real error is replaced by a KeyError.

clusters.rule: Provider CLI commands must raise `SystemExit` for user-facing configuration errors, not `AirflowConfigException`/`AirflowException`.
clusters.trigger: A `raise AirflowConfigException(...)`/`raise AirflowException(...)` appears inside a CLI command function.
clusters.rationale: CLI argument validation elsewhere exits with a message rather than a traceback.

clusters.rule: Provider secrets-backend classes must implement only the methods declared on `BaseSecretsBackend`; do not add extra public methods (e.g. `get_config`) absent from the base interface.

clusters.rationale: Nothing calls the extra method, and it implies a backend capability the secrets machinery does not use.

clusters.rule: Freeze time with `time_machine` in tests that compare timestamps or durations; do not derive expected values from `datetime.now()`/`utcnow()`.
clusters.trigger: A test calls `datetime.datetime.now()` or `utcnow()` to compute an expected duration or timestamp rather than using `@time_machine.travel`.
clusters.rationale: Clock-relative expectations are flaky under slow CI.

clusters.rule: In `SparkKubernetesOperator` pod-selection tests, keep `metadata.name` identical across all mock pods and set `deletion_timestamp` explicitly so each selection criterion is exercised independently.

clusters.rationale: Differing names let the name check alone decide the result, so the other criteria are never tested.

clusters.rule: Provider documentation that exposes a subset of an upstream library's capabilities must link the upstream capability list and state which features are not yet supported.

clusters.rationale: Users otherwise read the shorter list as the library's full capability.

clusters.rule: Complete runnable DAGs in provider documentation must be pulled in with `.. exampleinclude::` from a tested file under `example_dags/`; `.. code-block:: python` is for fragments only.

clusters.rationale: Inline DAGs are never executed by CI and rot; included examples are tested.

clusters.trigger: A new `example_dags/*.py` omits `schedule` on its `@dag` or `DAG()` definition.
clusters.rationale: An unspecified schedule inherits a default that starts running the example on import.

clusters.rule: Provider factory mappings keyed by enum members must be annotated `dict[EnumType, ...]`, and public entry points must accept both the enum and a string, normalising strings with an informative `ValueError`.
clusters.trigger: A `_providers` dict annotated `dict[str, type]` is keyed with enum instances, or a factory accepts only the enum where callers pass strings from connection config or YAML.
clusters.rationale: The values arrive as strings from user configuration, so an enum-only signature fails for every real caller.

clusters.rule: Do not set `trigger_rule="all_success"` explicitly on a `@task` or Operator.

clusters.rationale: It is the default, and stating it signals to readers that something non-standard is going on.

clusters.rule: Provider hooks mapping Airflow connection extras onto a third-party library's kwargs must filter on truthiness (`if extra.get(k)`), not on `is not None`, so empty-string values entered in the UI fall through to environment-based auth.

clusters.rationale: The connection UI stores untouched fields as empty strings, which then override the library's own credential discovery with nothing.

clusters.rule: Connection-extra field names in a provider hook must match the exact parameter names the target library accepts; where they differ, document the mapping and convert or load the value before passing it.

clusters.rationale: The mismatched key is silently ignored by the library and the user sees an auth failure with no clue why.

clusters.rule: Reuse the shared exception types from `providers/standard/exceptions.py` (e.g. `HITLRejectException`) instead of defining a per-provider duplicate for the same semantic error.
clusters.trigger: A provider defines a new exception class duplicating the purpose of one already in `providers/standard/exceptions.py`.
clusters.rationale: User code catches one type; a per-provider clone silently escapes those handlers.

clusters.rule: Do not expose operator or mixin parameters in `__init__` and docstrings before they are implemented; a stub parameter with no effect must be removed, or must raise/warn until the feature ships.
clusters.trigger: An operator stores `self.param = param` in `__init__` but no method in the class or its mixins ever reads it.
clusters.rationale: A documented parameter that does nothing is worse than a missing one — users set it and believe it took effect.

clusters.rule: Do not list `bytes` fields in `template_fields`.
clusters.trigger: An Operator subclass includes a parameter typed `bytes` in its `template_fields` sequence.
clusters.rationale: Jinja renders bytes as their repr (`b'...'`), so `.decode()` raises and binary parsers receive literal repr text.

clusters.rule: When building a prompt or string incrementally, do not interpolate the accumulator into the expression being appended to it; construct the string linearly from separate parts.
clusters.trigger: A method contains `prompt = prompt + (... f"{prompt}" ...)` where the variable being built is interpolated inside the appended expression.
clusters.rationale: The accumulated text is duplicated on every append.

clusters.rule: Provider operator methods that iterate over connection IDs must use the class's cached hook mapping (e.g. `self._db_hooks[conn_id]`) rather than constructing a hook on each iteration.
clusters.trigger: A loop over connection IDs calls a factory such as `self._get_db_hook(conn_id)` inside the loop while a cached property already exists on the class.
clusters.rationale: Each construction opens a fresh connection to the same database.

clusters.rule: Use `Literal[...]` for Pydantic model fields whose valid values are an enumerable set of strings; do not encode the constraint only in the field description.
clusters.trigger: A Pydantic `Field(description='One of: ...')` or plain `str` field whose accepted values are a fixed, enumerable set
clusters.rationale: A description string is not validated; a Literal makes the contract enforceable and visible to type checkers and generated schemas.

clusters.rule: Provider code must import Task SDK symbols through `airflow.providers.common.compat.sdk`, never directly from `airflow.sdk.*`.
clusters.trigger: A direct `from airflow.sdk.<module> import <Symbol>` inside any file under `providers/`
clusters.rationale: Providers support multiple Airflow core versions; the compat shim is what keeps them installable against cores where the SDK module does not exist or lives elsewhere.

clusters.rule: Import an optional provider feature dependency lazily inside the function that needs it, rather than at module level, when other code paths in the same module work without that dependency.
clusters.trigger: A module-level `try: import <optional_dep> / except ImportError: raise AirflowOptionalProviderFeatureException` in a module where only one of several independent operator or toolset paths needs the dependency
clusters.rationale: A module-level raise makes the whole module unimportable, breaking operators that never touch the optional dependency.

clusters.rule: In the common.ai LangChain bridge `_sync_call`/`_async_call`, catch `pydantic_core.ValidationError` alongside `ModelRetry` and route it through `_handle_retry`.
clusters.trigger: An `except ModelRetry` clause in `langchain_bridge.py` that does not also catch `ValidationError`
clusters.rationale: Reviewer-identified gap in one specific bridge implementation rather than a standing repo-wide expectation.

clusters.rule: A sqlglot-based denylist of data-modifying SQL statements must include `exp.Command`, sqlglot's fallback node for unrecognised syntax, so unparsed statements fail closed.
clusters.trigger: A tuple/set of `exp.*` node types used to reject mutating SQL that omits `exp.Command`
clusters.rationale: Anything sqlglot cannot classify becomes `exp.Command`; omitting it lets arbitrary unrecognised DDL/DML slip past validation.

clusters.rule: Log messages in `airflow.providers.common.compat.connection` must interpolate the actual hook class name instead of hardcoding `BaseHook`.
clusters.trigger: A `log.debug`/`log.info` call in `get_async_connection` containing the literal `BaseHook` after the hook became a parameter
clusters.rationale: A stale hardcoded class name in one helper's log line; a specific fix, not a standing rule.

clusters.rule: Tests for `get_async_connection` with a custom `hook=` argument must cover both the `aget_connection` path and the sync `get_connection` fallback path.
clusters.trigger: A test exercising `get_async_connection(hook=...)` that asserts only on the async branch
clusters.rationale: A missing-branch-coverage note on one specific helper's tests.

clusters.rule: Do not collapse `None` to an empty container with `param or []` in an operator `__init__` when the empty value has distinct meaning in the downstream API call; keep `None` and the empty list distinguishable.
clusters.trigger: `self.param = param or []` in an operator `__init__` where `param` is forwarded to an external API and an explicit empty list means something (e.g. clearing permissions)
clusters.rationale: `or []` erases the caller's ability to express 'send an empty list', which for some remote APIs is a destructive-but-intended request distinct from 'omit the field'.

clusters.rule: When a provider operator or hook gains a new documented parameter or changes its documented behaviour (auth types, supported options), update the class docstring and the matching provider RST guide under `providers/<name>/docs/` in the same PR.
clusters.trigger: A new `__init__` parameter or a changed `:param ...:` docstring list in a provider operator/hook with no corresponding edit to `providers/<name>/docs/operators/*.rst` or `providers/<name>/docs/connections/*.rst`
clusters.rationale: The published provider guides are the user-facing documentation; code-only changes leave them silently wrong at release time.

clusters.rule: In RST documentation, write version milestones as "Airflow version X.Y.Z", not a bare "version X.Y.Z".
clusters.trigger: An RST sentence containing `version <n>.<n>` without `Airflow` immediately before it
clusters.rationale: Provider docs sit alongside provider version numbers, so a bare version string is ambiguous about which artefact it refers to.

clusters.rule: Use `timezone.utcnow()` for timestamps in provider code rather than `datetime.now()`/`datetime.utcnow()`, and never initialise a mutable timestamp as a class-level attribute.
clusters.trigger: A class attribute assigned `datetime.now()` or `datetime.utcnow()` outside `__init__` in a provider module
clusters.rationale: Airflow standardises on timezone-aware UTC timestamps, and a class-level default is evaluated once at import and shared by every instance.

clusters.rule: Name provider migration files after the next unreleased Airflow/provider version; rename the file before merge if a new minor has been cut since the branch was opened.
clusters.trigger: A migration path under `providers/*/migrations/versions/` whose embedded version string is at or below the latest released version
clusters.rationale: The version in the filename is what tells operators which release first requires the migration; a stale one misleads upgraders.

clusters.rule: FastAPI `Query`/parameter descriptions in provider routes must describe what the implementation actually accepts (e.g. do not advertise comma-separated multi-field ordering when only a single field is supported).
clusters.trigger: A `Query(..., description=...)` string in a provider route that promises behaviour the handler does not implement
clusters.rationale: The description ships in the generated OpenAPI spec and the API reference, so a wrong one becomes a documented but unsupported contract.

clusters.rule: FastAPI route handlers in provider packages must carry an explicit return type annotation matching the decorator's `response_model`.
clusters.trigger: A handler declared with `response_model=Foo` but no `-> Foo` return annotation
clusters.rationale: The annotation is what makes the handler's contract checkable by mypy rather than only at request time.

clusters.rule: A SQLAlchemy `before_create` DDL event listener must not permanently mutate shared metadata such as `table.indexes`; express dialect differences with dialect-scoped DDL that adds or skips instead of discarding.
clusters.trigger: `table.indexes.discard(...)` / `.remove(...)` inside an `@event.listens_for(Table, 'before_create')` listener
clusters.rationale: The MetaData object is process-global, so a discard performed for one dialect silently removes the index for every later use of that table in the same process.

clusters.rule: Edge provider frontend code must issue HTTP calls through React Query (`useQuery`/`useMutation`) layered over Axios, not by calling Axios directly from components.
clusters.trigger: A direct `axios.get/post/...` call inside a `.tsx` component in the Edge plugin UI
clusters.rationale: React Query owns caching, refetching and request state for this UI; bypassing it produces components with hand-rolled loading and staleness handling.

clusters.rule: Regenerate a provider's OpenAPI client whenever its source spec YAML changes, so spec and `openapi-gen/` output stay in sync under the `ts-compile-lint-ui` hook.
clusters.trigger: A change to `openapi/*.yaml` in a provider UI package with no matching regeneration of the generated client, or the reverse
clusters.rationale: The generated client is committed to the tree; a spec change without regeneration means the UI compiles against a contract the backend no longer serves.

clusters.rule: Provider `package.json` files must not list `npm` itself or single-letter packages such as `i` among their dependencies.
clusters.trigger: `"npm"` or `"i"` appearing as a key in `dependencies` or `devDependencies` of a provider `package.json`
clusters.rationale: These entries are the fingerprint of a mistyped `npm i` command and pull an entire package manager into the shipped dependency tree.

clusters.rule: A provider's prek/pre-commit hooks and their supporting scripts must live inside that provider's own directory, not in the repository root.
clusters.trigger: A hook entry in a provider `hatch_build.py` (or provider hook config) pointing at scripts outside `providers/<name>/`
clusters.rationale: Providers are released as independent distributions; root-level scripts are not part of the provider package and break for anyone working on it standalone.

clusters.rule: Provider log handlers must track airflow-core field renames on structured log records (e.g. `.message` becoming `.event`) and version-gate the access when both cores are supported.
clusters.trigger: Access to `.message` on a structured log record inside a provider log handler
clusters.rationale: The record shape is core-owned; providers reading the old field emit empty or broken log lines against newer cores.

clusters.rule: A provider log handler that receives the task-log location from task startup metadata must not re-query `TaskInstance` from the metadata database to work out where to write.
clusters.trigger: A `TaskInstance.get_task_instance(...)` (or equivalent DB lookup) inside a provider log handler's write/emit path
clusters.rationale: Log handlers run in the worker/task process, which is not supposed to hold a metadata DB connection; the location is already supplied to it.

clusters.rule: Extract repeated `test_client.app.dependency_overrides[...]` setup into a shared fixture instead of duplicating it in each test method.
clusters.trigger: Several test methods in one class repeating the same `dependency_overrides` assignment block
clusters.rationale: Generic de-duplication advice about test setup, not a repo-specific expectation.

clusters.rule: When re-raising a missing optional provider dependency as an `ImportError`, suppress the chained original with `raise ImportError(...) from None`.
clusters.trigger: `except ImportError: raise ImportError(...)` for an optional dependency without `from None`
clusters.rationale: The chained traceback adds noise the user cannot act on; the actionable message is the install hint alone.

clusters.rule: Give `timetable_type` a sensible default in the `DagModel` constructor so tests do not have to assign it on every instance.
clusters.trigger: Tests assigning `dag_model.timetable_type = ""` in setUp or individual test bodies
clusters.rationale: A one-off suggestion about a single new column's default, prompted by one PR's test churn.

clusters.rule: In `GitDagBundle._initialize()`, assign and properly close `self.repo` before any early return on the cached-version path when `prune_dotgit_folder=False`.
clusters.trigger: A new early `return` in `_initialize()` after `_local_repo_has_version()` that leaves `self.repo` unset
clusters.rationale: A specific leaked/unset-attribute defect introduced by one refactor of that method.

clusters.rule: Treat `GitDagBundle.version` as a commit-ish (tag, branch or short SHA) and resolve it with `repo.commit(self.version).hexsha` before comparing it against `repo.head.commit.hexsha`.
clusters.trigger: A string equality comparison between `self.version` and `repo.head.commit.hexsha` in a git bundle method
clusters.rationale: Bundle versions are user-supplied refs, not full SHAs, so raw string comparison reports a mismatch for a repo that is already at the right commit.

clusters.rule: Do not import underscore-prefixed internals of a third-party package (e.g. `google.genai._api_client`, `structlog._output.WRITE_LOCKS`); where such an import is unavoidable, wrap it in `try/except ImportError` with a `None` fallback, guard every use of it, and add tests that catch upstream removal.
clusters.trigger: An import of a symbol whose module path contains a leading-underscore component from a third-party package under `providers/` or `task-sdk/src/`
clusters.rationale: Private internals carry no compatibility promise, so a routine dependency upgrade can break DAG parsing or task execution outright unless the import is optional and guarded.

clusters.rule: Keep the public surface of provider operators, hooks and extractors backward compatible: a changed return value, changed traversal, or new constructor keyword must be opt-in via a new parameter defaulting to the legacy behaviour, and existing public signatures (e.g. `BaseExtractor.__init__(self, operator)`) must keep working.
clusters.trigger: A diff that changes an existing operator's `execute()` return shape, alters what an existing hook method traverses or returns, or passes a new required keyword to a subclass constructor unconditionally
clusters.rationale: These classes are third-party extension points and DAG-facing API; silently changing their contract breaks user DAGs and out-of-tree subclasses at upgrade time with no deprecation path.

clusters.rule: When a trigger yields a `TriggerEvent` with `status: error` from a broad `except Exception`, prefix the message with the operation being performed rather than emitting the bare exception string.
clusters.trigger: `yield TriggerEvent({"status": "error", "message": str(err)})` inside a bare `except Exception` block
clusters.rationale: The event message is all the user sees in the task log; without the operation context an upstream error is untraceable to the call that produced it.

clusters.rule: When validation of a GCP resource identifier raises, the exception message must state every constraint the check enforces, including length bounds implied by the regex, not just the format.
clusters.trigger: A regex-based ID validation raising with a message that omits the length range the regex enforces
clusters.rationale: A user given only half the rule cannot fix their input from the message alone.

clusters.rule: Place forward-looking compatibility notes in a provider changelog above the upcoming release section, never inside or below an already-published release block.
clusters.trigger: A `.. note::` or compatibility banner inserted into or after an existing versioned release block in `changelog.rst`
clusters.rationale: Published release blocks are historical records; a note about future support inside one misattributes it to a release that never carried it.

clusters.rule: Add new provider documentation as `.rst` files wired into the existing docs structure, not as standalone `.md` files.
clusters.trigger: A new `.md` file added under `providers/*/docs/`
clusters.rationale: The provider docs are built by Sphinx from the RST tree; a Markdown file is never rendered or linked from the published site.

clusters.rule: Raise a dependency version floor — on a cross-provider `apache-airflow-providers-*` requirement or on an optional extra — only for a genuinely breaking change; an additive parameter with a `None` default or a new optional feature does not justify one.
clusters.trigger: A new or raised `>=x.y.z` constraint in a provider `pyproject.toml` accompanying a purely additive change
clusters.rationale: Every unnecessary floor narrows the installable version matrix and forces upgrades on users who do not use the new feature.

clusters.rule: Pass camelCase REST API field names (e.g. `definitionBody`, `routineType`) — not Python SDK attribute names (`body`, `type_`) — in the `fields`/update-mask argument of Google client update methods.
clusters.trigger: A writable-properties constant built from Python attribute names and passed as `fields` to a Google client update call
clusters.rationale: The update mask is sent to the REST API, which knows only its own field names; Python attribute spellings are silently ignored, so the update does nothing.

clusters.rule: Name provider system test files after the existing files in the same system-test folder; do not append a `_system` suffix.
clusters.trigger: A new file under `providers/*/tests/system/` named `test_<service>_system.py`
clusters.rationale: The system test runner and the docs that embed these files rely on the established naming; an off-pattern name is not picked up.

clusters.rule: Document a hook's connection configuration behaviour in its docstring: which `extra` keys are supported and in what precedence order, and exactly when a keyless fallback such as Application Default Credentials applies versus when an explicit key is still required.
clusters.trigger: A hook connection-init or auth method that adds conditional key-file skipping or several `extra.get(...)` branches without a matching `:param ...:`/docstring description
clusters.rationale: Connection setup is the part of a provider users configure by hand; undocumented precedence and fallback rules are only discoverable by reading the hook source.

clusters.rule: Read boolean Airflow configuration values with `conf.getboolean()`, never `conf.get()`.
clusters.trigger: `conf.get("<section>", "<key>", fallback=...)` for a key used as a boolean elsewhere
clusters.rationale: `conf.get` returns a string, so the literal `"False"` is truthy and the option silently cannot be turned off.

clusters.rule: Use the same `fallback=` value for every read of the same configuration (section, key) pair within a module.
clusters.trigger: Two or more `conf.get*()` calls for one (section, key) pair with different `fallback=` values in the same file
clusters.rationale: Divergent fallbacks make behaviour depend on which code path runs first when the option is unset.

clusters.rule: Provider documentation links must use the canonical `https://airflow.apache.org/docs/apache-airflow-providers-<name>/` form; do not omit the `-providers-` segment.
clusters.trigger: An RST hyperlink to `https://airflow.apache.org/docs/apache-airflow-<name>/`
clusters.rationale: The published docs are hosted under the providers path, so the short form is a dead link the moment the package is released.

clusters.rule: Each release version heading must appear exactly once in a provider's `changelog.rst`.
clusters.trigger: A version heading plus RST underline that already exists earlier in the same changelog file
clusters.rationale: Duplicate headings break the rendered changelog and the release tooling that parses it.

clusters.rule: Namespace a new provider by vendor, not by service: `package-name` in `provider.yaml` must be `apache-airflow-providers-<vendor>`, and a hook's `conn_type` must be vendor-qualified (e.g. `ibm_mq`) rather than a generic protocol category (`mq`).
clusters.trigger: A `provider.yaml` declaring `apache-airflow-providers-<vendor>-<service>`, or a hook declaring a generic `conn_type` such as `mq`, `queue` or `stream`
clusters.rationale: Amazon and Google consolidate every service under one vendor package, and `conn_type` is a global registry where a generic name collides with the next vendor implementing the same protocol.

clusters.rule: Instantiate `MessageQueueTrigger` with `queue=` carrying the full URI; `scheme=` takes only a scheme and raises `ValueError` at DAG parse time when given a URI.
clusters.trigger: `MessageQueueTrigger(scheme="<scheme>://...")` in a DAG or example
clusters.rationale: The failure happens during parsing, so the whole DAG file fails to import rather than the task failing at runtime.

clusters.rule: Items of `triggering_asset_events` are `AssetEvent` ORM objects: read their payload via the `.extra` attribute, not by dict-key subscription.
clusters.trigger: Square-bracket key access such as `event["payload"]` on an item iterated from `triggering_asset_events`
clusters.rationale: Subscripting the ORM object raises `TypeError` at task runtime, and example DAGs that do it are copied by users.

clusters.rule: Target `@patch` at the symbol as the module under test imports it; patching a path the module never imports is a silent no-op.
clusters.trigger: `@patch("airflow.providers.<pkg>.hooks.<module>.<name>")` where `<name>` is not imported by that module
clusters.rationale: Standard mock-library advice about patch targets, not a repo-specific expectation.

clusters.rule: Async hook tests must exercise the real method body with only the underlying I/O primitives patched, rather than patching the method under test itself.
clusters.trigger: `patch.object(hook, 'consume', side_effect=[...])` (or equivalent) replacing the very method the test claims to cover
clusters.rationale: Generic testing advice about not mocking the unit under test.

clusters.rule: A provider's docs requirements table must list exactly the packages declared in that provider's `pyproject.toml` dependencies — no extras, no omissions.
clusters.trigger: A row in the Requirements table of `providers/*/docs/index.rst` naming a package absent from the provider's `pyproject.toml`
clusters.rationale: The table is the published statement of what installing the provider pulls in; drift makes it a false promise.

clusters.rule: Every provider hook that declares a custom `conn_type` must have a matching `hooks:` block and `connection-types:` entry in the provider's `provider.yaml`.
clusters.trigger: A hook class with `conn_type = "<custom>"` and no corresponding `connection-types:` entry in `provider.yaml`
clusters.rationale: `provider.yaml` is what makes the connection type discoverable in the UI and the generated docs; without it the hook exists but users cannot configure a connection for it.

clusters.rule: Providers must not re-implement operators that already exist in airflow-core or the standard provider (e.g. `EmptyOperator`); point users at the core operator instead.
clusters.trigger: A new provider operator whose behaviour duplicates a core/standard operator, such as a no-op or passthrough task
clusters.rationale: Duplicates fragment the operator surface users have to learn and drift from the core implementation's behaviour over time.

clusters.rule: Provider code (hooks, listeners, plugins) must not call `settings.configure_orm()`; ORM setup belongs to the scheduler/executor process that hosts the provider code.
clusters.trigger: A `settings.configure_orm()` call anywhere under `providers/`
clusters.rationale: Re-configuring the ORM from provider code re-points the session factory for the whole process, affecting every other component running in it.

clusters.rule: Provider unit tests must build `Connection` fixtures with the provider's own `conn_type`, not a generic type such as `http`.
clusters.trigger: A test under `providers/*/tests/` creating a `Connection(conn_type="http")` for a hook that declares its own `conn_type`
clusters.rationale: Hook lookup and connection-form behaviour key off `conn_type`, so a generic type tests a path users never take.

clusters.rule: Every `__init__.py` in an `airflow/providers/` namespace directory must contain the legacy pkgutil namespace line `__path__ = __import__("pkgutil").extend_path(__path__, __name__)`; empty or implicit-namespace `__init__.py` files are not acceptable.
clusters.trigger: A new `__init__.py` under `providers/` (or `airflow/providers/`) that is empty or omits the `extend_path` line
clusters.rationale: Providers are separately installed distributions sharing one `airflow.providers` package path; pkgutil namespaces are what let them coexist in the same environment.

clusters.rule: Use proper RestructuredText footnote syntax in provider docs rather than plain bracketed numbers like `[1]`.
clusters.trigger: A `[N]` reference in `providers/*/docs/*.rst` that is not a real RST footnote or citation
clusters.rationale: A bare bracketed number renders as literal text with no link to its target.

clusters.rule: When a provider hook is fully async, the operator on top of it must wait exclusively through defer/trigger; do not add a synchronous polling path gated by `deferrable=False`.
clusters.trigger: A non-deferrable `while True` / `time.sleep` polling loop added to an operator whose hook is async
clusters.rationale: A blocking loop occupies a worker slot for the whole wait, which is precisely what the async hook and trigger exist to avoid.

clusters.rule: Adding deferrable mode to a provider operator requires both an update to that operator's RST docs page and a `providers/<pkg>/newsfragments/<pr>.feature.rst` newsfragment.
clusters.trigger: A diff adding `self.defer(...)` to a provider operator with no newsfragment file and/or no operator docs update
clusters.rationale: Deferrable mode is a user-visible feature that must appear in the provider's release notes and in the guide users configure it from.

clusters.rule: Build Azure blob names and paths with `posixpath.join`, never `os.path.join`.
clusters.trigger: `os.path.join` used to construct a blob name or path in an Azure hook or transfer
clusters.rationale: Blob names are always forward-slash separated, so `os.path.join` produces backslash-separated names on Windows workers.

clusters.rule: Use `str.removeprefix()` rather than `str.replace(prefix, "", 1)` when stripping a known leading prefix.
clusters.trigger: `.replace(prefix, "", 1)` used to strip a leading path prefix
clusters.rationale: General Python idiom advice that carries no repository-specific judgement.

clusters.rule: A trigger's timeout branch must always yield a `TriggerEvent` carrying the timeout status and a descriptive reason: do not `break`/`return` out of the polling loop, and wrap any cancellation side-effect in its own try/except so a failed cancel cannot replace the timeout event.
clusters.trigger: A polling loop in `providers/*/triggers/*.py` that reaches its timeout condition and breaks without yielding, or performs a cancel call in the timeout branch outside a dedicated try/except
clusters.rationale: A trigger that ends without yielding leaves the deferred task hanging, and a cancellation error surfacing instead of the timeout reports the wrong cause to the user.

clusters.rule: An `AirflowPlugin` subclass docstring must describe only the events the plugin actually registers and handles.
clusters.trigger: A plugin docstring claiming to handle event types (e.g. DAG run events) that the plugin body does not implement
clusters.rationale: Plugin docstrings are how integrators decide what a listener covers; an aspirational one leads them to expect callbacks that never fire.

clusters.rule: Assertions on `trigger.serialize()` must check that the result is a tuple, that the class path string matches the trigger's `__module__`/`__name__`, and that the full kwargs dict is as expected.
clusters.trigger: A test destructuring `trigger.serialize()` without verifying the tuple type or the fully-qualified class path
clusters.rationale: The serialized class path is what the triggerer uses to rebuild the trigger, so a wrong or moved path only fails in production if the test does not assert on it.

clusters.rule: Build trigger deadline values in tests with the same clock the trigger implementation uses; never mix `time.time()` in the test with `time.monotonic()` in the trigger.
clusters.trigger: A test constructing a deadline such as `END_TIME = time.time() + ...` for a trigger whose implementation reads `time.monotonic()`
clusters.rationale: The two clocks have unrelated epochs, so the deadline is meaningless and the test asserts on accidental behaviour.

clusters.rule: A task log handler's `delete_local_copy` must remove only the uploaded log file (`path.unlink()`), never its parent directory via `shutil.rmtree()`.
clusters.trigger: `shutil.rmtree(os.path.dirname(log_file))` in a task log handler's upload-and-delete path
clusters.rationale: The parent directory holds logs for other attempts and tasks, which the handler has no business deleting.

clusters.rule: A `ClassVar` dict used as an in-process cache in a provider utility is acceptable because provider worker processes are short-lived.
clusters.trigger: A reviewer questioning whether a `ClassVar[dict]` cache in a provider utility can grow unboundedly
clusters.rationale: This records the answer to a review question rather than an expectation a diff can violate.

clusters.rule: Read fields that exist directly on the `DagRun` model (e.g. `dagrun.team_name`) from the object itself instead of re-deriving them through `dag_version_info()`.
clusters.trigger: A `cls.dag_version_info(dagrun, "field_name")` call for a field that is a plain attribute on `DagRun`
clusters.rationale: The indirection adds a lookup that can disagree with the authoritative attribute on the run.

clusters.rule: When refactoring the OpenLineage extractor manager's no-extractor branch, keep the `unknownSourceAttribute` facet and the inlets/outlets fallback intact under the default `hook_lineage=True` configuration.
clusters.trigger: A change to the else/elif branching around `extract_metadata`'s no-extractor path in `openlineage/extractors/manager.py`
clusters.rationale: Describes a specific regression a single refactor introduced in one branch, not a standing rule.

clusters.rule: Update `tests/unit/openlineage/plugins/test_manager.py` whenever the OpenLineage extractor manager's branching changes.
clusters.trigger: A change to `openlineage/extractors/manager.py` with no corresponding test change
clusters.rationale: Generic keep-tests-in-step advice tied to one file pair.

clusters.rule: Do not call `logging.shutdown()` from a provider listener without proving the call cannot affect global Airflow logging.
clusters.trigger: A `logging.shutdown()` added inside a provider's listener plugin
clusters.rationale: Listeners run inside the scheduler and task processes, so shutting logging down there silences the host component's own logs.

clusters.rule: The install hint in an `AirflowOptionalProviderFeatureException` must read `pip install --upgrade <package>`, not a bare `pip install <package>`.
clusters.trigger: An `AirflowOptionalProviderFeatureException` message containing an install hint without `--upgrade`
clusters.rationale: The dependency is usually already installed at too old a version, so a plain install is a no-op and the user is left stuck.

clusters.rule: In the Postgres hook, do not skip psycopg3 notice logging with an early return when `enable_log_db_messages=True`; implement the psycopg3 notice handling instead.
