clusters.trigger: `if USE_PSYCOPG3 or not self.enable_log_db_messages: return` before the notice-logging loop in `postgres.py`
clusters.rationale: A specific shortcut taken in one psycopg3 migration PR, not a general expectation.

clusters.rule: A retryable-error tuple in the Postgres hook must list the narrowest psycopg exception subclasses (e.g. `UndefinedColumn`, `UndefinedTable`) from the matching package — `psycopg` for v3, `psycopg2` for v2 — never a broad class such as `OperationalError`.
clusters.trigger: A `_POSTGRES_RETRYABLE_ERRORS` tuple containing `OperationalError` or another broad psycopg exception class
clusters.rationale: Retrying on a broad class re-runs statements after genuine connection and authentication failures, turning a clear error into repeated timeouts.

clusters.rule: Assert a mock was called exactly once (`assert_called_once()` or a `call_count` check) before inspecting `call_args`.
clusters.trigger: Access to `mock_*.call_args` with no preceding call-count assertion
clusters.rationale: Standard mock-library advice with no repository-specific content.

clusters.rule: Type-stub packages (`types-*`) belong in a provider's dev/type-check dependency group, never in its runtime `[project] dependencies`.
clusters.trigger: A `types-*` package added to the runtime `dependencies` list of a provider `pyproject.toml`
clusters.rationale: Stubs are build-time artefacts; shipping them forces every runtime install to pull packages that do nothing at runtime.

clusters.rule: Initialise expensive provider clients and connections in a `@cached_property`, not eagerly in `Hook.__init__`.
clusters.trigger: A provider client, session or sub-hook constructed directly in `Hook.__init__`
clusters.rationale: Hooks are instantiated during DAG parsing and templating where no connection should be opened; the cached property defers the work to first real use.

clusters.rule: Provider logo and image assets must live under the `providers/` tree, not in a parallel top-level `registry/` folder.
clusters.trigger: Image or logo files added under `registry/` rather than `providers/<name>/`
clusters.rationale: Assets outside the provider directory are not part of the released provider distribution.

clusters.rule: Test whether a sentinel is unset with the `is_arg_set()` helper from `airflow.serialization.definitions.notset` rather than an inline `is NOTSET` comparison, and annotate the parameter with `ArgNotSet` in its type signature.
clusters.trigger: An `if value is NOTSET` check without `is_arg_set()` and without `ArgNotSet` in the parameter annotation
clusters.rationale: The helper and the annotation are what make the unset sentinel visible to type checking and serialization; inline identity checks silently diverge from it.

clusters.rule: Extract repeated `str | datetime | None` type-dispatch into a shared utility rather than duplicating the `isinstance` block per method.
clusters.trigger: The same `isinstance(value, (str, datetime.datetime))` dispatch block repeated in more than one method
clusters.rationale: Generic de-duplication advice with no repository-specific content.

clusters.rule: Pass the Alembic revision message as a single quoted string rather than `"${@}"` when generating migrations from a shell script.
clusters.trigger: `"${@}"` passed as the `-m` argument to `alembic revision --autogenerate`
clusters.rationale: A one-off quoting bug in a single container script.

clusters.rule: A behaviour change to a public provider hook method — different return shape, different filtering — must be recorded in that provider's `docs/changelog.rst` under the next release.
clusters.trigger: A diff altering the return value or filtering logic of an existing public hook method with no changelog entry
clusters.rationale: Users pin provider versions and read the changelog to decide whether an upgrade is safe; an unannounced behaviour change breaks their DAGs without warning.

clusters.rule: A process-wide singleton pool must not implement `__aenter__`/`__aexit__`; expose an explicit lifecycle hook instead of pretending to have a scoped lifetime.
clusters.trigger: `__aenter__`/`__aexit__` added to a class that registers itself in a module-level `_instances` dict
clusters.rationale: Context-manager syntax invites callers to close a resource shared by every other user of the singleton in the process.

clusters.rule: Put `AIRFLOW_V_x_y_PLUS` version gating for notifier behaviour in `BaseNotifier` rather than repeating the guard in each concrete notifier.
clusters.trigger: An `if AIRFLOW_V_x_y_PLUS:` guard added inside a concrete `Notifier.__init__` or `notify()`
clusters.rationale: Every notifier faces the same core-version difference, so a per-notifier guard guarantees some of them are eventually missed.

clusters.rule: Log the error response body before calling `response.raise_for_status()` against a provider API.
clusters.trigger: A `response.raise_for_status()` with no preceding log of the response body on 4xx/5xx
clusters.rationale: `raise_for_status` discards the body, which is where these vendor APIs put the actual reason for the rejection.

clusters.rule: Expose the timeout for a long-running provider API call as a constructor parameter on the operator/hook rather than fixing it in a module-level constant.
clusters.trigger: A module-level `*_TIMEOUT` constant gating an HTTP request to an ML/agent/query workload with no matching constructor parameter
clusters.rationale: How long these workloads take is deployment-specific; a module constant leaves users no way to adjust it short of patching the provider.

clusters.rule: In a deferrable operator, push the query/job identifier to XCom as soon as it is obtained, before entering the poll or defer, not after the wait completes.
clusters.trigger: An `xcom_push` for a query/job id placed after the polling loop in a deferrable operator's `execute`
clusters.rationale: If the task fails or is killed during the wait, the identifier is the only way to find and clean up the remote job — and it is lost if it was never pushed.

clusters.rule: Handle symbols that moved or were added across versions with `try/except ImportError` fallbacks — stdlib first, then the backport — rather than `if AIRFLOW_V_x_y_PLUS` version branches.
clusters.trigger: An `if AIRFLOW_V_x_y_PLUS: from airflow.sdk... else: from airflow.sensors...` import split, or a bare `from typing_extensions import NotRequired` with no stdlib guard
clusters.rationale: The import either works or it does not; testing for it directly stays correct across the whole supported version range without a table of version constants to maintain.

clusters.rule: Mutate an Airflow `ContextVar` with the token/reset pattern — capture the token from `.set()` and `.reset(token)` in a `finally` — following the precedent in `initdb()`.
clusters.trigger: A `ContextVar.set()` whose token is not stored and never `.reset()` in a `finally` block
clusters.rationale: Without the reset the variable leaks into whatever runs next on the same context, which in a scheduler or test process is unrelated work.

clusters.rule: Tests for SecretsMasker exception redaction must traverse the whole exception chain: attach a secret via `__cause__`/`__context__` and assert it is redacted, and include a cross-attribute cycle (`exc1.__cause__ = exc2; exc2.__context__ = exc1`) to prove the visited-set guard holds.
clusters.trigger: A redaction test that only inspects `exc.args`, or a circular-chain test that covers only same-attribute cycles
clusters.rationale: Secrets leak through chained exceptions as readily as through the primary one, and the cycle guard is exactly the code a same-attribute-only test cannot exercise.

clusters.rule: Task SDK documentation examples showing an async `@task` function must include the enclosing `@dag`-decorated wrapper so the snippet is a runnable DAG file.
clusters.trigger: An `.rst`/`.md` example defining an `@task` function and calling it at module level with no `@dag` function around it
clusters.rationale: Users copy these snippets verbatim; a fragment that calls a task at module level does not parse as a DAG.

clusters.rule: The `check_provide_session_kwargs` hook tests must cover the bypass path where an allowlist entry is removed or newly added, not only where an existing entry's count is loosened.
clusters.trigger: Tests for `_expand_for_allowlist_edits` exercising only the increased-count case
clusters.rationale: A specific coverage gap identified in one PR's tests.

clusters.rule: Pre-commit hook tests must pass `Path.resolve()`d paths so they match the production hook's path normalisation.
clusters.trigger: A hook test passing a raw path where the production code calls `Path(f).resolve()` before comparing
clusters.rationale: A specific mismatch corrected in one PR's tests.

clusters.rule: A shared metrics registry must key every instrument type the same way, or keep separate sub-maps per instrument type, so gauges and histograms cannot collide in one slot.
clusters.trigger: A `MetricsMap`-style registry keying one instrument type by name alone and another by name plus tags, or storing all instrument types in one dict
clusters.rationale: Mixed key schemes in one dict let a gauge silently overwrite a histogram registered under the same name.

clusters.rule: When a class reads an Airflow config value to supply an argument default, add a regression test that changes that config key before constructing the object and asserts the default is picked up.
clusters.trigger: An `__init__` reading `conf.get*` for a default with no test that constructs the class after modifying that section/key
clusters.rationale: Config-driven defaults are easy to wire to the wrong section or key, and nothing else in the test suite exercises that lookup.

clusters.rule: Insert new entries into `airflow/sdk/__init__.py`'s `__all__` and lazy-import dict in alphabetical position, not appended at the end.
clusters.trigger: A symbol added to `__all__` or the lazy-import dict in `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/__init__.py` out of alphabetical order
clusters.rationale: The alphabetical ordering is what keeps this heavily-edited public export list reviewable and merge-conflict-free.

clusters.rule: In the Java coordinator, register the stdout/stderr socketpair pipe readers before starting the connection accept loop.
clusters.trigger: `_accept_connections` called before `_register_pipe_readers` on the socketpair write-ends handed to the subprocess
clusters.rationale: A specific ordering defect in one coordinator implementation.

clusters.rule: A language coordinator's constructor arguments need only make sense for its own runtime; do not copy another coordinator's argument names or types for the sake of symmetry.
clusters.trigger: A coordinator given argument names or types mirroring a different language's coordinator rather than idiomatic ones for its runtime
clusters.rationale: These coordinators are configured independently per language, so forced signature symmetry buys nothing and produces arguments that read wrongly in context.

clusters.rule: In Task SDK coordinator modules, log caught exceptions with `exc_info=True` as a structlog keyword rather than `error=str(exc)`.
clusters.trigger: `log.debug(..., error=str(exc))` or `log.warning(..., error=str(exc))` under `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/coordinators/`
clusters.rationale: Stringifying the exception throws away the traceback, which is the only thing that makes these subprocess failures debuggable.

clusters.rule: Do not define a `__version__` attribute inside `airflow.sdk.coordinators.*` sub-packages; the distribution version is exposed only as `airflow.sdk.__version__`.
clusters.trigger: A `__version__ = "..."` assignment or `"__version__"` in `__all__` under `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/coordinators/*/`
clusters.rationale: Per-subpackage versions imply independent release cadences that do not exist and drift from the real distribution version.

clusters.rule: Wrap every datetime placed into a callback context dict with `coerce_datetime` from `airflow.sdk._shared.timezones`, matching `RuntimeTaskInstance.get_template_context()` and the triggerer-side context builder.
clusters.trigger: A context dict in `callback_supervisor.py` populated with datetime fields from `DagRunResult` or similar without `coerce_datetime()`
clusters.rationale: Template code and user callbacks expect `pendulum.DateTime` throughout the context; a raw datetime breaks the pendulum-only methods users call on it.

clusters.rule: When renaming a message class in `task-sdk/.../execution_time/comms.py`, update the hardcoded message-type allowlists in `airflow-core/tests/unit/dag_processing/test_processor.py` and `airflow-core/tests/unit/jobs/test_triggerer_job.py` in the same PR.
clusters.trigger: A renamed `ToTask`/`ToSupervisor` message class with no corresponding edit to the allowlists in those two core test files
clusters.rationale: Those allowlists are the sync check between SDK and core message types; leaving them stale breaks the core test suite for an SDK-only change.

clusters.rule: Accumulate partition keys for a task instance in a set rather than a list, matching how asset aliases deduplicate repeated keys.
clusters.trigger: A `attrs.field(factory=list)` partition-keys field on a task-instance context object appended to without deduplication
clusters.rationale: Repeated keys are expected during a run, and the downstream consumers treat them as a set anyway.

clusters.rule: In Asset lookup code, treat `Asset(uri=...)` as having `name == uri` — the DB storage convention — instead of adding `name is None` branches as a distinct state.
clusters.trigger: None-guarded name/uri paths added to Asset or AssetRef handling in `task-sdk/.../execution_time/context.py` without normalising an absent name to the uri
clusters.rationale: The database never stores a null asset name, so a `None`-name branch is unreachable state that diverges from what lookups actually match against.

clusters.rule: A concrete Task SDK class exported from the public API must implement every abstract method of its base (including `to_upstream()` on partition mappers); leave it abstract or unexported until it does.
clusters.trigger: A concrete mapper under `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/definitions/partition_mappers/` inheriting `RollupMapper` without overriding `to_upstream()`
clusters.rationale: Anything exported from `airflow.sdk` is a supported API users will instantiate; a partially implemented class fails at DAG runtime instead of at import.

clusters.rule: When a Task SDK API method queries only the metadata database and deliberately skips secrets backends (e.g. `Variable.keys()` versus `Variable.get()`), document the asymmetry and its reason in a `.. note::` block in the docstring.
clusters.trigger: A new listing method in `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/definitions/variable.py` with no note about secrets-backend exclusion
clusters.rationale: Users reasonably assume the whole Variable API consults the configured secrets backend; the silent exception produces confusing partial results.

clusters.rule: `supervise_callback` must call `_make_process_nondumpable()` before spawning its subprocess, exactly as `supervise_task` does.
clusters.trigger: A `supervise_callback` in `callback_supervisor.py` that spawns a subprocess without `_make_process_nondumpable()`
clusters.rationale: Callback processes hold notifier tokens and connection passwords in memory; without the dumpable flag cleared a core dump writes them to disk.

clusters.rule: Pass `context` to a callback callable only when `accepts_context` is true and the context value is not `None`; never forward `context=None`.
clusters.trigger: `**callback_kwargs` forwarded unconditionally when `accepts_context()` is true, without checking the context is not None
clusters.rationale: User callbacks that declare a context parameter assume it is populated; handing them `None` fails inside third-party code rather than at the call site.

clusters.rule: Exception log calls in `callback_supervisor.py` must carry structured identifying fields (`callback_id=`, `pid=`), mirroring the `ActivitySubprocess` pattern in `supervisor.py`.
clusters.trigger: A `log.exception(...)`/`log.error(...)` in `callback_supervisor.py` without `callback_id` or `pid` keywords
clusters.rationale: Callbacks run concurrently, so an unlabelled traceback cannot be attributed to the callback that failed.

clusters.rule: Size-limit warnings and API error messages in task-SDK execution code must name the worker-side `[workers] state_store_backend` option as the remedy, using the same section name in the asset-store warning and the API errors.
clusters.trigger: A size-limit warning or HTTP error in task-sdk execution code naming a `[state_store] backend` option
clusters.rationale: A specific wrong-config-section fix in one PR's message text.

clusters.rule: When instantiating a user-configured class from a config classpath (`import_string(spec.classpath)(**spec.kwargs)`), catch `ImportError`/`TypeError` and re-raise naming the offending key and classpath, and assert the result `isinstance` of the expected base class before caching it.
clusters.trigger: An `import_string(<spec>.classpath)(**<spec>.kwargs)` for a config-driven plugin or coordinator with no error wrapping and no base-class check
clusters.rationale: The raw exception names none of the user's configuration, leaving a misconfigured deployment with a traceback that does not identify the offending entry.

clusters.rule: When client-level exception translation replaces an existing error path, keep end-to-end coverage at the supervisor level: replace the removed `test_supervisor.py` test with one asserting the new exception propagates from `ActivitySubprocess.start()`/`supervise` and the child process is killed.
clusters.trigger: A diff deleting a test from `task-sdk/tests/task_sdk/execution_time/test_supervisor.py` while adding the equivalent coverage only in `tests/task_sdk/api/test_client.py`
clusters.rationale: The client-level test proves the translation happens; only the supervisor test proves the supervisor reacts to it and reaps the child.

clusters.rule: Tests that keep a task subprocess alive to exercise signal delivery must bound their worst case to tens of seconds; do not write operator bodies like `for i in range(1000): sleep(1)`.
clusters.trigger: A test operator whose `execute` sleeps in a loop with a worst-case total well beyond a minute
clusters.rationale: If the signal under test fails to arrive, the unbounded sleep becomes the CI job's timeout rather than a fast, legible test failure.

clusters.rule: Use `partition_key` only for exact-match asset-event filtering; any regex or pattern value must go through `partition_key_pattern`, in tests as well as production code.
clusters.trigger: `partition_key=` set to a value containing regex metacharacters in a `GetAssetEventByAsset` message or asset-event query
clusters.rationale: The exact-match field is compared literally, so a pattern passed there matches nothing while looking like it should work.

clusters.rule: A regression test for a new `sys.exit(...)` inside `run()` must assert more than `SystemExit(1)`: it must also verify `on_failure_callback`, the `on_task_instance_failed` listener and `email_on_failure` still fire for the failed task instance.
clusters.trigger: A task-runner test asserting only `pytest.raises(SystemExit)` or an exit code for a failure path introduced by a new `sys.exit()`
clusters.rationale: An early exit is exactly the change that can skip the failure-notification machinery, and an exit-code assertion cannot see that.

clusters.rule: New language-SDK task registration APIs should follow the two-step registration the Java and Go SDKs use — define the callable, then register the task against a Dag — so Dag-level arguments remain expressible; an inline `registerTask({dagId, taskId}, fn)` must be justified against that path.
clusters.trigger: A task registration entrypoint added or documented under `ts-sdk/` that binds dagId and taskId inline in one call
clusters.rationale: Whole-Dag definition in the language SDKs is planned; an API that binds the Dag identity into the task call has nowhere to put Dag-level arguments when it lands.

clusters.rule: Every `Socket` created by the ts-sdk coordinator must register an `error` handler at construction that writes the channel name and message to stderr.
clusters.trigger: A `Socket` constructed or stored under `ts-sdk/src/coordinator/` wiring only `data`/`close`/`connect` handlers
clusters.rationale: An unhandled socket `error` event terminates the Node task process outright, losing the task with no diagnostic.

clusters.rule: Client-side socket reconnection in a language SDK is only correct if the Airflow coordinator accepts a second connection on the same channel; when adding `scheduleReconnect`/backoff logic, verify and cover the coordinator-side re-accept path in the same PR.
clusters.trigger: Reconnect or backoff logic added to a ts-sdk coordinator socket, e.g. `sock.on("close", ...)` calling `this.scheduleReconnect()`
clusters.rationale: Reconnect logic against a coordinator that never re-accepts turns a single dropped connection into an infinite retry loop that looks healthy from the client side.

clusters.rule: A secrets backend cannot enforce a denial by raising alone: the backend-iteration loops (`_get_connection`, `_async_get_connection`, `_get_variable` in `execution_time/context.py` and the same pattern in `models/connection.py`) swallow every exception with `except Exception: continue`, so a new deny signal must be special-cased and re-raised there in the same change.
clusters.trigger: A secrets backend made to raise `PermissionError` or another auth-denied exception without changing the backend-fallthrough loops to re-raise it
clusters.rationale: Otherwise the deny is swallowed and lookup falls through to the next backend, turning an intended refusal into a silent bypass.

clusters.rule: A tracing helper that no-ops below a configured OTel detail level must return `contextlib.nullcontext(trace.INVALID_SPAN)`, not `trace.INVALID_SPAN` itself, so `with detail_span(...) as span` still works and yields `INVALID_SPAN`.
clusters.trigger: A span wrapper whose disabled branch returns `trace.INVALID_SPAN` while `__enter__` calls `self._ctx.__enter__()`
clusters.rationale: Returning the span directly removes `__enter__`/`__exit__`, so every call site raises as soon as the detail level is lowered — the configuration that was supposed to be the safe one.

clusters.rule: A comment or docstring that tells the reader to run a benchmark or helper script must name an entrypoint that exists in the tree (e.g. under `dev/`); otherwise add the script in the same PR or drop the instruction.
clusters.trigger: A comment or docstring pointing at a `dev/...` script or other repo entrypoint that is not present in the repository
clusters.rationale: An instruction naming a file nobody can find wastes the next reader's time and cannot be distinguished from a rename that was missed.

clusters.rule: Hand-written lists inside `.github/` that mirror repository state (the provider inventory in issue templates, locale/namespace inventories in agent SKILL.md files) must be generated or validated by a prek/pre-commit hook rather than maintained by hand
clusters.trigger: A PR adds a manually enumerated list of providers, locales, or i18n namespaces to `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml` or `.github/skills/**/SKILL.md` without a corresponding hook entry in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`
clusters.rationale: Airflow's provider and locale inventories change constantly; a hand-maintained mirror of them in repo metadata silently rots, so reviewers insist the list be derived mechanically and enforced in CI.

clusters.rule: A new pre-commit hook's `files:` pattern must be narrowed to exactly the distributions and subpackages the rule applies to; never a bare `\.py$` or a whole-distribution glob
clusters.trigger: A new `- id:` block in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` uses `files: \.py$` or a broad `^providers/<dist>/(src|tests)/.*\.py$` for a check that only holds in part of that tree
clusters.rationale: Over-broad hook scopes fire on unrelated distributions in a monorepo of this size, producing false failures that contributors learn to ignore.

clusters.rule: In GitHub Actions steps do not `source .venv/bin/activate` after `uv venv`; uv commands pick up the project virtualenv on their own
clusters.trigger: A workflow `run:` block contains `uv venv` followed by `source .venv/bin/activate` before `uv pip install`
clusters.rationale: uv already resolves the project virtualenv, so the activation line is dead weight that suggests the author does not know how the tool works and diverges from the rest of the workflows.

clusters.rule: When dropping a `needs:` gate to parallelise a release workflow, split the publish/sync steps into a job that still `needs:` the gating job instead of discarding the ordering guarantee outright
clusters.trigger: A job in a release workflow has its `needs:` replaced (e.g. `needs: [publish-docs-to-s3, build-info]` becomes `needs: [build-info, build-ci-image]`) while it still contains sync or publish steps that must not land before the gating job
clusters.rationale: Reviewers wanted the parallelism without losing the publish ordering, but the fix is specific to this one workflow restructure rather than a standing expectation.

clusters.rule: The version dropdown in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/1-airflow_bug_report.yml` must list only currently released, non-yanked versions; a yanked release is rolled back until `main` is bumped to its replacement
clusters.trigger: A PR adds or leaves a version string in the bug report template's `options:` list for a release that has been yanked or not yet cut
clusters.rationale: Offering a yanked or unreleased version invites bug reports against artifacts nobody can install, which triagers then have to unpick.

clusters.rule: Adding a new UI translation locale requires an identified, dev-list-confirmed owner recorded in `.github/CODEOWNERS` and a locale guideline file at `.github/skills/airflow-translations/locales/<code>.md`
clusters.trigger: A PR adds a new `airflow-core/src/airflow/ui/public/i18n/locales/<code>/` directory or CODEOWNERS entry without a dev@airflow.apache.org thread establishing owners and without the matching locale guideline file
clusters.rationale: An unowned locale decays into stale half-translated UI that nobody in the community can review; the project makes ownership a merge precondition rather than a follow-up.

clusters.rule: Do not add hand-written documentation pages that enumerate REST API endpoints or their schemas; the auto-generated `stable-rest-api-ref` page already publishes them
clusters.trigger: A new `.rst` file under `airflow-core/docs/` documents an API surface (endpoints, request/response shapes) that is already generated from the OpenAPI spec
clusters.rationale: A second, hand-written copy of the API surface drifts from the spec and misleads users; the generated reference is the single source of truth.

clusters.rule: A new provider-governance policy section in `PROVIDERS.rst` must state its applicability to already-existing providers - either that it applies only to providers created after the governing AIP's approval date, or how existing providers are transitioned
clusters.trigger: A PR adds a governance section (stewardship, lifecycle, ownership requirements) to `PROVIDERS.rst` stating requirements without scoping them to new versus existing providers
clusters.rationale: Airflow ships dozens of pre-existing providers; a governance rule with no applicability clause reads as retroactively invalidating most of them.

clusters.rule: Documentation of provider attic status must spell out the CI and maintenance consequences: not actively tested in `main`, dependencies not checked for conflicts with other providers, common refactorings not applied, and significant effort required to restore the provider
clusters.trigger: A PR describes provider lifecycle or attic status listing only that modules stay readable and unmaintained, without the CI, dependency-conflict and refactoring consequences
clusters.rationale: Reviewers were completing the content of one specific governance document rather than stating an expectation future contributors could violate elsewhere.

clusters.rule: Treat `providers/edge3/.../worker_api/` and `.../plugins/` as the server side and `.../cli/` as the client side: server-only imports such as FastAPI, and checks that assume server context, must not reach the `cli` subtree
clusters.trigger: A path-scoped check, import rule, or FastAPI/server-side import applies to all of `providers/edge3/` rather than excluding `providers/edge3/src/airflow/providers/edge3/cli/`
clusters.rationale: The edge worker CLI runs on machines that do not install the server stack, so leaking server-only imports into it breaks the deployment model the provider exists to support.

clusters.rule: Classify a change to the serialized structure of triggerer context data as a breaking provider change, alongside behaviour changes in `execute()`/`poke()`/`get_conn()` and xcom/connection/asset schema changes
clusters.trigger: A provider PR alters the fields or shape of data a Trigger serializes into triggerer context, and the changelog or documentation classifies it as a feature or bugfix rather than breaking
clusters.rationale: Triggers deserialize state written by an older release while in flight, so a shape change breaks running deployments exactly as a signature change would.

clusters.rule: Locale guideline files under `.github/skills/airflow-translations/locales/` must use the same heading format as the existing ones - the language name plus the locale code only, e.g. `# Thai (th)`
clusters.trigger: A new `locales/<code>.md` file opens with a descriptive heading such as `# Thai (th) Translation Guidelines for Apache Airflow` instead of `# Thai (th)`
clusters.rationale: These files are consumed as a set by the translation skill; a uniform heading keeps them machine- and reviewer-legible.

clusters.rule: A locale guideline file adapted from another locale's document must carry over every glossary term from the source, including deliberately untranslated ones such as `Dag ID`
clusters.trigger: A new or updated `locales/<code>.md` glossary omits terms that the locale document it was derived from lists
clusters.rationale: The glossary is what keeps terminology consistent across locales; silently dropping entries when copying a template reintroduces the divergence the glossary exists to prevent.

clusters.rule: Every provider extra added to the root `pyproject.toml` must pin a minimum provider version (`apache-airflow-providers-<name>>=X.Y.Z`), matching the surrounding extras
clusters.trigger: A new entry is added to the extras tables in `pyproject.toml` as a bare `"apache-airflow-providers-foo"` with no version specifier while neighbouring extras carry `>=` bounds
clusters.rationale: Unpinned extras let resolvers pick a provider release predating the feature the extra exists for, producing import errors that look like Airflow bugs.

clusters.rule: When docs enumerate a feature's parameters, each bullet must name the exact keyword argument in double backticks (``reference``, ``interval``, ``callback``) and the stated mandatory/optional counts must match the real signature
clusters.trigger: A docs page lists parameters as capitalised prose words (`Reference:`, `Interval:`, `Callback Kwargs:`) or claims a number of mandatory parameters that disagrees with the constructor signature
clusters.rationale: Readers copy parameter names straight out of the docs; prose-cased labels and a wrong mandatory count send them to a TypeError.

clusters.rule: Security-model guidance that narrows credential distribution must keep connection credentials available to the Dag processor and triggerer; only the JWT signing key is withheld from components that neither generate nor validate tokens (workers)
clusters.trigger: `security_model.rst` or deployment guidance adds advice that connection credentials should be available only to the API server, without carving out the Dag processor and triggerer
clusters.rationale: The Dag processor and triggerer genuinely need connections to do their jobs; hardening advice that ignores that would break every deployment that followed it.

clusters.rule: A `.feature.rst` newsfragment must state what the new API does for users, not the internal defect it fixes
clusters.trigger: A newsfragment sentence is phrased as "... to fix <internal component/behaviour>" instead of describing the capability the change adds
clusters.rationale: Newsfragments become the release notes users read; an internal-defect framing tells them nothing about what they can now do.

clusters.rule: A `.significant.rst` newsfragment that ticks the Behaviour-change or Code-interface-change checkbox must spell out the delta in prose: "Previously it worked as X, now it works as Y" / "Previously the interface was X, now it is Y"
clusters.trigger: A `.significant.rst` file marks `[x] Behaviour changes` or `[x] Code interface changes` but contains no before/after explanation of what changed
clusters.rationale: The significant newsfragments are the upgrade guide; a ticked checkbox with no before/after leaves operators unable to tell whether the change affects them.

clusters.rule: A significant newsfragment describing an observability or process-management change must add the operator-visible impact and migration step (dashboards built on the old Gauge must move to Histogram aggregations; how to roll-restart the api-server on Kubernetes)
clusters.trigger: A `.significant.rst` describes an internal representation or process change (metric instrument type, uvicorn worker/restart model) without saying what existing deployments must do about it
clusters.rationale: Internal descriptions of metric or process changes are useless to an operator whose dashboards or restart procedure just broke; the fragment must name the action they have to take.

clusters.rule: Partition mapper classes must be named `To<Granularity>Mapper` (`ToHourlyMapper`, `ToDailyMapper`, `ToWeeklyMapper`, `ToMonthlyMapper`, `ToQuarterlyMapper`), not the bare granularity name
clusters.trigger: A new partition mapper class, or documentation of one, uses a bare granularity name such as `HourlyMapper` or `DailyMapper`
clusters.rationale: The `To<Granularity>` form says which direction the mapping runs, which a bare granularity name leaves ambiguous.

clusters.rule: Profiling and other developer-only libraries (e.g. `memray`) must be declared as an optional extra in `airflow-core/pyproject.toml`, never appended to the mandatory `dependencies` list
clusters.trigger: A diff adds an entry to the top-level `dependencies = [...]` array in `airflow-core/pyproject.toml` for a tool that only some users need
clusters.rationale: Every mandatory dependency is installed by every Airflow user and constrains the resolver for all of them; debugging tooling does not earn that cost.

clusters.rule: Cross-team asset-event triggering must ship with the most restrictive default (a teamless API user may trigger only teamless consumers) and the restriction must be documented with the reasoning behind it
clusters.trigger: Multi-team documentation or code defines which producers may trigger which consumers across team boundaries, and either proposes a permissive default or states a rule with no explanation
clusters.rationale: Multi-team exists to isolate teams; a permissive default silently hands one team the ability to trigger another's workloads, and an unexplained rule cannot be reasoned about later.

clusters.rule: In `multi-team.rst`, feature-specific sections belong above the concluding multi-team architecture diagram, which is meant to end the page
clusters.trigger: A new section is appended after the `multi_team_arch_diagram.png` image block in `airflow-core/docs/core-concepts/multi-team.rst`
clusters.rationale: The diagram is the page's summary; content appended after it reads as an afterthought and breaks the intended narrative order.

clusters.rule: Architecture docs must say the scheduler reads serialized Dags from the metadata database and needs no direct Dag bundle access, and must not assert that another component (e.g. the triggerer) accesses bundles directly without verifying it
clusters.trigger: A docs diff enumerates which Airflow components require access to Dag bundles or Dag files
clusters.rationale: Which components need bundle access drives real deployment decisions (volume mounts, git sync placement); getting it wrong in the overview misconfigures clusters.

clusters.rule: `curl` examples in the docs must percent-encode reserved characters in the query string (`%7C` for `|`, `%5E` for `^`) or use `curl --data-urlencode`, so the example runs when copied verbatim
clusters.trigger: A `.. code-block:: bash` block adds a curl invocation whose URL query string contains a raw `|`, `^`, or other RFC 3986 reserved character
clusters.rationale: Doc examples are copy-pasted; an unescaped pipe is eaten by the shell and the user gets a confusing failure that looks like an API bug.

clusters.rule: A language-SDK docs page that documents log forwarding must also document the configuration the SDK already reads for it - for the Java SDK, `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__LOGGING_LEVEL` and `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__NAMESPACE_LEVELS`
clusters.trigger: A new Logging section under `airflow-core/docs/authoring-and-scheduling/language-sdks/` lists the integration artifacts but has no subsection on setting log levels
clusters.rationale: The SDK already honours these variables; omitting them leaves users unable to control log volume from a feature the page claims to document.

clusters.rule: A new row in `extra-packages-ref.rst` must describe exactly the component types the provider ships (hooks, triggers, queue providers, operators); do not write "hooks and operators" for a provider that defines no operators
clusters.trigger: A diff adds a row to the extras table in `airflow-core/docs/extra-packages-ref.rst` whose description does not match the components actually defined in the corresponding provider package
clusters.rationale: This table is how users decide which extra to install; promising operators that do not exist sends them down a dead end.

clusters.rule: A PR's title and description must describe the scope actually present in the diff; a documentation/CI/repo-metadata-only change must not be titled as a CLI or behaviour fix
clusters.trigger: PR title or description claims a code/CLI behaviour change but the diff touches only docs, CI configuration, or repo metadata
clusters.rationale: Reviewers asked for an accurate title, but this is generic PR hygiene rather than a repo-specific expectation that could be encoded as an Airflow convention.

clusters.rule: `AsyncCallback` must wrap something that is actually awaitable; synchronous notifiers such as `SlackWebhookNotifier` expose no awaitables and must not appear inside `AsyncCallback` in deadline-alert examples or Dag code
clusters.trigger: `AsyncCallback(` is constructed with a notifier or callable that defines no async interface, in docs examples or in deadline configuration
clusters.rationale: The deadline-alert docs are the pattern users copy; showing a sync notifier inside AsyncCallback teaches a construction that cannot work.

clusters.rule: Do not describe the Execution API as an "internal" API; describe it as an API for use by Airflow itself rather than third-party callers, because it is deliberately reachable from outside the deployment
clusters.trigger: Security or API documentation introduces the Execution API with the word "internal", or implies it is not exposed outside the deployment boundary
clusters.rationale: Calling it internal invites operators to assume network isolation they do not have, which is a security-relevant misreading of the Airflow 3 architecture.

clusters.rule: The UI authentication JWT must be stored in a secure, HTTP-only `_token` cookie with `SameSite=Lax`, never in browser local storage or local settings
clusters.trigger: Auth-manager or UI code, or documentation of it, stores or describes storing the `access_token` anywhere other than the secure HTTP-only cookie
clusters.rationale: A token reachable from JavaScript is an XSS-exfiltratable credential; the HTTP-only cookie is the deliberate design and documentation must not contradict it.

clusters.rule: Execution API JWTs are minted by the scheduler via the executor's `jwt_generator` property while the workload is built; `executor.queue_workload()` must not generate tokens, it forwards whatever workload it is given
clusters.trigger: An executor implementation creates or refreshes a task JWT inside `queue_workload()` (or elsewhere in the executor) instead of consuming the token already present on the workload
clusters.rationale: Keeping minting in one place at workload construction keeps the signing key out of executor code paths and keeps token lifetime tied to the workload it authorises.

clusters.rule: Connection-listing methods in auth managers must account for all connection sources (env vars, secrets backends, etc.), not only the database; a DB-only query must be documented as returning a partial list
clusters.trigger: New method on BaseAuthManager queries Connection table without considering non-DB connection sources
clusters.rationale: Connections in Airflow come from several backends; a DB-only listing silently under-reports and callers will treat the result as complete.

clusters.rule: Any new public method added to BaseAuthManager that introduces user-facing behaviour must be accompanied by a newsfragment and a defined default behaviour for auth managers that do not override it
clusters.trigger: New method added to BaseAuthManager (or subclass) without a newsfragment file and without a documented/implemented default fallback
clusters.rationale: BaseAuthManager is a public extension point implemented outside the repo; adding an abstract-ish method with no default breaks third-party auth managers on upgrade.

clusters.rule: Do not shorten ILIKE performance-warning descriptions in filter_param_factory docstrings; the explicit version explaining that `ILIKE '%term%'` prevents B-tree indexes and that prefix_pattern is preferred is required to guide operators on large tables
clusters.trigger: Performance note in filter_param_factory description shortened or replaced with an abbreviated form that omits the ILIKE expansion and index guidance
clusters.rationale: This was a reviewer restoring wording that a specific PR had trimmed, not a standing expectation new code could violate.

clusters.rule: The API representation of infinite pool slots must use -1, not None; JSON cannot represent float('inf') and None conflicts with the existing API spec for open slots
clusters.trigger: Serialiser or Pydantic validator converts float('inf') pool slots to None before returning an API response
clusters.rationale: The public API already assigns a meaning to None for open slots, so reusing it for infinity makes two different states indistinguishable to clients.

clusters.rule: All exception types that a service function can raise must be caught at the route level; when a dry-run variant catches an exception (e.g. DagRunTypeNotAllowed) the non-dry-run counterpart must catch it too
clusters.trigger: except tuple in a route handler is missing an exception type that the called service function is documented to raise, while a sibling route (e.g. dry-run) already handles it
clusters.rationale: An uncaught domain exception surfaces as a 500 for what is really a client error, and the dry-run/real pair diverging means the dry run lies about what the real call will do.

clusters.rule: Do not duplicate a DB lookup at the route level when the same lookup already occurs inside the service function; raise a domain exception from the service and catch-and-convert it at the route level instead
clusters.trigger: Route handler calls session.scalar/session.get for a model that the downstream service function already queries for the same purpose
clusters.rationale: The duplicate query costs a round trip and opens a window where the two lookups disagree; the service layer is where the lookup belongs.

clusters.rule: Broad AirflowException catches at route boundaries must not forward arbitrary internal error messages as 4xx detail strings; narrow the catch to user-facing exceptions or validate the message before re-raising
clusters.trigger: except AirflowException as e: raise HTTPException(4xx, str(e)) without narrowing the caught exception type or filtering the message
clusters.rationale: AirflowException is a very wide base class, so this pattern leaks internal detail to API clients and labels genuine server faults as client errors.

clusters.rule: Authorization checks must short-circuit the query path entirely; do not pass an empty list to XComModel.get_many (or equivalent) as a proxy for 'no results' when the user is unauthorized
clusters.trigger: result_task_ids = [] or equivalent empty-collection sentinel used to suppress results after a failed authorization check, instead of returning early before the query
clusters.rationale: Relying on an empty filter to produce no rows makes the security outcome depend on query semantics; one change to the helper's handling of empty input turns a denial into a full disclosure.

clusters.rule: Aggregate statistics over DagRun history (durations, averages) must not be computed by fetching unbounded result sets; pre-compute them incrementally or use windowed queries, and confirm migration safety before adding new computed columns
clusters.trigger: select() over DagRun with no row limit used to compute aggregate statistics (avg duration, p90, etc.) in a route handler
clusters.rationale: DagRun is one of the largest tables in a real deployment; loading its history into Python per request will not survive contact with production.

clusters.rule: Bulk DAG updates must use a single subquery-based UPDATE (DagModel.dag_id.in_(subquery)) rather than paginated SELECT loops that issue one DB query per page
clusters.trigger: paginated_select or offset/limit loop used to fetch DAG IDs before issuing individual UPDATE statements in a bulk-patch route
clusters.rationale: A bulk endpoint that fans out into per-page queries defeats the purpose of being bulk and holds the transaction open far longer than necessary.

clusters.rule: Response models must not include fields already available through a separately fetched resource on the same page; check existing endpoint payloads before adding redundant fields to a datamodel
clusters.trigger: Field added to a Grid/collection response datamodel (e.g. GridRunsResponse) that duplicates data already returned by a companion detail endpoint called by the same UI view
clusters.rationale: Grid payloads are large and fetched constantly; duplicating a field the UI already has inflates every response and creates two sources of truth that can disagree.

clusters.rule: Do not use runtime `inspect` introspection to discover whether a callable accepts a parameter and pass arguments conditionally; make the parameter-presence decision on the caller side, or fix the caller/test to pass the expected arguments directly
clusters.trigger: inspect.signature() / inspect.Parameter / `'param' in params` used inside BaseAuthManager or a test to decide whether to pass a keyword argument to an override such as an auth-manager method or clear_task_instances
clusters.rationale: Signature sniffing hides an interface mismatch instead of resolving it, and it silently changes behaviour depending on which version of a subclass or helper happens to be installed.

clusters.rule: Config values read inside hot paths (called once per task during scheduling) must be cached at construction time, not re-read on every call
clusters.trigger: conf.get* called inside a method that is invoked per-task or per-DAG-run in the scheduler loop rather than once at object construction
clusters.rationale: conf lookups are not free and the scheduler calls these paths thousands of times per loop; the value cannot change mid-process anyway.

clusters.rule: Database error handlers in the FastAPI exception layer must follow the existing per-dialect pattern; do not add new string-sniffing markers for individual error sub-types without matching the established dialect-aware structure
clusters.trigger: New tuple of string markers (e.g. _TOO_LARGE_MARKERS) added to an exception handler in api_fastapi/common/exceptions.py without dialect-specific branching
clusters.rationale: Airflow supports several database backends whose error text differs; ad-hoc substring matching works on the author's backend and silently fails on the others.

clusters.rule: DataError exception messages surfaced to API clients must be generic enough to cover all possible DataError sub-cases, not worded as if only one specific cause (e.g. text-size overflow) can trigger them
clusters.trigger: HTTPException detail string inside a DataError handler mentions a specific column type (MEDIUMTEXT, LONGTEXT) or a single error cause
clusters.rationale: A handler that catches a whole exception class but names one cause misdiagnoses every other case for the user.

clusters.rule: When exposing SQL statement details via conf expose_stacktrace, retrieve sensitive fields (statement, orig) only after the guard check, not before; default them to None rather than a placeholder string
clusters.trigger: getattr(exc, 'statement', ...) or getattr(exc, 'orig', ...) assigned before the expose_stacktrace config check inside an exception handler
clusters.rationale: Reading the sensitive value before the guard makes it one refactor away from leaking, and a placeholder string is indistinguishable from real content downstream.

clusters.rule: SQLAlchemy JSON column type checks must use isinstance(col.type, JSON) for cross-dialect compatibility; do not add a string-comparison fallback (str(col.type).upper() in ('JSON','JSONB')) unless you can confirm isinstance fails for a specific dialect
clusters.trigger: str(self.attribute.type).upper() in ('JSON', 'JSONB') used alongside isinstance(self.attribute.type, JSON) in a filter parameter
clusters.rationale: A speculative string fallback added "just in case" is untested code that hides the real dialect problem if one ever exists.

clusters.rule: Task-group filters on list endpoints must use exact group-id matching, not pattern/prefix matching, to avoid returning TaskInstances from unrelated groups
clusters.trigger: TaskInstance list filter applies pattern matching (LIKE / regex) against task_group display_name or group_id
clusters.rationale: Group ids share prefixes in real Dags, so prefix matching quietly returns instances the caller did not ask for.

clusters.rule: Single-value filter parameters on list endpoints should accept multiple values (list[str] with FilterOptionEnum.ANY_EQUAL) so callers can request several items in one request instead of needing a dedicated GET /{id} endpoint
clusters.trigger: filter_param_factory used with a scalar type (str | None) for a unique-key field (e.g. uri, conn_id) on a list endpoint that could naturally accept multiple values
clusters.rationale: The UI and clients routinely need several records at once; a scalar filter forces N requests where the list-endpoint machinery already supports one.

clusters.rule: DagModel subqueries that filter by file location must also include bundle_name to correctly scope results across bundles
clusters.trigger: select(DagModel.relative_fileloc).distinct().subquery() without bundle_name column
clusters.rationale: relative_fileloc is only unique within a bundle, so a fileloc-only filter matches Dags from other bundles that happen to share a path.

clusters.rule: Execution-API JWT data models should expose only the scope field needed at the application layer; JWT validation fields (exp, aud, iss, nbf, iat) belong in the upstream JWTValidator, not in the application-level token model
clusters.trigger: Pydantic model for an execution-API token including JWT standard claims (exp, aud, iss, nbf, iat) alongside application-level fields like scope
clusters.rationale: Duplicating claims into the application model implies the application validates them, when validation has already happened upstream - an invitation to check them twice, or worse, only there.

clusters.rule: Regex-based query parameters in the execution API must use a _pattern suffix to match the public REST API naming convention
clusters.trigger: Annotated[str | None, Query(description='... pattern ...')] parameter whose name does not end in _pattern
clusters.rationale: The public REST API already signals pattern-matching parameters by suffix; diverging in the execution API makes the two surfaces read as unrelated products.

clusters.rule: AssetEvent.extra filtering in execution-API routes must use _parse_extra_params() and JsonContains() rather than ad-hoc string splitting on '='
clusters.trigger: for item in extra: if '=' in item: k, v = item.split('=', 1) pattern applied to AssetEvent.extra
clusters.rationale: The shared helper handles typing and dialect-portable JSON containment; hand-rolled splitting mishandles values containing '=' and produces backend-specific SQL.

clusters.rule: Execution-API asset resolvers must filter by AssetModel.active.has() when resolving an asset by name, to prevent workers from reading or writing state against removed assets
clusters.trigger: select(AssetModel.id).where(AssetModel.name == name) inside an execution-API route without .where(AssetModel.active.has())
clusters.rationale: Removed assets stay in the table; without the active filter a task can resurrect state on an asset the deployment has retired.

clusters.rule: OpenAPI HTTP exception description strings within the same route file must consistently either all end with a period or none do
clusters.trigger: create_openapi_http_exception_doc([...]) call where some description strings end with '.' and others do not within the same file
clusters.rationale: These strings are published verbatim in the API reference, where inconsistent punctuation within one endpoint group reads as sloppiness.

clusters.rule: Do not use hasattr(state, 'value') guards on Airflow state enum types; all TerminalTIState, TerminalStateNonSuccess, and TaskInstanceState values always have .value
clusters.trigger: hasattr(some_state, 'value') pattern used with a variable typed as TerminalTIState, TerminalStateNonSuccess, or TaskInstanceState
clusters.rationale: The guard implies these types can be non-enums, which is false; it hides real type errors instead of catching them.

clusters.rule: Remove TODO comments that document conclusions of already-completed investigations; if the conclusion is 'no easy way to achieve this', delete the comment rather than leaving it in code
clusters.trigger: # TODO: comment in execution_api routes where the investigation has already concluded it is infeasible
clusters.rationale: This was a reviewer clearing one stale comment; as a rule it is generic tidy-up advice rather than Airflow-specific judgement.

clusters.rule: Multi-team validation error messages shared across connections, pools, and variables routes must be extracted into a single shared constant to avoid drift
clusters.trigger: identical multi_team error message string literal duplicated across two or more of connections.py / pools.py / variables.py
clusters.rationale: These three routes implement the same multi-team check; copies of the message drift apart and users see different wording for the same refusal.

clusters.rule: Error messages that cite 'manually triggered' as the reason logical_date is None must also cover asset-triggered DAG runs, which equally have logical_date=None
clusters.trigger: error message string containing 'manually triggered' adjacent to a logical_date is None check on a DagRun
clusters.rationale: Asset-triggered runs are a first-class Airflow 3 run type with no logical date, so a message naming only manual triggering misdiagnoses them.

clusters.rule: Removing an existing public REST API query parameter is a breaking change; keep the old parameter and add the new one alongside it
clusters.trigger: diff removing a Query parameter (e.g. xcom_key) from a public route that previously exposed it
clusters.rationale: The public REST API carries stability guarantees across minor releases; silently dropping a parameter breaks clients that pass it.

clusters.rule: Logic used exclusively by a public API endpoint must not be placed under the ui/ service layer; move it to a common or public service module
clusters.trigger: service function inside api_fastapi/.../services/ui/ being imported or called from a public/ route
clusters.rationale: The ui/ tree is explicitly the UI's own unstable surface; public routes depending on it erases the stability boundary the split exists to create.

clusters.rule: Dashboard DAG state counts (active, failed, running, queued) must use a consistent semantic baseline - either all based on latest run or all based on any run - so counts cannot exceed the total number of DAGs
clusters.trigger: dashboard query mixing latest-run state with any-run state counts in the same response (e.g. failed uses latest_state while running/queued use any DagRun in that state)
clusters.rationale: This describes a specific defect in the dashboard endpoint where mixed baselines produced impossible totals, rather than a standing repo expectation.

clusters.rule: Skip calling _serialize_xcoms() entirely when result_task_ids is an empty list; only call it when result_task_ids is None (DAG-authored default) or a non-empty list
clusters.trigger: await self._serialize_xcoms() called unconditionally or without checking result_task_ids == []
clusters.rationale: A one-off optimisation tied to a single call site in the dag_run service, not a pattern future code could generally violate.

clusters.rule: OpenTelemetry span names in the task execution path must embed the executing component (worker or triggerer) as a segment, e.g. `task_run.worker.{task_id}` or `worker.{task_id}`
clusters.trigger: New `tracer.start_span(name=...)` call in task execution routes uses a flat name like `task_run.{task_id}` without a component segment
clusters.rationale: Traces are read across components; without the component segment a worker span and a triggerer span for the same task are indistinguishable in the backend.

clusters.rule: Bundle names persisted in `DagBundleModel` rows and emitted in REST API responses must be finalised before the first release that ships them; renaming afterwards requires a DB migration
clusters.trigger: A new auto-generated bundle name string (e.g. via an f-string concatenating package names) is introduced in bundle-discovery code that writes to `DagBundleModel`
clusters.rationale: Bundle names are persisted identifiers and appear in API payloads, so what looks like an internal naming choice becomes a migration and a compatibility break once released.

clusters.rule: Use structlog keyword-argument style for all log calls; do not use `%s` positional format strings as log message arguments
clusters.trigger: A `log.info(...)`, `log.warning(...)`, or similar structlog call passes positional `%s` format arguments instead of keyword arguments for metadata fields
clusters.rationale: Airflow 3 emits structured logs; interpolating values into the message string destroys the machine-readable fields the structlog pipeline is there to produce.

clusters.rule: Config entries in `config.yml` must document the meaning of all special sentinel values (e.g. `0` meaning "disabled" or "unlimited") in the `description` field
clusters.trigger: A new config key with a numeric `default` of `0` (or another sentinel) is added to `config.yml` without the `description` explaining what `0` means
clusters.rationale: config.yml generates the published configuration reference; an undocumented sentinel leaves operators guessing whether 0 disables the feature or breaks it.

clusters.rule: A config `description` in `config.yml` must not reference Airflow features or model fields that do not exist at HEAD in the same PR
clusters.trigger: A new config key's `description` mentions a field name or feature (e.g. `TaskInstanceDTO.language`) that is not present in the codebase in the same PR
clusters.rationale: The generated config reference is user-facing documentation; naming fields that do not exist yet documents a product Airflow does not ship.

clusters.rule: A new single-entry config section must not be created as a top-level section in `config.yml`; place the entry in the `core` section following the precedent of `xcom_backend` and similar singleton settings
clusters.trigger: A new top-level YAML section is added to `config.yml` containing only one config key, when no further keys are planned
clusters.rationale: Config sections are part of the public configuration surface and cannot be moved without a deprecation cycle; single-key sections proliferate and follow the precedent already set by core.xcom_backend.

clusters.rule: `VersionChange` subclass names must describe the schema migration performed (what field or model changes), not the behaviour of the old code being replaced
clusters.trigger: A class that subclasses `VersionChange` is named after what the previous code did (e.g. `ValidateSomething`) rather than after the data-model delta (e.g. `ChangeFooToBar`)
clusters.rationale: These classes are read as an ordered changelog of the Execution API schema; naming them after old behaviour makes the sequence unreadable.

clusters.rule: Do not add application-level mutex lock tables to guard writes that SQLite already serialises; skip the lock for SQLite backends
clusters.trigger: A new ORM model used as a mutex lock (e.g. `MutexLock`, `LockTable`) is added and `session.add`/`session.delete` are used around a critical section without a SQLite exemption
clusters.rationale: SQLite serialises writers at the database level, so the extra lock table adds contention and failure modes for the backend that least needs it.

clusters.rule: Use `if TYPE_CHECKING: assert x is not None` to narrow a variable's type within a branch rather than widening a downstream function's signature to accept `None`
clusters.trigger: A function's parameter type is widened to `T | None` solely because a caller cannot statically prove the value is non-None at the call site, and the value is known to be non-None at runtime
clusters.rationale: Widening the signature to satisfy one call site tells every other caller that None is acceptable, pushing None handling into code that should never see it.

clusters.rule: Prefer `session.scalar()` or `session.scalars().one()` over `session.get()` with a composite primary-key dict when querying ORM models
clusters.trigger: `session.get(ModelClass, {"key1": val1, "key2": val2})` is used to look up a model with a composite primary key
clusters.rationale: The dict form of session.get is easy to get subtly wrong across Airflow's composite-key models and reads worse than an explicit select in this codebase.

clusters.rule: Setting `_AIRFLOW_PROCESS_CONTEXT` must be centralised in the `action_cli` decorator (when `check_db=True`), not scattered at individual CLI command call sites
clusters.trigger: A CLI command manually sets or reads `os.environ["_AIRFLOW_PROCESS_CONTEXT"]` inside the command body rather than relying on the `action_cli` decorator
clusters.rationale: Per-command environment fiddling means every new command must remember to do it; the decorator every command already carries is the one place that cannot be forgotten.

clusters.rule: When adding a new keyword argument to a DB-command callable passed to `run_db_migrate_command`, all concrete implementations of that callable (including `BaseDBManager.upgradedb` and `FABDBManager.upgradedb`) must accept the new kwarg
clusters.trigger: A new `kwarg` is forwarded to a `command(...)` call inside `run_db_migrate_command` but the corresponding `upgradedb` methods on `BaseDBManager` or `FABDBManager` are not updated to accept it
clusters.rationale: The dispatch is dynamic, so a missing kwarg on one implementation only fails at runtime for the deployments that use that DB manager.

clusters.rule: CLI date arguments that document a `yyyy-mm-dd` format must strictly validate that format and reject ISO-8601 datetime strings (e.g. timestamps with a `T` component)
clusters.trigger: A CLI argument parsed with `parsedate` or similar permissive parser is documented as accepting only `yyyy-mm-dd` but is not validated to reject datetime strings with time components
clusters.rationale: A permissive parser silently accepts a value the documented contract excludes, so the user gets a result computed against a different date semantics than they asked for.

clusters.rule: The DAG-importer extension registry must raise or warn when a newly registered importer tries to claim an extension that is already owned by another importer, preventing silent override
clusters.trigger: A `register()` method or dict assignment in the importer registry performs `self._importers[ext] = importer` without first checking for an existing entry
clusters.rationale: Importers come from plugins and providers; a silent override means whichever loads last wins and users get inexplicably different parsing behaviour.

clusters.rule: In example DAGs, inject context values via named `@task` parameters (e.g. `def load(asset_state):`) rather than capturing them from `**context`
clusters.trigger: An example DAG `@task` function signature uses `**context` and then accesses `context["asset_state"]`, `context["task_state"]`, or similar named keys
clusters.rationale: Example DAGs teach the recommended authoring style; named parameters are the modern TaskFlow idiom and self-document what the task consumes.

clusters.rule: Do not use the variable name `ts` in example DAG task functions, because `ts` is a reserved Airflow template variable (execution timestamp) and the abbreviation causes confusion
clusters.trigger: An example DAG assigns `ts = context["task_state"]` or uses `ts` as a local variable name inside a `@task` function
clusters.rationale: `ts` already means the execution timestamp everywhere else in Airflow; reusing it in an example teaches readers a collision.

clusters.rule: When renaming an example DAG file or model, rename the corresponding test file and all test class names in the same commit; do not leave stale `*State` names in files that now test `*Store` semantics
clusters.trigger: A PR renames an example DAG (e.g. `example_task_state` -> `example_task_store`) but the matching test file path or class name still contains the old identifier
clusters.rationale: Airflow's test layout mirrors the source tree by convention, so a half-applied rename leaves tests nobody can locate from the file they cover.

clusters.rule: When forcibly failing a stuck queued TaskInstance in the scheduler, update both the TI ORM state (`ti.set_state(FAILED)`) and the executor state (`executor.fail(ti.key)`) together; do not rely solely on executor drift detection to propagate the failure
clusters.trigger: Code in `scheduler_job_runner.py` that handles stuck TIs calls only `executor.fail(ti.key)` without also setting `ti.set_state(TaskInstanceState.FAILED, session=session)`
clusters.rationale: Drift detection is best-effort and runs on its own schedule; leaving the DB row queued means the task stays stuck exactly as before from the user's view.

clusters.rule: Deadline/callback workloads must capture the `bundle_version` from the DAG run at the time the workload is created, not resolved lazily at execution time, to ensure the correct bundle version is used even after a bundle upgrade
clusters.trigger: Code building a deadline or callback `WorkloadDTO` in `executors/workloads/task.py` sets `bundle_info.version` from `ti.dag_run.bundle_version` at execution time rather than at enqueue/creation time
clusters.rationale: Bundles can be upgraded between enqueue and execution, so a lazily resolved version runs the callback against code the run was never planned with.

clusters.rule: `trigger_connection_tests()` in `BaseExecutor` must check remaining slot capacity (`self.slots_available`) before dispatching queued connection-test workloads, not assume slots are fully available after `trigger_tasks()` has already consumed some
clusters.trigger: The `trigger_connection_tests()` method in `base_executor.py` dispatches all entries in `queued_connection_tests` via `_process_workloads` without first checking `self.slots_available`
clusters.rationale: A specific over-dispatch defect in one newly added executor method, not a standing rule new code elsewhere could violate.

clusters.rule: The abstract `key` property on workload base classes in `executors/workloads/` must be typed as `Hashable` (not `Any`) to enforce the constraint that workload keys must be usable as dict keys
clusters.trigger: An `@abstractmethod` property named `key` in `executors/workloads/base.py` is declared with return type `Any` instead of `Hashable`
