clusters.rationale: provider.yaml is rendered into the connection UI and provider docs, so stale descriptions mislead users directly.

clusters.rule: Never hand-edit generated files; change the source of truth and regenerate in the same commit - `get_provider_info.py` comes from `provider.yaml` via `prek run update-providers-build-files`, and the task-SDK `datamodels/_generated.py` comes from the Execution API OpenAPI schema
clusters.trigger: A diff edits `providers/**/get_provider_info.py` or `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/api/datamodels/_generated.py` by hand, or edits a `provider.yaml` without the matching regenerated `get_provider_info.py`
clusters.rationale: Hand edits to generated files are overwritten by the next regeneration and break the pre-commit consistency checks.

clusters.rule: When a hook deliberately ignores parameters it inherits from its parent signature (e.g. `api_key`, `base_url`) and reads the values from the connection `extra` instead, say so explicitly in the docstring
clusters.trigger: A method in `providers/**/hooks/*.py` accepts parameters whose names duplicate `extra` keys but reads the `extra` values and never uses the parameters, with no docstring note
clusters.rationale: Silently ignored parameters look like they work; users pass them and cannot tell why nothing changes.

clusters.rule: Fields that act as discriminators for a polling loop (e.g. a human-in-the-loop XCom `action`) must be typed as `Literal` or an `Enum`, not bare `str`
clusters.trigger: A dataclass/TypedDict/Pydantic field typed `str` is compared against specific literal values ("approve", "reject", ...) to decide whether a poll loop terminates
clusters.rationale: A typo in the written value silently never matches and the task loops forever instead of failing.

clusters.rule: Every hook subclass that introduces its own `conn_type` must declare a matching `default_conn_name` rather than inheriting the parent hook's generic one
clusters.trigger: A hook subclass defines `conn_type` but no `default_conn_name`
clusters.rationale: Inheriting the parent default makes two different connection types resolve to the same default connection id.

clusters.rule: A deferrable operator's `get_job_status` must translate a not-found/expired remote job into a non-active, non-succeeded status so the resumable mixin resubmits, instead of letting the API error propagate as a task failure
clusters.trigger: A `get_job_status` implementation calls the remote API without handling the 404/expired-run error path
clusters.rationale: Remote job history expires; a task that merely lost its job record should be resubmitted, not hard-failed.

clusters.rule: In Databricks trigger constructors, pass `owner=caller` to validation helpers rather than `owner=self.__class__.__name__`, matching the existing `caller` attribution pattern
clusters.trigger: A validation helper invoked from a trigger `__init__` uses `owner=self.__class__.__name__` while the constructor already accepts a `caller: str`
clusters.rationale: The `caller` value is what the rest of the Databricks provider reports in attribution and error messages.

clusters.rule: Import `Connection` from `airflow.models.connection` in provider code, not from `airflow.providers.common.compat.version_compat` or another compat shim
clusters.trigger: A provider file imports `Connection` from any module other than `airflow.models.connection`
clusters.rationale: The compat module re-exports it only for its own use; importing through it couples providers to compat internals.

clusters.rule: A changelog `.. note::` about minimum Airflow version must not claim the release requires a newer Airflow than it does when the provider still runs on older versions and only conditionally activates the new feature
clusters.trigger: A `changelog.rst` note states the provider *requires* Airflow X.Y while the code activates the feature behind a version guard
clusters.rationale: Overstated constraints push users into unnecessary upgrades and misrepresent the provider's support matrix.

clusters.rule: Refer to Airflow's metrics integration generically (statsd and OpenTelemetry) in documentation; do not describe it as "statsd" only
clusters.trigger: Docs or comments describe Airflow metrics/observability exclusively as statsd with no mention of OTel
clusters.rationale: Airflow's stats layer has supported OpenTelemetry alongside statsd for several releases.

clusters.rule: Edge executor SQL that filters on a recently added column must tolerate databases that predate the migration adding it
clusters.trigger: A SQLAlchemy query in the Edge executor adds a `.where(Model.new_column == ...)` on a newly introduced column with no schema-version guard
clusters.rationale: Edge components run against Airflow deployments whose schema may lag the provider release.

clusters.rule: Tests for a validation or safety helper must include the exact call signature the production operator uses (e.g. `allowed_types=DEFAULT_ALLOWED_TYPES`), not only synthetic argument combinations
clusters.trigger: New tests for a validation function cover argument combinations that the owning operator never produces, leaving the operator's real code path untested
clusters.rationale: A helper can be fully covered while the only call site in production remains unexercised.

clusters.rule: When a module referenced by `providers/common/compat/.../sdk.py` is renamed or moved, update the compat mapping tuple in the same change
clusters.trigger: A module path renamed while `common/compat/sdk.py` still maps to the old location
clusters.rationale: The compat mapping is what lets providers resolve SDK symbols across Airflow versions; a stale entry fails at import time.

clusters.rule: Values in `provider.yaml` that a user is meant to copy - config `example:` values and `ui-field-behaviour` `placeholders` - must be literal, runtime-valid values (the codec name the code accepts, valid JSON for a Connection `extra`), never file-extension aliases or Python expressions
clusters.trigger: A `provider.yaml` config entry's `example:` is not a value the runtime accepts (e.g. `"gz"` where the code wants `"gzip"`), or a `placeholders.extra` block contains a non-JSON token such as `cls.default_open_options`
clusters.rationale: These strings are rendered verbatim into the connection UI and provider docs, so anything that is not directly usable is actively wrong.

clusters.rule: When an operator has both a synchronous and a deferred execution path, the two must emit equivalent progress log messages so task logs are comparable between modes
clusters.trigger: A sync code path in an operator that also has a deferred path omits the progress/offset logging the deferred path emits
clusters.rationale: Operators are switched between deferrable and sync at will; log output disappearing is a silent regression for anyone debugging.

clusters.rule: Represent config-driven defaults consistently: keep the inline `conf.getboolean("operators", "default_deferrable", fallback=False)` expression in the runtime `__init__` signature rather than defaulting to `None` and resolving in the body, and use `...` for that parameter in the corresponding `.pyi` stub instead of a hardcoded literal
clusters.trigger: An `__init__` changes `deferrable=conf.getboolean(...)` to `deferrable=None`, or a `.pyi` stub declares `deferrable: bool = False` for a parameter whose runtime default reads Airflow configuration
clusters.rationale: The inline call is the documented Airflow pattern for config-backed defaults, and a stub literal misstates the default to type checkers and IDE users.

clusters.rule: A dependency used by only one optional code path must not appear in a provider's mandatory `dependencies`; put it in a named extras group and guard the import, especially when it is experimental or a protocol upgrade
clusters.trigger: A new package is added to the `dependencies` list in a provider's `pyproject.toml` while being used in a single optional feature, or the added dependency is described as experimental/optional
clusters.rationale: Mandatory entries are installed for every user of the provider, so an optional or experimental library becomes an unavoidable install and a resolver constraint.

clusters.rule: Every authentication branch added to or reordered inside a hook's `_get_token`/`_init_conn`/`get_conn` must come with a unit test that pins that branch - including the ambiguous case where several auth extras are set at once
clusters.trigger: A provider hook gains a new auth branch, or reorders existing auth if-branches, with no test covering that branch or the multi-extra precedence
clusters.rationale: Auth dispatch precedence is invisible in the diff and silently changes which credential a deployment ends up using.

clusters.rule: Every Edge3 job row inserted into the database must carry `team_name` so the fetch endpoint and callback handling can route jobs in multi-team deployments
clusters.trigger: An `EdgeJobModel` (or equivalent) insert inside edge3 executor or callback-handling code omits `team_name`
clusters.rationale: Rows without a team cannot be matched to a worker or a callback in a multi-team setup.

clusters.rule: Do not commit compiled provider UI build output; `dist/` bundles must be produced by Breeze or at provider-package build time and be gitignored
clusters.trigger: Files under `providers/*/**/plugins/www/dist/` (`*.js`, `*.js.map`, `*.d.ts`) added in a diff
clusters.rationale: Committed bundles go stale against their sources and pollute review diffs.

clusters.rule: Obtain the FAB auth manager through `get_fab_auth_manager()` or an explicit `isinstance` check that raises a clear error when FAB is not the configured auth manager - never `cast(FabAuthManager, get_auth_manager())`
clusters.trigger: `cast("FabAuthManager", get_auth_manager())` or `cast(FabAuthManager, ...)` in FAB provider route or helper code
clusters.rationale: The cast is a lie to the type checker: with a non-FAB auth manager configured the code fails later with an unrelated AttributeError instead of a clear message.

clusters.rule: Pass `Model.__tablename__` rather than `Model.__table__` when programmatically dropping the Edge3 ORM tables
clusters.trigger: `EdgeWorkerModel.__table__`, `EdgeJobModel.__table__` or `EdgeLogsModel.__table__` used in a drop-table list
clusters.rationale: The drop helper expects table names; passing Table objects was a defect in the edge3 db teardown path.

clusters.rule: Use HTTP verbs rather than action suffixes for Edge3 worker UI routes - `PUT /worker/{name}/queues` to replace the queue list, not `POST /worker/{name}/queues/add`
clusters.trigger: An `@ui_router.post` decorator whose path ends in an action segment such as `/queues/add` or `/queues/remove`
clusters.rationale: RPC-style action paths break the REST conventions the rest of the Airflow API follows.

clusters.rule: Declare `testcontainers` once as a shared `devel-common` dependency instead of adding it to an individual provider's dev-dependency group
clusters.trigger: `testcontainers` added to a `[project.optional-dependencies]` dev block in any provider's `pyproject.toml`
clusters.rationale: Test tooling shared by several providers is pinned in one place so versions cannot diverge.

clusters.rule: Build Elasticsearch response fixtures with the existing `_build_es_search_response()` test helper rather than hand-rolling response dicts
clusters.trigger: A literal ES response dict such as `{"hits": {"total": ..., "hits": []}}` used as a mock return value in elasticsearch provider tests
clusters.rationale: Hand-written fixtures drift from the real response shape when the client version changes.

clusters.rule: Name FastAPI request and response datamodels `*Body` and `*Response`, matching the Airflow Core API convention - not `*In`/`*Out`
clusters.trigger: A Pydantic model class name ending in `In` or `Out` in an Airflow FastAPI datamodels file
clusters.rationale: The generated OpenAPI schema and clients are shared with Core API consumers who expect the Body/Response naming.

clusters.rule: Import FastAPI utilities from `fastapi`, not directly from `starlette`, in provider route and dependency files
clusters.trigger: `from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException` or `from starlette import status` in a provider FastAPI module
clusters.rationale: FastAPI's re-exports are the supported surface; importing from starlette bypasses FastAPI's own handling and version guarantees.

clusters.rule: Do not mutate Flask-AppBuilder's global `Model.metadata` at import time; scope metadata overrides to Airflow's own mapper registry
clusters.trigger: Assignment to `Model.metadata` or `Base.metadata` at module level inside the FAB provider
clusters.rationale: Import-time mutation of a third-party global leaks into every consumer of FAB in the same process, including code that never touches Airflow's models.

clusters.rule: Google provider operator `execute` methods must log what operation they are performing with `self.log.info` before or after calling the hook
clusters.trigger: An operator `execute()` in `providers/google` calls a hook method with no accompanying `self.log.info`
clusters.rationale: Task logs are the only visibility users have into which GCP call an operator made.

clusters.rule: Write `AIRFLOW_CONN_*` environment-variable examples in Google provider docs in connection-URI form rather than as a JSON object literal
clusters.trigger: A provider `.rst` file contains `export AIRFLOW_CONN_<ID>='{...}'` with a JSON object literal
clusters.rationale: The URI form is what the rest of the Google connection documentation uses and it round-trips through the connection parser without quoting pitfalls.

clusters.rule: When a new operator parameter's default is planned to change in a future release, default it to `None` as the unset sentinel and emit a `FutureWarning` when `None` is seen, instead of shipping the current default directly
clusters.trigger: A new `__init__` parameter is added with a concrete default that is documented or discussed as changing in a later release
clusters.rationale: The sentinel lets Airflow distinguish "user did not choose" from "user chose the old value" and warn only the former when the default flips.

clusters.rule: A substring check on a URL used for security decisions must assert the trusted value's position (typically that it is the hostname), not merely that it appears somewhere in the string
clusters.trigger: `if "<trusted-domain>" in url` or a similar unanchored substring test used to authenticate or route a request
clusters.rationale: An attacker-controlled URL can contain the trusted domain in its path or query and pass an unanchored check.

clusters.rule: Prefer removing an existing `# type: ignore` over broadening it; do not add new error codes to a suppression comment
clusters.trigger: A diff appends a new mypy error code to an existing `# type: ignore[...]` comment
clusters.rationale: Each added code widens what the suppression hides; the underlying typing problem should be fixed instead.

clusters.rule: Under Uvicorn, remove the Flask/Werkzeug `Date` response header unconditionally in the FAB app's `after_request` hook so only one `Date` header is emitted
clusters.trigger: A `flask_app.after_request` hook conditionally reads or removes the `Date` header in the FAB ASGI integration
clusters.rationale: One-off fix for duplicate Date headers when the Flask app is served through the ASGI adapter.

clusters.rule: Derive the `secure` cookie flag from the request scheme as well as the `api.ssl_cert` configuration, not from `ssl_cert` alone
clusters.trigger: `secure = bool(conf.get("api", "ssl_cert", fallback=""))` with no check of the request's scheme
clusters.rationale: TLS is frequently terminated by a proxy, so `ssl_cert` being unset does not mean the request was plaintext - and the cookie ends up unprotected.

clusters.rule: Google provider hook methods must take the components of a GCP resource name (project, location, id) as separate parameters rather than a single full `projects/{p}/locations/{l}/...` string
clusters.trigger: A Google hook method accepts a `name: str` parameter holding a full GCP resource path
clusters.rationale: Component parameters let the hook apply `fallback_to_default_project_id` and match the rest of the Google provider's hook signatures.

clusters.rule: Type Google hook method parameters with the concrete Google Cloud client library types instead of widening them to `Any`
clusters.trigger: A Google hook method annotates a parameter `Any` where the client counterpart has a concrete type (e.g. `types.DeleteAgentEngineConfigOrDict`)
clusters.rationale: The hook is a thin pass-through; losing the client's types loses the only type checking users get.

clusters.rule: In Google hooks decorated with `@GoogleBaseHook.fallback_to_default_project_id`, document `project_id` as optional and place it last in the parameter list and docstring
clusters.trigger: A method with that decorator documents `project_id` as required or lists it before the other parameters
clusters.rationale: The decorator supplies `project_id` from the connection when omitted, so describing it as required contradicts the actual call contract.

clusters.rule: Apply an operator's passthrough config dict (e.g. `extra_config`) last - after every field derived from top-level parameters - so it genuinely wins for overlapping keys as documented
clusters.trigger: A passthrough dict is merged into the API-representation dict before top-level params (`schema_fields`, `max_bad_records`) are assigned onto the constructed object
clusters.rationale: Merging it early makes the documented escape hatch silently lose to the operator's own parameters.

clusters.rule: When a docstring's `:param api_version:` example is bumped, update the versioned API documentation links in the same docstring to the matching version
clusters.trigger: A `:param api_version:` example changes (e.g. v4 to v5) while an official-API-docs link in the same class docstring still contains the old `/rest/v4/` path
clusters.rationale: The links are the only place users find the field definitions for the version the operator now defaults to.

clusters.rule: Collapse provider unit tests that differ only in one input and one expected value into a single `@pytest.mark.parametrize`d test
clusters.trigger: Two adjacent tests such as `test_x_with_<flag>` / `test_x_without_<flag>` with identical bodies apart from one argument and one assertion
clusters.rationale: Airflow's provider test suites use parametrize for this, and duplicated bodies drift apart when the code changes.

clusters.rule: Tests must assert the behaviour a change produces, not that arguments were forwarded or internals were touched: for an error-suppression flag, give the mocked client a `side_effect` raising the real provider exception and assert nothing propagates
clusters.trigger: A test for `ignore_error=True`/soft-fail behaviour only asserts `<method>.assert_called_once_with(..., on_error=mock.ANY)` and never sets `side_effect`, or a test asserts only on `inspect.signature` or internal state the fix did not change
clusters.rationale: A forwarding assertion passes even when the flag has no effect, so the test provides no protection against the bug returning.

clusters.rule: Every public hook method added must gain a unit test that asserts the mocked client call chain arguments and the returned value, matching the pattern already used in that test module
clusters.trigger: A hook gains public methods while the corresponding `providers/*/tests/unit/.../test_<hook>.py` covers only some of them
clusters.rationale: Hook methods are thin wrappers whose only real content is the argument mapping, which is exactly what an untested method gets wrong.

clusters.rule: Resolve team-scoped secrets through the same `_get_team_or_global_secret` helper for connections, variables and config; do not gate the team-aware lookup behind the `core.multi_team` config flag
clusters.trigger: A secrets backend getter branches on `conf.getboolean("core", "multi_team")` to choose between team-aware and plain lookup
clusters.rationale: Config-gated scoping means the team boundary silently disappears in deployments that have not set the flag.

clusters.rule: Tests for behaviour gated on an Airflow config flag must also exercise the flag-off state with `conf_vars`, asserting the legacy path is unchanged
clusters.trigger: Every new test wraps the call in `with conf_vars({("core", "multi_team"): "True"})` and none exercises the same call with the flag disabled
clusters.rationale: The whole point of the flag is that existing deployments keep the old behaviour, and nothing checks that.

clusters.rule: Do not add a boolean opt-in flag whose only effect is the format of the value `execute()` returns when the previous value is still pushed to its own named XCom key
clusters.trigger: A new `__init__` boolean parameter (e.g. `return_gcs_uris`) that only switches the return-value format while the legacy value remains available under a separate XCom key
clusters.rationale: Users can already read the value they want from the named key, so the flag adds a permanent API branch for nothing.

clusters.rule: Import an optional third-party SDK once - at module level behind `try`/`except ImportError`, or in a single shared helper that raises `AirflowOptionalProviderFeatureException` - rather than repeating a bare `import` inside each hook or operator method
clusters.trigger: The same optional library (e.g. `import ibmmq`, an optional redis extra) is imported inside several method bodies of a provider hook/operator with no shared helper and no optional-feature exception
clusters.rationale: Scattered in-method imports surface a raw `ImportError` at task runtime instead of Airflow's optional-feature message, and each site has to be fixed separately.

clusters.rule: Log transient, retried API errors inside a trigger's async polling loop at info/debug level or rate-limit them; do not emit a warning on every retry
clusters.trigger: `except <TransientError>` inside a trigger `run()` loop calls `self.log.warning(...)` immediately before `await asyncio.sleep(self.polling_period_seconds)`
clusters.rationale: A per-poll warning floods triggerer logs for a condition the trigger is designed to ride out.

clusters.rule: In a trigger, filter a bulk list result that is already in scope instead of issuing one API request per item
clusters.trigger: A comprehension inside a trigger awaits `self.hook.get_<resource>(name=...)` once per name when a `list_<resources>()` result for the same namespace/selector has already been awaited
clusters.rationale: The triggerer multiplexes many triggers on one event loop, so per-item calls in a poll loop multiply into API rate-limit pressure.

clusters.rule: A trigger's `run()` must poll in a loop until its condition holds (bounded by a timeout where one applies), never a single await/check that can return nothing and fall back to stale data or exit silently
clusters.trigger: A trigger's async `run()` performs one list/get call and then does `if not <resource>:` to fall back to a previously captured value, or contains a single await that can return `None` with no enclosing `while True` loop
clusters.rationale: The state a trigger waits on becomes true only eventually; a one-shot check either uses stale data or lets the trigger terminate without ever firing an event.

clusters.rule: Add new optional parameters to an existing provider hook or operator `__init__` as keyword-only arguments, after a `*` separator
clusters.trigger: A new optional parameter is inserted positionally into an existing `__init__` signature with no preceding `*`
clusters.rationale: Positional insertion silently reinterprets existing callers' arguments.

clusters.rule: Probe an optional credential capability with `callable(getattr(credentials, "with_quota_project", None))` rather than `hasattr`
clusters.trigger: `if not hasattr(credentials, "<method>")` guards a subsequent call to that method on a google-auth credentials object
clusters.rationale: google-auth credential classes expose non-callable attributes of the same name, so hasattr passes and the call then fails.

clusters.rule: The OpenLineage JDBC authority extractor must strip `user:pass@` userinfo from the URL and handle Oracle thin URLs that use `@//` instead of `://`
clusters.trigger: `_get_openlineage_authority` or an equivalent JDBC URL parser splits on `://` only and does not strip userinfo
clusters.rationale: Specific defect in the JDBC authority parser that leaked credentials into lineage and mis-parsed Oracle URLs.

clusters.rule: Do not mutate `sys.modules` from a provider test package's `__init__.py`; install the stub with `monkeypatch.setitem` in a fixture scoped to the tests that need it
clusters.trigger: `sys.modules["..."] = ...` in a `tests/` package `__init__.py` rather than in a fixture or conftest
clusters.rationale: Package-level module injection leaks into every test collected afterwards in the same session.

clusters.rule: Provider documentation examples for providers whose minimum Airflow version is 3 must use `schedule=` and import `PythonOperator` from `airflow.providers.standard.operators.python`
clusters.trigger: A provider README or docs example uses `schedule_interval=` or imports `PythonOperator` from `airflow.operators.python`
clusters.rationale: Those APIs were removed in Airflow 3, so the example cannot run on the versions the provider supports.

clusters.rule: An async (deferrable) hook must accept the same connection extras as its synchronous counterpart; where an extra genuinely cannot be supported, raise `AirflowException` explicitly instead of ignoring it
clusters.trigger: An async hook's credential-setup branch omits handling for connection extras (e.g. `key_path`, `key_json`) that the sync hook supports
clusters.rationale: The same connection is used in both modes, so silently ignoring an extra makes the deferrable path authenticate as something else.

clusters.rule: A test for a polling-retry loop must assert the sleep mock's call count, not only the final result
clusters.trigger: A test patches `time.sleep` while exercising a polling retry loop but never asserts `mock_sleep.call_count`
clusters.rationale: Without the count the test passes whether the loop retried once, many times, or not at all.

clusters.rule: In deferrable Azure container operators, do not treat `provisioning_state` alone as a terminal signal for stopping deferral; check the container's execution state via `instance_view.current_state`
clusters.trigger: A deferrable operator tests `cg_state.provisioning_state` (e.g. `"Succeeded"`) as the condition to stop deferring without also checking `instance_view.current_state`
clusters.rationale: Provisioning succeeding only means the container group was created, not that the container ran.

clusters.rule: Compare cross-provider versions with `packaging.Version` directly rather than re-wrapping `Version(...).base_version` in another `Version()`
clusters.trigger: `Version(Version(...).base_version)` in a cross-provider version comparison
clusters.rationale: Single-line redundancy noted during review of the gcs_to_wasb version check.

clusters.rule: Pass a new connection keyword from a hook only when the user actually supplied it, so existing connections keep their previous client behaviour
clusters.trigger: A hook's `get_conn()` or connection-building method unconditionally passes a newly added keyword argument that previously had no default
clusters.rationale: An unconditional new kwarg changes the client's behaviour for every existing deployment that never opted in.

clusters.rule: Client-identification metadata sent to a third-party service must use the full provider package name (e.g. `apache-airflow-providers-redis`) so the reported version matches the component being identified
clusters.trigger: Provider code sets a client library name or `driver_info` string to `apache-airflow` while reporting `provider_version`
clusters.rationale: Reporting the Airflow name with the provider's version makes the telemetry meaningless to the vendor and to us.

clusters.rule: Use the `NOTSET` sentinel to distinguish "user explicitly passed None" from "parameter not provided" in Airflow 2.x compatibility branches
clusters.trigger: Code in an Airflow-2.x compat branch tests `getattr(self, attr) is not None` to decide whether the user supplied the parameter
clusters.rationale: `None` is a legitimate user-supplied value here, so the None test silently reinterprets an explicit choice as an omission.

clusters.rule: A task-log handler must not set `metadata["end_of_log"] = True` merely because a log fetch returned no records; an empty result can mean logs are not yet indexed
clusters.trigger: A log handler sets `end_of_log` to True inside a branch triggered by an empty `logs_by_host` or equivalent empty response
clusters.rationale: Marking end-of-log early makes the UI stop polling and permanently hide logs that arrive moments later.

clusters.rule: When an optional dependency is missing but the surrounding method can still return partial results, emit a warning and continue rather than raising `AirflowOptionalProviderFeatureException`
clusters.trigger: An `except ImportError` block in a provider method raises `AirflowOptionalProviderFeatureException` for a dependency the method could work around
clusters.rationale: Raising discards the parse results the method already has for the sake of one unavailable enrichment step.

clusters.rule: The `check_provide_session_kwargs` CI script must inspect both `args.posonlyargs` and `args.args` when detecting a positional `session` parameter
clusters.trigger: The script's positional-detection function reads only `args.args`
clusters.rationale: Specific gap in the enforcement script that let positional-only session parameters through.

clusters.rule: Documentation for the `_openlineage` DAG-run conf dict must state that all six parent and root ID fields should be provided together, and that omitting root information is discouraged for consumers supporting ParentRunFacet 1.1.0
clusters.trigger: Docs list the `_openlineage` parent/root fields as fully optional with no note about supplying all six
clusters.rationale: Partial parent/root information produces lineage graphs that consumers cannot stitch back together.

clusters.rule: Import `airflow.settings` only after `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_CONN` has been set, and leave a comment stating why the import is deferred
clusters.trigger: An import of `airflow.settings` inside a function body near `settings.SQL_ALCHEMY_CONN` assignment or `settings.configure_orm()`
clusters.rationale: Importing settings reads the connection string once at import time, so an earlier import silently binds the ORM to the wrong database - and without the comment someone will hoist the import back to the top.

clusters.rule: The structlog serialization fallback in `airflow_shared.logging` must catch `ValueError` (including `UnicodeEncodeError`) in addition to `TypeError`
clusters.trigger: An `enc_hook`/serialization fallback except clause that catches only `TypeError`
clusters.rationale: Specific crash fix: non-encodable payloads raise ValueError subclasses that the original handler did not cover.

clusters.rule: Any flag or attribute a `_TaskDecorator.__call__` sets on the operator it builds must also be applied on the mapped-operator path created by `expand`/`expand_kwargs`
clusters.trigger: An operator attribute assigned inside `_TaskDecorator.__call__` with no equivalent assignment in the `expand`/`expand_kwargs` construction path
clusters.rationale: The two construction paths are separate, so anything added to only one silently does not apply to mapped tasks.

clusters.rule: Do not add module-level imports to `airflow.sdk.configuration` that defeat the lazy `conf` object; heavy or provider-touching imports belong inside `initialize_config()` or `__init__`
clusters.trigger: A top-level import of `ProvidersManagerTaskRuntime` or another provider-manager/heavy module added to `airflow.sdk.configuration` module scope
clusters.rationale: The lazy conf object exists so importing the SDK does not drag in the providers manager on every task start.

clusters.rule: Sockets created by task-SDK coordinator/supervisor code must bind to `127.0.0.1`, never to all interfaces
clusters.trigger: `socket.bind(("", port))` or `socket.bind(("0.0.0.0", port))` in a module under `task-sdk/`
clusters.rationale: These sockets carry task IPC and must not be reachable from outside the worker host.

clusters.rule: When `ExecutableCoordinator.find` locates a bundle but rejects it for a schema-version mismatch, include the rejection reason in the raised error instead of a debug log plus a generic `FileNotFoundError`
clusters.trigger: Bundle-lookup code logs the rejection at debug level and raises a generic not-found error
clusters.rationale: Specific diagnosability gap raised on the executable-bundle lookup path.

clusters.rule: `ResumableMixin.external_id_key` must be documented as the stable contract shared between an operator and its trigger, including the naming convention (`<provider>_<resource>_id`)
clusters.trigger: A `ResumableMixin`/`ResumableJobMixin` subclass overrides `external_id_key` with no docstring or comment explaining its cross-component role
clusters.rationale: The key is matched by string between the sync and deferrable halves, so a silent rename breaks resumption with no type error.

clusters.rule: Build dotted import paths for `import_string` from `__qualname__`, not `__name__`, and do not make that opt-in behind a flag
clusters.trigger: `obj.__name__` used to construct a dotted path intended for `import_string`, or a `use_qualname` flag gating `__qualname__`
clusters.rationale: `__name__` loses the enclosing class for nested objects, producing a path that cannot be imported back.

clusters.rule: `accepts_context` must not treat `VAR_POSITIONAL` (`*args`) as accepting context; only a named `context` parameter or `VAR_KEYWORD` counts
clusters.trigger: `inspect.Parameter.VAR_POSITIONAL` included in the kinds that make `accepts_context` return True
clusters.rationale: Specific defect: `*args` cannot receive the context kwarg, so matching it made callables look context-aware when they were not.

clusters.rule: Deserializing a Connection from a secrets backend must not require `conn_type` or `uri`; connections lacking them stay valid for Airflow 2 to 3 migration
clusters.trigger: Validation in `_deserialize_connection_value` or `BaseSecretsBackend` that raises when a JSON connection blob has neither `conn_type` nor `uri`
clusters.rationale: Existing secret stores hold connections written by Airflow 2 that never carried those fields; rejecting them breaks upgrades.

clusters.rule: Abstract `BaseStateBackend.serialize_*_to_ref` / `deserialize_*_from_ref` methods must document the JSON encoding contract the Execution API requires
clusters.trigger: One of those abstract methods is added or modified without a docstring stating the JSON round-trip requirement
clusters.rationale: Implementers outside this file have no other way to learn what shape the Execution API expects back.

clusters.rule: New documentation added under `task-sdk/docs/` must be linked from the corresponding `airflow-core/docs/authoring-and-scheduling/` page
clusters.trigger: A new `.rst` file under `task-sdk/docs/` with no link or `toctree` entry from the core authoring docs
clusters.rationale: DAG authors start in the core docs; unlinked task-SDK pages fragment the authoring documentation.

clusters.rule: Every `@lru_cache`d `@property` operations accessor on the task-SDK `Client` must carry a return-type annotation and a one-line docstring, matching the existing accessors
clusters.trigger: An `@lru_cache` + `@property` method on `Client` lacking a return annotation or docstring
clusters.rationale: These accessors are the SDK's public API surface and are consumed through type checking.

clusters.rule: `Client` operations `get` methods must convert an HTTP 404 `ServerResponseError` into a typed `ErrorResponse(error=ErrorType.*_NOT_FOUND)` rather than letting the raw exception escape
clusters.trigger: A new `*Operations.get` method on `Client` that does not translate a 404 into the typed error variant
clusters.rationale: Callers in the task runtime branch on the typed error; a raw transport exception crosses the API boundary unhandled.

clusters.rule: In DAG-parsing and other hot paths, pass log arguments lazily with %-style placeholders instead of calling `repr()`/`str()` before `log.debug()`
clusters.trigger: `log.debug(..., repr(x), ...)` or `log.debug(..., str(x), ...)` outside an `isEnabledFor` guard in a DAG-parsing code path
clusters.rationale: The formatting cost is paid on every parse even when debug logging is off, and DAG parsing runs continuously.

clusters.rule: Keep stdlib imports at the top of the file rather than inside function bodies when the module is already imported at top level and there is no circular-import risk
clusters.trigger: An import of a stdlib module (`sys`, `uuid`, `socket`, `traceback`) inside a function or method body in task-sdk source
clusters.rationale: General style cleanup rather than a repo-specific expectation.

clusters.rule: Task-SDK coordinator classes must not expose a separate `close()`; lifecycle cleanup belongs inside `execute_task` so the coordinator is self-contained
clusters.trigger: A `close()`/`cleanup()` method on a class that also implements `execute_task()` in `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/execution_time/coordinator.py` or a subclass
clusters.rationale: An externally called close makes correct cleanup the caller's responsibility, which nothing enforces.

clusters.rule: `get()` on task-SDK context accessors (`VariableAccessor`, `TaskStateAccessor`, `AssetStateAccessor`) must accept a `default` so callers can tell "key not set" from "key set to None"
clusters.trigger: A `get(key)` method on a task-SDK accessor in `execution_time/context.py` that returns None on missing and takes no default
clusters.rationale: These accessors store user values where None is legitimate, so returning None for both cases is ambiguous.

clusters.rule: Hoist repeated serialisation-envelope string literals (`__type`, `__var`, type tags) to module-level constants with small helper functions instead of repeating them inline
clusters.trigger: The same envelope string literal appears more than once in a file encoding/decoding a task-SDK IPC or state payload
clusters.rationale: General magic-string cleanup rather than a repo-specific expectation.

clusters.rule: Capture the previous signal handler from `signal.signal()`'s return value rather than making a separate `signal.getsignal()` call
clusters.trigger: `signal.getsignal(SIG...)` immediately before `signal.signal(SIG..., handler)` for the same signal
clusters.rationale: One-line redundancy noted on the supervisor signal-handling change.

clusters.rule: An error path in a post-`fork()` child must terminate with `os._exit()` unconditionally and never fall through into the parent's code path
clusters.trigger: An exception handler in a post-fork child path (`_fork_main`, `_child_exec_main`) that logs but does not call `os._exit()`
clusters.rationale: A child that returns instead of exiting continues executing the parent's supervisor logic in a forked process.

clusters.rule: Every method implemented on a concrete class that stands in for a Protocol must also be declared on the Protocol
clusters.trigger: A method on a concrete implementation (e.g. `_RealFernet`) absent from its Protocol (e.g. `FernetProtocol`) in task-sdk Protocol/impl pairs
clusters.rationale: Callers type against the Protocol, so methods missing from it are unreachable for type checkers and for alternative implementations.

clusters.rule: New fields in task-SDK IPC message types must be covered by direct unit tests exercising both the populated and the absent/None case
clusters.trigger: A new field added to a `CommsDecoder` message type or `_RequestFrame` in `execution_time/comms.py` with no corresponding presence/absence tests under `task-sdk/tests/`
clusters.rationale: The wire protocol is versioned across supervisor and task processes, where a field mishandled on one side fails only at runtime.

clusters.rule: Every data model consumed by `CommsDecoder` must be registered in the task-SDK schema-versions bundle, whether or not it originates from the Execution API spec
clusters.trigger: A new or modified Pydantic model used as a `CommsDecoder` message type that is absent from `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/execution_time/schema/versions/`
clusters.rationale: Version negotiation between supervisor and task processes is driven by that bundle, so an unregistered model cannot be negotiated.

clusters.rule: When `__attrs_post_init__` normalises a field in place (e.g. resolving a preset alias to its canonical value), add an inline comment explaining the transformation and that `attrs.evolve`, equality and serialisation will see the resolved value
clusters.trigger: `self.<field> = <transform>(self.<field>)` inside `__attrs_post_init__` in a task-sdk attrs class with no explanatory comment
clusters.rationale: The in-place rewrite is invisible at the call site but changes attrs semantics that later readers depend on.

clusters.rule: Place `otel_context.attach()` inside the `try` block whose `finally` detaches the token in the supervisor request handler
clusters.trigger: `otel_context.attach(...)` before a `try` whose `finally` calls `otel_context.detach(token)` in supervisor.py or task_runner.py
clusters.rationale: Specific leak fix in the OTel context handling of the supervisor request loop.

clusters.rule: Comment `force_flush(timeout_millis=...)` call sites to note that the value is an upper bound rather than a fixed wait
clusters.trigger: `provider.force_flush(timeout_millis=...)` added in task-SDK teardown with no explanatory comment
clusters.rationale: One-off review request on the OTel teardown change.

clusters.rule: Override Airflow configuration in tests with the `conf_vars` context manager rather than `unittest.mock.patch` on `conf.get`
clusters.trigger: `with patch("airflow.sdk.configuration.conf.get", ...)` or `patch("airflow.configuration.conf.get", ...)` in task-sdk tests
clusters.rationale: conf_vars restores state and goes through the real config machinery, so the test exercises the same lookup path as production.

clusters.rule: Delete unused test helper functions instead of leaving them as dead code
clusters.trigger: A helper defined in a test module under `task-sdk/tests/` that no test in the file calls
clusters.rationale: Generic dead-code cleanup rather than a repo-specific expectation.

clusters.rule: Guard tests that depend on POSIX `dup2` semantics with `pytest.mark.skipif(os.name == "nt", ...)`
clusters.trigger: `os.dup2(socket.fileno(), 0/1/2)` inside a test in `test_supervisor.py` with no platform guard
clusters.rationale: The task-SDK suite runs on Windows CI, where these calls fail outright.

clusters.rule: Use a short `time.sleep` (2 seconds or less) in the signal-forwarding integration test DAG so the test exits on SIGTERM instead of waiting out the supervisor watchdog window
clusters.trigger: `time.sleep(N)` with N > 5 inside a test operator's `execute()` in `signal_forward_test.py`
clusters.rationale: One-off runtime complaint about this specific integration test DAG.

clusters.rule: OTel span tests in the task SDK must assert parent/child span relationships, not merely that a span with the expected name was exported
clusters.trigger: A test asserts `"task.execute" in [s.name for s in exporter.get_finished_spans()]` without checking `span.parent.span_id`
clusters.rationale: Span nesting is the property that actually breaks, and a name-only assertion passes for orphaned spans.

clusters.rule: The TS-SDK log channel must buffer records emitted before the coordinator socket is connected and flush them on connect, rather than dropping them or writing only to stderr
clusters.trigger: `LogChannel.write()` returns early or writes only to stderr while `connected === false`, with no buffering
clusters.rationale: Specific gap raised on the initial TS-SDK log channel implementation.

clusters.rule: The TS-SDK public `TaskInstance` context must identify a task instance by the dag/run/task/map tuple, matching the Go and Java SDKs, rather than exposing a raw `taskInstanceId`
clusters.trigger: `readonly taskInstanceId: string` added to the public `TaskInstance` interface in `ts-sdk/src/task.ts`
clusters.rationale: Specific API-shape decision taken on the TS-SDK task interface.

clusters.rule: Re-snapshot contextvars after entering an OTel `detail_span` so operator child spans nest under it instead of becoming siblings
clusters.trigger: `contextvars.copy_context()` called before a `@detail_span`/`start_as_current_span` wrapper in task_runner.py, with `ctx.run()` used inside the span
clusters.rationale: Specific span-nesting defect in the task runner's OTel instrumentation.

clusters.rule: When `clear_on_success` clears task state through a worker backend, clear the asset-state accessors for the same task instance too
clusters.trigger: `context["task_state"].clear()` under `clear_on_success` with no corresponding walk of `context["asset_state"]`
clusters.rationale: Specific omission found in the clear_on_success implementation.

clusters.rule: Yield one outlet-event record per partition key rather than a single record carrying a `partition_keys` list
clusters.trigger: `yield {"dest_asset_key": ..., "partition_keys": list(...)}` in task_runner.py outlet-event iteration
clusters.rationale: Specific shape decision made for the partitioned outlet-event payload.

clusters.rule: A task-SDK RPC helper's docstring must describe its own parameters and return value, not those of a sibling method it was copied from
clusters.trigger: A new `@staticmethod` in task_runner.py whose docstring names parameters or return values absent from its own signature
clusters.rationale: Copied docstrings on near-identical RPC helpers are actively misleading precisely because the methods look alike.

clusters.rule: `pytest.param` ids must describe the scenario they actually configure, including whether a parameter has a default
clusters.trigger: `pytest.param(..., id="...")` whose id claims a property (e.g. `without_default`) contradicted by the lambda/function signature in the same case
clusters.rationale: Generic test-hygiene point rather than a repo-specific expectation.

clusters.rule: When fixing a `KNOWN_CONTEXT_KEYS` decorator bug, add a regression case using the actual context key names from the report (`start_date`, `end_date`), not placeholder names
clusters.trigger: `test_construction_succeeds` parametrize cases added for a KNOWN_CONTEXT_KEYS fix with no case using real context key names
clusters.rationale: Tied to one reported decorator defect.
